title: fix(xtask): pin the env that enters the cargo unit hash for gate steps
body:
## What changed

Cargo 1.100 puts each workspace unit in its own directory, `target/<profile>/build/<package>/<hash>/`. The hash covers the profile of the unit. Agents ran gates in the shared build worktree with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and with the default (incremental on). `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` sets `profile.incremental`. Thus each run with the other value gave all of about 600 `camcraft-app` units a new directory (about 190 MB each). Cargo does not remove the old directories.

- New `xtask/src/unit_env.rs`: each cargo call of a gate gets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`. The gate removes the caller's `CARGO_PROFILE_*` and `CARGO_BUILD_INCREMENTAL` variables.
- `direct::cargo` (the one place where a gate step starts cargo) and the three catalog cargo calls apply the pin.
- At the start, the gate prints the pin, each removed variable, and a note when `RUSTFLAGS` / `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` / `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS` is set.
- The summary prints the number of unit directories that the run added.
- The `gate` skill tells about the pin. `docs/decisions/3150-gate-unit-env.md` records the cause and the choice (incremental off, because sccache cannot cache incremental units and the disk is the defect).

## Readings (shared build worktree issue-917, 2026-11-21)

- The manifests, `Cargo.lock` and `.cargo/config.toml` were the same at the last six gated heads. But the `profile` fingerprint hash of one test unit had 3 values over 5 runs. Third-party units did not change.
- After the fix, `cargo xtask gate test flat_volume_has_finite_width_depth_and_segment_ends --crate cl` ran two times: caller `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` unset gave `unit directories: 5152, none added`; caller `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1` gave `unit directories: 5152, none added`.
- A plain `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=1 cargo test -p camcraft-cl --no-run` selected the other unit hash of `camcraft-kernel` (`573773ead6d4af3d`, an incremental variant). This confirms the cause.

## Pinning tests (`cargo test -p xtask`: 240 passed)

- `unit_env::tests::every_gate_cargo_call_gets_the_same_unit_env`
- `unit_env::tests::direct_cargo_steps_apply_the_unit_env`
- `unit_env::tests::batch_steps_share_the_flags_that_enter_the_unit_hash`
- `unit_env::tests::profile_variables_are_removed_and_others_kept`
- `unit_env::tests::notes_name_the_pin_and_each_removed_or_noted_variable`
- `unit_env::tests::units_count_nested_unit_directories_only`

## Not exercised

- A full quick or batch gate two times on the same tree. The probe used one `gate test` step.
- The old unit directories are not removed. The first gate run after the merge can add one more `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` variant where none is present. The decision file says why there is no prune.
- No heavy lane: the diff touches only `xtask/`, `.claude/skills/gate/` and `docs/decisions/`.

Process change: yes

Effort: high

Changelog: none

Fixes #3150

title: fix(test): run the wide-pocket parallel-lane test in the motion heavy lane
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/tests/adaptive_troch_parallel.rs`: `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes` has the ignore reason `heavy lane: ...`. The release tier and `cargo xtask gate heavy` run it with `--ignored` in the step `motion heavy: adaptive_troch_parallel`. The test keeps its two pockets (30x24 D6, 44x36 D10), all its shape asserts and its 90 s budget. The budget is now a guard on the release run.
- New light twin `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light` (`light lane: ...`). It checks the 30x24 D6 pocket only, in release.
- `docs/decisions/3141-parallel-lane-heavy.md` records the decision. It replaces the rule "apply the budget in every run" of decision #2990 for this test.

## Why

The debug test took 36, 64, 106, 140 and 145 s on unchanged motion code (#3116, #3141). The red runs were on a loaded post-merge runner. Wall time on a loaded runner is not a function of the code. AGENTS.md "Testing" moves a test above about 60 s in debug to the heavy lane.

Dropped: a larger debug budget (any number can fail under load); a smaller fixture (decision #2990 measured that a 38x33 D10 pocket fails the rest-area assert, and a smaller pocket weakens the 32.36 mm case).

## Readings (local, at 2c2b4bcbb, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, -j 18)

- Release, `--ignored --exact`: `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes` ok in 15.72 s (budget 90 s).
- Release, `--ignored --exact`: `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light` ok in 7.58 s.
- Debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test adaptive_troch_parallel`: 1 passed (`corner_cleanup_reduces_34x16_rest_to_at_most_hsm_rest`, 28.81 s), 2 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests

- `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes` (heavy lane)
- `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light` (light lane)

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate heavy` and `cargo xtask gate light` were not run as gate commands. The same tests ran with direct cargo calls in release.
- The batch gate on the post-merge runner.

The `#[test]` count of the binary goes from 2 to 3 (the light twin). No test was removed.

title: feat(2d): V-Carve operation - depth from the region width along the medial axis
body:
## What changed

- A new 2D operation, **V-Carve** (kind tag 44). A V-bit carves a closed region. The tip follows the medial axis. At each point the depth is where the cone touches the two walls. A maximum depth (`Top Z - Bottom Z`) limits the cut.
- Motion kernel: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/vcarve.rs`, `vcarve_axis.rs`, `vcarve_walk.rs`.
  - The tip positions come from the largest inscribed circle at each sampled boundary point. The centre of that circle is a point of the medial axis.
  - The cone keeps a wall allowance of 0.01 mm. The kernel checks each straight feed move against the outline before it writes the move. A move that fails becomes a retract and a new plunge.
  - A branch into a corner that turns less than 20 degrees is not ridden. A tessellated circle is one dip, not a star.
  - Deep carves step down. An optional flat-clearing pass uses offset rings of the same V-bit inside the wall pass.
  - The cone height also limits the depth. The path carries a note when it does.
- App: the `VCarve` kind row, the generator arm, the seed, heights, the mark depth law (`DepthLaw::Mark`), the project-file arm `VCarve` (appended, no version step), posting and the setup sheet.
- Sim: a new `Mode::Carve`. It has the stand-downs of `Mode::Engrave`, and the crossing law is off. The walk rides each axis branch from its two walls, so the two rides lie on one another by design.
- UI: a V-Carve parameter page and an original icon (`assets/ui/op-v-carve.png`, `.svg`).
- MCP: the generic `add_operation` tool takes the kind `V-Carve`. `list_operation_types` lists the kind and its fields. No new MCP tool is necessary.
- The V-bit is the existing `Taper` tool kind. The included angle is the tool's `tip_angle`.

## Sources (literature)

The algorithm is written from these published sources. The module heads name them.

- H. Blum, "A transformation for extracting new descriptors of shape", 1967 (the medial axis transform).
- H. I. Choi, S. W. Choi, H. P. Moon, "Mathematical theory of medial axis transform", Pacific J. Math., 1997.
- J. Ma, S. W. Bae, S. Choi, "3D medial axis point approximation using nearest neighbors and the normal field", The Visual Computer, 2012 (the tangent-circle shrink).
- M. Foskey, M. C. Lin, D. Manocha, "Efficient computation of a simplified medial axis", 2003 (the separation angle).
- M. Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991 (the floor rings).
- The cone law `depth = radius / tan(angle / 2)` is machine-tool handbook geometry.

The session had no web access, so no Perplexity search ran. camlib was a feature list only. No code or output of another program was read.

## Cause

There was no V-carve operation. The engrave ride follows a line at one depth only.

## Tests

- `crates/motion/tests/v_carve.rs` (11 tests):
  - `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region`: sweeps the cone along the path against the region outline.
  - `the_depth_follows_the_width_of_the_region`, `a_sharp_corner_rises_to_the_surface`, `a_stroke_is_cut_in_one_engagement`, `a_tessellated_circle_is_one_dip_not_a_star`, `the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut`, `flat_clearing_removes_the_floor_the_cone_cannot_reach`, `a_deep_carve_steps_down`, `a_cone_shorter_than_the_maximum_depth_limits_the_cut_and_says_so`.
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`: angle, diameter, maximum depth, stepdown, feed, clearance, retract, stepover, non-finite numbers, an empty region.
  - `degenerate_regions_give_a_clean_answer`: a fuzz set of 45 regions (zero width, a 1 micron sliver, a bow tie, a spike, far from the origin, 40 seeded random polygons), with and without flat clearing. Each gives a clean error or a path whose cone stays inside.
- `crates/app/tests/v_carve_op.rs` (7 tests):
  - `a_letter_is_carved_verified_simulated_and_posted`: the letter L generates, the program sim finds 0 gouge cells, and it posts.
  - `the_letter_matches_its_golden_cl_file`: golden `crates/app/tests/golden/v_carve_letter_l.cl`.
  - `the_operation_is_undone_and_done_again`, `a_tool_that_is_not_a_v_bit_is_refused_by_name`, `a_top_typed_under_the_surface_is_a_gouge_that_holds_the_post`, `a_saved_v_carve_opens_with_its_numbers`, `over_mcp_a_letter_is_carved_verified_and_undone`.
- Red before the change: yes. The pins do not compile on `main`, because the kind and `v_carve` do not exist there.

### Mutation checks

- `link_ok` in `vcarve_walk.rs` always returns true: `the_cone_never_leaves_the_region` is red. Restored: green.
- `VCarve` removed from the mark law (`mark_law.rs`): `a_letter_is_carved_verified_simulated_and_posted` and `over_mcp_a_letter_is_carved_verified_and_undone` are red. Restored: green.
- `Mode::Carve` with the crossing law on: the letter L is refused (checked in the earlier session, see the decision record).
- `OpType::VCarve` declared after `Engrave` (its old place): `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` (the registry row law) and 13 more app and ui steps are red. At the end of the enum: green. The held work had this defect; this PR fixes it.

### Kind-table pins that take the new kind

- `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input`: the registry count is 45.
- `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`: the lathe refuses 32 kinds (was 31).
- `operation::types::tilt_basis::tests::the_tilt_slot_covers_each_kind_whose_file_shape_has_a_tilt`: `tilt_slot` now covers `VCarve` (code change in `tilt_basis.rs`; main's #2599 added the slot after the held work).
- `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`: `VCarve` is refused on a reduced model, as `Engrave` is.
- `ribbon::the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`: `SinkerSideBurn` keeps 43, `VCarve` is the tail at 44.

## Goldens moved

- One new golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/v_carve_letter_l.cl`.
- After the merge of `main`, its `START` line changed from `0 0 25000` to `6000 -3000 25000`. The cause is main's #2901: the opening rapid now starts over its own entry point. No move line changed.
- No existing golden changed.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `5343a166a`: green, 782 steps, 0 failed (59 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The branch contains `upstream/main` at `8be100737`. A trial merge (`git merge-tree`) with `aa4c785db` is clean. Those 68 commits do not touch the kind table, the `OpType` enum or the project-file arms.

## Not exercised

- A heavy-lane run (`cargo xtask gate heavy`). The diff reaches the `motion` and `app` heavy lanes; they did not run in this session.
- A second, flat tool for floor clearing. One operation holds one tool. A 2D Pocket with a flat tool does this today.
- A refusal for "a tip flat larger than the narrowest feature". The `Tool` record has no tip-flat field for a taper tool. This needs a tool-model change first.
- An exact segment Voronoi diagram. The decision record gives the reason and the cost to change later.
- The UI page was not driven by hand.

## Overlaps

- #3058 (Waterjet Profile) also appends kind tag 44 and `ALL[44]` in `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`. These are appends to one table, not shared logic. The PR that merges second takes tag 45. The decision record has the reason for no stack.
- These open PRs touch the same files (`kinds.rs`, `generate.rs`, `types/params.rs`, `project/params.rs`, `sim/src/verify/types.rs`) in other functions: #3115, #3108, #3103, #3099, #3097, #3087, #3080, #3059. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1443-v-carve.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: New 2D operation V-Carve: a V-bit carves a closed region along its medial axis, with the depth from the region width, a maximum depth, step-downs and optional flat clearing.

Fixes #1443

title: fix(2d): rest pass keeps corner reliefs on the rest center boundary
body:
## What changed

- `rest_pocket_with_relief` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest2d.rs`) keeps a planned corner relief when its start is in the rest center area grown by 0.01 mm (`RELIEF_START_TOL`).
- Each relief that the rest pass does not keep now gives a toolpath note: `corner relief at (x, y) is not cut: the rest area does not reach that corner`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3146-rest-relief-boundary.md`.

## Cause

The old filter was `.filter(|r| plan.center.contains(r.start))`. Each relief start is a vertex of the pocket's own center area. Where the rest area touches a corner, that vertex is on the boundary of the rest center area. `Region::contains` on a boundary point gives `true` or `false` by rounding. On a sharp 30 x 30 mm pocket, the rest pass cut 1 of 4 dogbones and gave no note.

The start stays a legal tool position. It is always on the plain pocket's own center area, so the tolerance cannot move the tool past a wall.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/rest_corner_relief.rs`:

- `rest_pass_cuts_all_four_dogbones_of_a_sharp_square_pocket`: the 30 x 30 mm pocket, 6 mm tool, previous tool 16 mm, `CornerReliefKind::Dogbone`. Each of the 4 dogbone ends is cut at the floor, for Waterline, OffsetRings and Zigzag. No relief note.
  - Red before the fix: `Waterline: rest pass missed dogbone ends [(27.88, 27.88), (2.12, 27.88), (27.88, 2.12)]`.
- `rest_pass_notes_a_forced_relief_the_rest_area_does_not_reach`: an override forces a dogbone on a 176 deg corner. The previous tool leaves only a film there, so the rest area does not reach it. The pass does not cut it, and a note names it.

Mutation checks:

- Old `rest2d.rs` from `upstream/main`: both pins red.
- The fix with a bare `plan.center.contains` (no tolerance): the count pin red, at line 72.
- Fix restored: both pins green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (motion lib, `rest_corner_relief`, `rest_zigzag`, `rest2d`, app `rest_pocket`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The shared spur emitter (`inject_relief_spurs`) can still skip a kept relief without a note when no pass vertex links to it. That code is shared with the plain pocket and is not changed here.
- Heavy lanes were not run.

## Overlaps

- #2822 and #2890 change other parts of `rest2d.rs` (`rest_pocket` / `emit_rest`). They do not contain the relief filter. This PR touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket rest pass with corner reliefs now cuts the relief at every inside corner that the rest area touches, and notes a relief that it does not cut.

Fixes #3146

body:
## What changed

`crates/app/tests/ai_guide.rs` failed on a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf`. Git writes `site/content/guide/automate/ai.md` with CRLF line ends there. The test split the text on "```json\n", found no fence, and counted 0 calls:

```
panicked at crates\app\tests\ai_guide.rs:40:5:
the four tasks need complete tools/call examples
```

- The test now changes CRLF to LF after it reads the guide (`guide_text`).
- The fence check moves into `checked_calls`, and the live tool list into `live_tools`. The two existing tests use them. Their assertions do not change.
- The new test `a_crlf_checkout_of_the_guide_reads_the_same_examples` makes a CRLF copy of the guide. It checks that the CRLF copy gives the same `tools/call` examples as the LF text, and that the two texts are equal after the change.

The decision (a fix in the test, not a `.gitattributes` rule) is in `docs/decisions/3119-ai-guide-crlf.md`. A `.gitattributes` rule changes only new checkouts, so an existing Windows clone stays red.

## Readings

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test ai_guide` on Linux: 3 passed, 0 failed (head 583d05fda)

- `a_crlf_checkout_of_the_guide_reads_the_same_examples`
- `ai_guide_calls_match_live_tools_list`

title: fix(app): read a 3+2 plane and a cross drill through every table pose
body:
## What changed

The post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the move with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `traverseZ`, `xyFirst`, `onRapid`). On a machine whose table tilts the work, the X/Y traverse of a 3+2 plane or of a cross drill runs at the pose that the previous program left. The #2987 law reads these operations only at their own pose.

- `first_traverse_posed::posed_kind`: the posed law of #3084 now also reads each kind that carries a `Tilt` (the 3+2 planes) and the cross drill. Everything else in `turn_of` is unchanged: the sphere about the WCS origin for two work-turning rotaries, a full turn about the line for one, and the refusal by name of a rotary with no line.
- `table_top` and `table_stays`: when every tilting rotary turns the work, the law reads the machine table fixed where it stands. The table does not turn. When a head tilts, the #2987 table law reads the table, as before.
- The op stamp word of #3084 now also covers these operations. So their caches read Stale once.
- `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`: three operation stamps change. The stamp values come from the test's own path (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`). `first-4axis-part.nc` is byte-identical, and no operation is refused.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/3100-table-tilt-first-traverse.md`.

## Coordinator decisions (recorded in the decision file)

1. The table is read fixed where it stands, not swept. A swept travel box refuses every 3+2 program.
2. A test fixture change in `first_traverse_table.rs`. The test `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work` sets the WCS origin to zero for `Rig::Work`.
   - Before: it expected no verdict.
   - Now: it expects the verdict of the block corner on its sphere (29.584, from the stock, not the table) at 20 over the plane origin, and a pass at 30.
3. The example restamp is stamp-only, and every `.nc` is byte-identical. The `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` save also rewrites fields that drifted on main before this PR (A `feed` / `travel`, `chain_order`, the machine `post`). It also writes a local absolute model path. So the PR takes only its three stamp values.
4. The cross drill: the one shipped mill-turn (`assets/machines/millturn.mch`) states only a C along Z, with the head under it. So no shipped mill-turn changes, and there is no end-to-end pin for the cross drill.

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse_table_tilt`:
  - `a_3_2_plane_under_the_work_a_turning_table_can_leave_turned_up_is_refused_by_name` (A table, A 30, top 18.735)
  - `a_3_2_plane_over_every_pose_of_a_turning_table_passes` (A table; trunnion B 30)
- `first_traverse_table`: `a_work_turning_rotary_keeps_the_table_under_the_work` (changed, see above)
- lib: `operation::first_traverse_posed::tests::the_fixed_table_reads_its_top_in_the_paths_height_scale`

## Readings (debug, head a1a3e8391; the later commits change only docs)

`cargo test -p camcraft-app`, all green:
- `--lib`
- `first_traverse_table_tilt`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_posed`, `first_traverse_rotary`
- `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`
- `first_4axis_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `machine`, `microarc_test_part`, `tilt_basis_compat`, `tormach_fourth_axis`
- `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn`
- `drilling_cross`, `drilling_cross_rapids`, `drilling_cross_spindle`, `drilling_cross_part`, `drilling_cross_stock`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_holder`
- `lathe_cross_drill`, `coarse_cross_drill`, `cross_drill_neighbours`, `stock_source_cross_drill`, `stitch_cross`
- `example_catalog`

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` reaches the app heavy lanes (every target). Not run, covered by the cut gate.

## Not exercised

- The cross drill end to end. No shipped mill-turn states a tilting rotary that turns the work.
- `tormach.cps` turns A before the X/Y traverse. The law reads every pose there too (a superset, see the decision file).
- The full quick gate. Only the binaries listed above were run.

Changelog: The first traverse of a 3+2 plane and of a cross drill, on a machine whose table tilts the work, is now judged through every pose that the previous program can leave; a clearance under the work turned up is refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation).

Fixes #3100

title: fix(contour): a None lead-in stands the wall arc entry down
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: on an outside ring, the Arc entry does not run its vertical wall arc when the lead-in is `Lead::None`. The level descends by the grazing dive at the ring's start. A note names the stand-down once.
- `crates/app/tests/contour_none_lead.rs`: new pins. Each test edits the contour through `EditOperationParams` and generates it, as the page's Apply does.
- `docs/decisions/3132-contour-none-lead.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

The report does not name the entry type. On `Milling-test.step`, only the Arc entry reproduces the symptom. Plunge, Ramp and Helix with both leads None already start the cut on the ring.

With both leads None, the Arc entry's wall arc lands on the seam itself. Its start is about 8.7 mm back along the seam's tangent. From above, that arc is a straight move into the seam. It has the same shape as the seeded 8 mm linear lead. An Arc lead changes the shape, and a Linear lead keeps it, as the report says.

## Tests

Pins, all in `contour_none_lead`:
- `arc_entry_with_both_leads_none_starts_the_cut_on_the_ring`: Linear to None, Lead out None, zero extensions, zero overlap, Arc entry. The first XY cut is flat at the level and starts on the ring's closed seam. The post has no G18/G19.

title: fix(multiaxis): refuse a work-turning rotary line off the WCS origin
body:
Stacked on #3125 (merge #3125 first).

## What changed

- New function `posting::index_swing::off_origin`. It is true when a rotary states a `pivot` or an `offset` that is not zero, or not finite.
- The index-swing clause (`posting_index_swing::verdict`) has a new verdict `OffOrigin`. A work-turning rotary with a level line and an off-origin `pivot` or `offset` refuses the post by name. With two or more work-turning rotaries, any off-origin rotary refuses.
- The posed first-traverse law (`operation::first_traverse_posed::turn_of`) refuses generation by name in the same cases.
- One vertical work-turning rotary with a pivot is not refused. A turn about a vertical line keeps every height.
- A zero `pivot` or `offset` is judged as before.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3127-offset-rotary-line.md`.

## Cause

The two clauses read each work-turning rotary line through the WCS origin. A machine file can state a `pivot` or an `offset` that moves the line. The clauses then read the swept set about the wrong line. The reading can be too low, and the post is not blocked.

`pivot` is in machine coordinates. The project does not state where the WCS origin is in machine coordinates. So the program cannot place the moved line. A refusal is the safe answer.

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_posed.rs`:
  - `a_table_line_off_the_wcs_origin_refuses_by_name` (red before the fix: "no refusal: Ok []").
  - `a_zero_pivot_reads_the_table_line_through_the_wcs_origin` (clear case).
- `crates/app/tests/index_swing_offset_line.rs` (new file):
  - `a_pivot_off_the_wcs_origin_refuses_the_index_swing_by_name` (red before the fix).
  - `an_offset_off_the_wcs_origin_refuses_the_index_swing_by_name` (red before the fix).
  - `a_zero_pivot_and_offset_judge_the_index_swing_as_before` (clear case; the program posts).
- Mutation: with the two source files put back to the #3125 head, the three refusal pins fail and the two clear pins pass. With the fix, all five pass.
- `index_swing` (13) and `first_traverse_posed` (5) pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, local, debug): 9 steps, 0 failed. Steps: app lib, `first_traverse_posed`, `index_swing`, `index_swing_horizontal`, `index_swing_offset_line`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `setup_mount_trace`.

## Goldens moved

None. No shipped machine file states `pivot` or `offset`.

## Not exercised

- The two-rotary branch of `turn_of` with an off-origin rotary has no own pin. It uses the same `off_origin` test as the pinned single-rotary branch.
- A vertical rotary with a pivot (not refused) has no own pin.

## Overlaps

- #3125: this PR is stacked on it. It changes `turn_of` in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse_posed.rs` and adds tests to `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_posed.rs`.
- #2831 touches `crates/app/tests/index_swing.rs`. This PR puts its index-swing pins in a new file, so there is no overlap.

Changelog: A work-turning rotary whose machine file states a non-zero pivot or offset now refuses the index-swing check and the posed first-traverse check by name, instead of a reading about a line through the WCS origin.

Effort: high

title: fix(slot): cut the round ends of a slot wider than the tool
body:
## What changed

- A Slot wider than its tool now runs one wall lap at each level, after the rows.
- The lap follows the boundary of the tool centre stadium: two straight sides and two half circles.
- Each half circle is a chain of arcs (G02/G03). The chain is split at every row end on it and at its tip, so no arc is more than 90 degrees.
- The rows and the lap compute a row end with one function (`cap_point`). Each row join meets the lap at the same point to the bit.
- The lap starts where the last row ends and closes at that point.
- Under `climb` the lap is counterclockwise (the slot's air on the left, the same sense as the rows). Under conventional it is clockwise.
- A full-width slot (`h = 0`, one row on the centre line) does not change.
- The lap code is in the new module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_lap.rs`. `slots.rs` is 394 lines.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2906-slot-round-ends.md`.

## Cause

A row touches a round end only at its end point. The move between two rows is a straight line. The tool did not follow the arc between two row ends. On a 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool, 0.86 mm stayed on the wall of each round end.

## Why the arcs are split at the row ends

The first version used two quarter arcs for each cap. The quick gate refused it on 8 app suites. The verifier's crossing law (a) flattens an arc into chords inside its circle. A row join is a chord that ends exactly on the circle, so it crossed those flattened chords, and the post was held. With the split, the join and the lap share their vertices. The law reads a shared vertex as a touch, not a crossing. The crossing law does not change.

## Tests

- New pin: `crates/motion/tests/slot_round_ends.rs`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_climb`
  - `wide_slot_cuts_its_round_ends_conventional`
  - `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends`
  - Each point on the stadium wall must be within the tool radius of the tool centre path (limit 0.01 mm). No tool centre point may leave the cutter centre stadium. `crossed_pairs` (the verifier's crossing law) must be empty.
  - Red before the fix: `climb=true z=9: 0.855 mm left on the wall at (28.536, 18.536)`.
- New unit tests in `slot_lap.rs`: the lap closes on its start; each row end is a lap vertex; CCW from `b` runs the +n side first; CW from `b` turns round `b` first.
- Mutations:
  - `slots.rs` set back to `upstream/main`: the pin fails (0.855 mm, both directions). Restored: green.
  - The cap split without the row ends (tangent points and tip only): `wide_slot_with_rows_off_the_tips_cuts_its_round_ends` fails with 22 crossing pairs. Restored: green.
- Expected-change test updates:
  - `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs`: `slot_offsets_rows_across_a_wide_channel`, `conventional_slot_starts_at_the_far_end`, `slot_stock_to_leave_narrows_the_center_area` read the rows as the prefix of the level and pin the lap (arc count, direction, tips at x = -7 and 47, close at the last row end). `slot_helix_orbits_in_the_certified_channel` counts only descending arcs as the helix.
  - `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` (`an_entry_edit_marks_the_slot_stale_and_the_orbit_proves_itself`): an orbit is a descending arc. The planar arcs are the lap.
  - `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_2d_slots.rs`: the Slot now has 8 arc blocks (4 for each level).
  - `crates/app/tests/clearance_in_stock.rs` (`a_slot_traverse_at_a_clearance_plane_inside_the_stock_is_convicted_and_holds_the_post`): see "Side effect" below.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `35020f6cc`: 732 steps, 0 failed.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Side effect (please check in review)

In `clearance_in_stock`, the slot's lateral traverse between its levels was convicted only because the uncut crescents of the round ends stood in its path. The traverse stays inside the slot's own channel. With the ends cut, the verifier acquits it. The plane is still convicted by the first traverse (`FirstTraverseLow`, #2901) and by the rapid from the plane down into the stock (`RapidInStock { at: 1 }`). The post is still held with "travels through stock". The test now asserts these facts.

## Goldens moved

All in `slot_wide_channel_rows` and the catalog case `2d/slots`.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/slot_wide_channel_rows.cl`: 12 lap moves added (2 lines, 10 arcs; each cap split at the rows -7, -3, 1, 5, 7 and the tip). The header changes from `v1` to `v2` because the CL now has arcs.
- The NC golden of each dialect (`nc/`, `carvera`, `doosan-dnm`, `grbl`, `grblhal`, `haas`, `heidenhain`, `linuxcnc`, `mach4`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `tinyg`, `tormach`, `tormach/explain_`): the same 12 moves added. In `heidenhain` and `sinumerik` the block numbers after the lap move up. No other line changes.
- Catalog case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` (`cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots`):
  - `slots.nc`: 6 lap moves added at each of the two levels (rows at -2, 0, 2: each cap is two quarter arcs).
  - `slots.camproj`: the cached Slot moves gain the lap. The stamps change.
  - The first rapid's `from` of the two operations changes from `(0, 0)` to the start point. This change is also in the Trochoidal slot, which this PR does not change. It is drift of the catalog file on main, written by the catalog tool. I kept the tool's output and did not edit it by hand.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) were not run. The change is in `motion` and reaches the `app` heavy lanes. Run them before this PR is flagged ready.
- The app's `verify` was not run by hand on the catalog case. The suites that post it (`example_catalog`, `solid_law_goldens`) are green.
- Ramp and Helix entries with the lap ran only through the existing slot tests.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot*.rs` or the catalog case `2d/slots`. The branch merges cleanly with the current `main` (`8be100737`).

Changelog: A Slot wider than its tool now cuts its two round ends to size with a wall lap at each level; before, up to 0.86 mm stayed on the end walls.

Effort: high

Fixes #2906

title: fix(2d): close Zigzag pockets with wall and island rings
body:
## What changed
- A 2D pocket that cuts as Zigzag now closes with one ring on each boundary loop of the cutter-center area. Auto resolves to Zigzag, so Auto gets the rings too. The rings cut the outer wall and each island wall.
- The pocket uses the existing rest-pocket plan (`pocket_zigzag::rest_passes`). The rows stand 0.01 mm inside the area, and the rings follow the area boundary.
- The row points now stand on the 1 um lattice.
- A Zigzag pocket with blended turns now holds its blends to the crossing law (`hold_crossings`), as the rest pocket does. A fillet that would cross a ring stays a sharp turn.

## Cause
- `pocket_over_with_relief` used the rows-only plan for an ordinary Zigzag pocket. Only rest pockets got the closing rings.
- The rows touch a side wall or an island only at their ends. A cusp stays between each two ends over the full depth.
- With a 6 mm tool and a 2 mm stepover, the cusp is 0.17 mm on a straight wall and 0.75 mm on an R4 corner. Verify has no law for that material, so the program passed as clean.
- Two more problems came from the change itself:
  - The 0.01 mm gap puts the row ends off the lattice. A helix entry snaps its turns to the lattice. Two levels' helices at one off-lattice start then differed by 3.5e-7 mm, and the post check read them as crossings (`setup_align`). Lattice row points remove this.
  - Blended row turns crossed the new rings (`app corner_blend`). The crossing hold removes this.

## Tests
New pins: `crates/motion/tests/pocket_wall_finish.rs`. The pocket is 60 x 40, with R4 corners and a 16 mm island. The tool is 6 mm, with a 2 mm stepover.
- `auto_pocket_with_island_finishes_walls_and_island`
- `zigzag_pocket_with_island_finishes_walls_conventional`
- `zigzag_pocket_without_island_finishes_walls`
- `blended_zigzag_pocket_finishes_walls_without_crossings`
- `blended_zigzag_turns_do_not_cross_the_closing_rings`

The first four tests measure the scallop on each wall at the floor. The limit is 0.02 mm. They also check `verify::crossed_pairs`.

Red before the fix: the first four tests fail on unchanged code (outer wall scallop 0.755 mm; 0.919 mm when blended).

Mutation checks:
1. Old `pocket.rs` guard: the 4 wall pins go red. Restored: green.
2. No lattice snap in `rest_passes`: `setup_align::the_pocket_and_face_kinds_cut_the_flipped_part_and_post` goes red ("post blocked - 4 warning(s): ... cross in XY at shared depth"). Restored: green.
3. No crossing hold for Zigzag: `blended_zigzag_turns_do_not_cross_the_closing_rings` goes red (12 crossing pairs, the same pairs as `app corner_blend`). Restored: green.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 6e3e4397b: 678 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Expected-change test: `setup_align` asserted the island clearance with a square box (`max(|x|, |y|) < 21.9`). A closing ring at a rounded corner is legal but failed that check. The assertion now measures the Euclidean distance to the 40 x 40 block (at least 1.9 mm for the 4 mm tool).

## Goldens moved
There are 18 changed files, all for one pocket case and the two first-part sample programs:
- `crates/app/tests/golden/pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island.cl` and `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island_blended.cl`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/*/pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island.nc`: 12 dialects, plus the Tormach `explain_` file.
- `examples/first-part.nc` and `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc`. The 2D Pocket1 of that part is Auto.

In each NC file, only motion blocks change: the rows move 0.01 mm inward, and the ring blocks are new. Block numbers after them move by the same count. No header, tool, spindle or coolant line changes. The `.camproj` files do not change.

## Not exercised
- The QA project from the report (`q01-first-post.camproj` on skull). The motion pin rebuilds the same shape.
- `pocket_avoid` (Do not touch) and the 3D pocket levels still cut Zigzag rows with no ring. #3129 tracks them.
- A pre-existing defect: in a narrow band, two helix entries of different passes can overlap. The post check blocks it. That is before and after this change. #3129 notes it.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) were not run.

## Overlaps

title: fix(kernel): measure a fan at a spline pole by its true sag
body:
## What changed

- New module `crates/kernel/src/mesh_pole.rs`. It finds a triangle corner that sits on a pole of a spline face. At a pole, the derivative along one parameter is zero.
- The module moves the free parameter of that corner to the mean of the other two corners. It takes those two corners on one side of the period.
- The module keeps the move only when the surface point stays within 1e-9 mm.
- `mesh_deviation::face` calls the module for spline faces before it samples a triangle. Analytic faces do not change.
- New fixture `testdata/models/sphere_quarter_pole.step`. This is our own file: a quarter sphere, R 25, with a rational B-spline dome that turns 180 degrees and ends in a pole at the apex.

## Cause

The issue reports an open mesh on v0.24.0. On upstream/main 8be100737 (after #917), the import itself refuses the q02 part:

```
solid #3738 'Mould' could not be tessellated: machining mesh: face Some(10) stands 5.089e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm
```

Face 10 is the ellipsoid boss (`#3666`, a rational B-spline with a pole at its top). The mesh is good. Its sag against the ellipsoid is about 0.004 mm. The planner gives the apex node u = 0 (and u = 1), and the ring under it has u near 0.5. The measure interpolated u across half the period in each fan triangle. It then projected from a hint on the far side of the surface. The bound of those triangles became 0.29 mm. The bound did not change at a finer chord. This showed that the measure was wrong and the mesh was not.

## Readings (q02 STEP from the QA host, local only)

- Before: the import refuses with the message above.
- After: 48780 facets, 0 open edges.
- After: the volume is 97163.50 mm^3. SolidCraft gives 97165.69 mm^3.
- After: the slice at z = 19.6875 (the reported height) gives 1382.27 mm^2. Slices at z = 18.5, 20, 25 and 29 also close.

## Tests

Pins:
- `camcraft-kernel` `mesh_deviation_pole::a_fan_at_a_spline_pole_measures_by_its_true_sag`. Red before the fix: "a good fan at a pole is judged 0.1065280187198439 mm off".
- `camcraft-kernel` `mesh_deviation_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_meshes_inside_the_tolerance`. Red before the fix: "face Some(2) stands 2.775e-1 mm off its surface, tolerance 5e-3 mm" (the same refusal as q02).
- `camcraft-app` `import_step_spline_pole::a_solid_with_a_spline_pole_imports_closed_and_slices`. Red before the fix with the same refusal. Green after: volume and five slices.
- `camcraft-kernel` lib `mesh_pole::tests` (3 unit tests).

Mutation: I put back `mesh_deviation.rs` from upstream/main. The three pins above went red. I restored the fix. The pins went green.

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 90 steps. 89 were green on the first run. The one red step was `kernel suites: step_agreement` (`step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name`: "a fixture has no row"). That test requires a row for each STEP fixture. I added the row for `sphere_quarter_pole.step` (`Truck::NotRecorded`, the form for fixtures after #2790) and its `per_file!` test. The bench reads the file as "watertight, within tolerance", V = 16358.3 mm^3 (exact pi R^3 / 3 = 16362.5). After that, `step_agreement` is green: 27 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The q02 STEP is not in the tree. It is on the QA host. This headless session could not copy it into the repository (the copy needs an approval prompt). The quarter-sphere fixture gives the same refusal on upstream/main and pins the cause. If the maintainer wants the recorded file as a fixture, commit it to `testdata/models/`.
- I did not run a Waterline, 3D Pocket, Scallop or Pencil generate on q02. The slices that those operations use close at the reported height.
- Heavy lanes were not run.
- The 1e-9 mm point check in `settle` has no separate pin. No surface that we can build has a zero derivative at a point that is not a pole.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/kernel/`.

Changelog: A closed STEP solid with a spline face that ends in a pole (for example an ellipsoid or a dome from SolidCraft) now imports. Before, the import refused it with "stands ... mm off its surface".

title: fix(2d): read a drafted side as a wall, not as a modelled chamfer
body:
## What changed

- A no-pick 2D chamfer now reads a drafted side as a wall. It does not read it as a modelled chamfer.
- The chamfer takes a third section of the material, half way between the top plane and the corner plane.
- A piece of a top loop is a drafted wall when two conditions are true:
  - It stands off the wall by no more than `depth * tan(15 deg)`.
  - The half-depth section stands half that distance off the wall (within a quarter). The face is one straight face.
- A loop with drafted pieces and no bevelled piece rides its wall at the corner depth. It counts with the sharp loops (#2596). Thus a plate with no modelled chamfer breaks every edge, the drafted side and the pocket included.
- `partly_bevelled` becomes `read`, which returns a `Reading`. The #2887 refusal text does not change.
- `ride_loops` takes two new arguments: `mid` (the half-depth section) and `depth`. The one caller, `material_source.rs`, makes the half-depth section.

## Cause

PR #2894 refuses a loop that is bevelled on only part of its length. It reads each piece more than 0.05 mm off the wall as "bevelled". A drafted side also stands off the wall. With a 1 mm chamfer and a 90 degree cone, a draft of more than about 3 degrees is more than 0.05 mm off. The plate was refused with a "modelled chamfer" message.

Two sections cannot tell a draft from a small modelled chamfer. A third section can: a draft is straight, so the half-depth section is at half the offset. A modelled chamfer that ends above half depth puts that section on the vertical wall.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride_tests.rs`:

- `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall`: #2887's plate with its X0 side drafted 3.5, 5 and 10 degrees. Red on unchanged code: `the edge loop near X0.087 Y20.000 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length`.
- `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft`: a 0.2 mm modelled bevel on one side is still refused.
- `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer`: a 45 degree bevel deeper than the ride is still refused.
- The #2887 tests (`a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_by_name`, `..._with_an_extra_vertex_too`) still pass. The old test calls go through a small `ride` helper.

Mutation checks (each guard taken out, then put back):

- Drafted reading off: `a_plate_with_one_drafted_side_rides_its_wall` red.
- Half-depth check off: `a_small_bevel_on_one_side_is_no_draft` red.
- Slope limit off: `a_straight_face_steeper_than_a_draft_is_a_chamfer` red.
- Drafted match arm after the vertex-gap arm: the 3.5 degree case of the drafted pin red (it rode the top loop, inside the part).

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 139 steps, 0 failed (includes `chamfer_partly_bevelled` and `chamfer_modelled_edge`). Run with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`: the compile cache did not answer on this machine.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No app-level test with a real drafted STEP or STL model. The pins use hand-built sections.
- A drafted side under a tilted frame. The check measures along the frame's lean, but no test covers it.
- Heavy lanes were not run.

## Overlaps

PRs #3058, #2836 and #2714 touch `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs`. They change other match arms, not the `Chamfer2D` arm. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2929-chamfer-drafted-side.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer with no picked edges no longer refuses a part with a drafted side as a partly bevelled edge loop; the drafted side is chamfered along its wall.

Fixes #2929

title: fix(sim): read the first traverse through every pose of the work-turning rotaries
body:
## What changed

The post sends Z, then X/Y, then the move with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `traverseZ`, `xyFirst`, `onRapid`). During the X/Y traverse, each rotary that turns the work stands where the previous program left it. The #2965 laws read one fitted axis or the part frame, so two cases were not judged (#3084).

- New law `sim::verify::first_traverse_low_posed` (`crates/sim/src/verify/first_traverse_posed.rs`). It reads the start stock, the part and the tagged steel through every pose:
  - two or more work-turning rotaries: on the sphere about the WCS origin;
  - one work-turning rotary that tilts: a full turn about its line through the WCS origin.
- New seam `operation::first_traverse_posed` (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse_posed.rs`). It reads:
  - a rotary kind on a machine where two or more rotaries turn the work;
  - a multi-axis kind on a machine where a tilting rotary turns the work.
- A lone work-turning rotary with no usable axis line refuses generation by name.
- The verdict is the blocking `FirstTraverseLow`. It replaces each first-traverse verdict at a lower top.
- The op stamp of a newly judged operation takes the word `first-traverse-posed-3084`. No shipped project moves.
- `first_traverse::judge` and the swept law do not change. `generate.rs` calls the new seam after each `judge` call.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3084-posed-first-traverse.md` (premises, limits, dropped options).

## Readings

- Two rotaries, rotary kind, laid square bar: the stock corner is 18.815 from the WCS origin. Clearance 12 is held (the fitted-axis law read 9.899). Clearance 20 passes.
- Table A, 5-Axis Contour over the dome: the stock edge turns up to 23.324 about A. Clearance 20 is held (the part frame read 12). Clearance 25 passes.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_posed.rs`:
  - `two_work_turning_rotaries_read_the_rotary_kinds_stock_on_its_sphere`
  - `a_tilting_table_reads_a_5_axis_kinds_stock_swept_about_its_line`
  - `a_work_turning_rotary_with_no_line_refuses_by_name`
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::first_traverse_posed::tests` (4 tests).

## Gate (head 4664df470, local, debug)

- `camcraft-sim` lib `first_traverse`: 12 passed.
- `camcraft-app` tests: `first_traverse_posed` 3, `first_traverse_rotary` 3, `first_traverse_table` 9, `rotary_contour_x` 2, `microarc_test_part` 4, `index_swing` 13, `setup_align_multiaxis` 10, `continuous_4axis_part` 10, `first_4axis_part` 4, `example_catalog` 33 (2 ignored). All passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.

## Not exercised

- A program that starts low near the work (premise of PR #2997).
- A 3+2 operation and a cross drill on a work-tilting machine: follow-up #3100. Refs #3100.
- The two held tests check the post refusal with `is_err` only. They do not check its text, because the index-swing clause can refuse first.

Changelog: The first-traverse check now reads the work through every pose of the machine's work-turning rotaries: a rotary kind on a machine with two such rotaries, and a multi-axis kind on a machine whose table tilts. A traverse under the turned-up work holds the post by name.

title: fix(app): judge a rotary kind's first rapid on the spindle C from the turret's index position
body:
## What changed

- A Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel or Rotary Offset whose path states the spindle C now has a first-traverse law on a mill-turn and on a lathe. Before this, no law judged that first rapid.
- The post order is the lathe order. A C-stamped path carries `PARAM LiveTool`, and the engine refuses each post that does not declare `liveTooling` (`crates/post/src/post/engine.rs:243`). Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it. Its `liveMove` writes `G00 C` with the turret at its index position, then `G00 X Z` to the first record. The mill post's Z-then-X/Y order is never posted for these paths.
- New seam `crates/app/src/operation/rotary_traverse.rs`. It calls #3077's `verify::live_first_traverse` in the two rotary arms of `generate.rs`, after the C stamp.
  - The stock, the parts and the turning steel (a chuck) are read in the part frame, at the angle of C.
  - The fixed steel (a tailstock, a steady, the table) is read in the machine frame, on the +X station. This is the `verify::c_steel` convention (#486).
  - The end and the start of the first move are judged. A hit is a refusal by name (`GenError::Invalid`).
- `rotary_gate::c_center` is the one source of the spindle line, for the stamp and for the law.
- A rotary kind on a mill-turn whose path states no C (a machine file with no axis lines) posts through the mill post. It now takes the mill laws (`mill_post_rotary` added to `mill_order`).
- Op-stamp word `live-traverse-rotary-3096` for the rotary kinds on a lathe or a mill-turn setup. Those caches read Stale one time. No mill's stamp moves.
- Premise (maintainer): the turret starts at its index position, the top of the travel. A program that starts low is not covered. The decision records this.

## Fixture decisions (coordinator; the fixtures are tests only)

- The shared C-axis bar fixture (box stock 14 x 14 x 34, top Z34; clearance 25; BN-0600) opened with a first record at r 2.000, Z28.000, inside the box stock. The posted `G00 X Z` went into uncut stock, and the new law refuses it. That is a true hazard.
- `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_fixture`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `lathe_workholding_live` and `rotary_letter` now use clearance 40, as `c_axis_unwind` already did. Each test keeps what it pins.
- `c_axis_unwind::a_rewind_through_stock_is_convicted_by_the_verifier` cannot keep its geometry on a mill-turn: the orbit and the first record are on the same clearance plane. It now asserts the mill-turn's refusal by name. Then it reads the verifier's `RapidInStock` orbit conviction on the same bench declared a mill, where #2965's swept law reports `FirstTraverseLow`.
- Dropped: move the stock (more readings change); expect only the refusal (loses the verifier coverage); drop the override (changes the intent).
- No shipped example, catalog project or golden holds a rotary kind on a lathe or a mill-turn. No shipped file changes.

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn::a_steady_on_the_station_line_refuses_the_rotary_contour_by_name`
- `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn::the_same_steady_opposite_the_station_stays_clear`
- `operation::rotary_traverse::tests::the_stated_c_picks_the_lathe_order_and_no_c_the_mill_order` (lib)
- `c_axis_unwind::a_rewind_through_stock_is_convicted_by_the_verifier` (both laws)

## Readings (debug, on the final head unless noted)

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- On the final head: `c_axis_unwind` 7/7.
- On the head before the last test change:
  - `c_axis_live` 5/5, `c_axis_fixture` 2/2, `lathe_work_spindle` 5/5, `lathe_workholding_live` 3/3, `rotary_letter` 3/3.
  - lib `rotary_traverse` / `first_traverse` / `rotary_gate` 12/12.
- On the first head (before the fixture changes):
  - `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn` 2/2, `c_axis_live_world` 3/3.
  - `drilling_cross` 9/9, `lathe_cross_drill` 9/9.
  - `first_traverse_mill_turn` 3/3, `first_traverse_rotary` 3/3.
  - `lathe_workholding_kinds` 10/10, `setup_align_mill_turn` 2/2, `setup_align_multiaxis` 10/10.
- All changed blobs have 0 CR bytes.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.
- The full `camcraft-app` suite was not run. Only the binaries above ran.
- The known limits of #3077 stay: the turret body is not modelled, the tool cross-section is read square, and the stated X/Z travel is not used.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3096-mill-turn-rotary-first-traverse.md`

Changelog: A Rotary Contour, Parallel or Offset on the spindle C of a mill-turn or a lathe now refuses by name a first rapid from the turret's index position that passes the stock, a part or the steel.

title: fix(2d): turn a contour seam lead only when it crosses its own ring
body:
## What changed
- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/lead_seam.rs` with `seam_tangents`.
- `lead_fit.rs` calls `seam_tangents` from `both_fit` and `plan_leads`.
- At the seam of a closed ring, the function builds the full lead along the walk's end tangent.
- It checks that lead against the ring's own feed moves. It uses the verifier's crossing law (`arc_cross::moves_cross_prior`).
- Only a lead that crosses gets a new tangent: the old tangent mirrored across the other end's tangent.
- The mirrored lead is used only if it does not cross.
- A lead that does not cross keeps its tangent. Open walks keep their tangents.
- New test file `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`.
- Decision record `docs/decisions/3019-contour-lead-cross-only.md`.

## Cause
- On the issue's R6 plate, the seam falls on a fitted corner arc.
- The 8 mm linear lead-out along that arc's end tangent crossed the ring's long bottom edge next to the seam. The lead-in did the same on a conventional cut.
- Verify found one crossing on each level. Tabs are not the cause: the same crossing occurs with no tabs.
- The first fix (#3053) mirrored the tangent on each closed ring that bent at the seam. That also changed plain rectangles with no crossing (#3111). #3114 reverted it.
- This fix changes a lead only when that lead crosses its own ring.

## Tests
Pins (120 x 80 plate, four R6 corners, D10 tool, stepdown 3, 12 deep, linear lead 8):
- `an_outside_tabbed_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing` (climb, 4 tabs).
- `an_outside_contour_with_a_linear_lead_has_no_crossing_with_or_without_tabs` (climb with 0 tabs; conventional with 0 and 4 tabs).
- Each case asserts no `crossed_pairs`, no `Crossing` or `Gouge` from `verify`, and a full 8 mm lead-in and lead-out.
- The regression pin of #3111 is `vertical_arc_entry` (motion and post). It is green on this head.

Red before the fix: yes, both pins. Failure text: `4 tabs, climb: feed crossings [[5, 14], [21, 30], [37, 46], [53, 62]]`.

Mutations:
- M1, old `lead_fit.rs` from upstream/main: both pins red.
- M2, lead-out mirror removed: both pins red (`[[5, 14], ...]`).
- M3, lead-in mirror removed: the conventional case red (`[[3, 12], [19, 28], [35, 44], [51, 60]]`).
- M4, crossing check replaced by the #3053 bend law: motion `vertical_arc_entry` red (`an_oblique_first_cut_stays_chords_and_says_so_once`, `an_x_aligned_first_cut_enters_on_one_g18_arc_per_level`). This shows that the crossing check keeps other rings unchanged.
- Fix restored: all green.

Gate (macOS arm64):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 132 planned steps (motion lib, all motion and app suites that the gate map names for `motion::machining2d`). 129 steps passed in the gate run. The run was stopped by a 20 min session limit during step 131. I ran the last three steps (`app` `wall_arc_entry`, `wcs_start`, `wear_comp`) by hand: green. An earlier run of 56 steps was green but marked VOID because I wrote a file during it.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test vertical_arc_entry`: 3/3 green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes.

## Not exercised
- The QA project file of the issue (`q01-blocked.camproj`) was not opened. The pin rebuilds the same plate and operation in `camcraft-motion`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` was not run. A run is necessary before the PR is flagged ready.
- Inside contours (bores) with a crossing seam lead. The check applies to them too. No pin covers them.
- Arc and tangential leads. The check applies to each lead shape. Only the linear lead is pinned.

## Overlaps
None. No open PR changes `lead_fit.rs`. This is a redo of #3053, which #3114 reverted.

Changelog: A 2D Contour with a linear lead on a part with round corners no longer gets a lead-in or lead-out that crosses the cut at the seam, so verify does not hold the post.

Effort: high

Fixes #3019

title: fix(post): Heidenhain G205 writes the retraction feed Q208 as a number
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`: the G205 UNIVERSAL PECKING definition writes `Q208=+99999.999`. It wrote `Q208=FMAX` before. The value is the constant `RETRACT_FEED_MAX`.
- `crates/post/tests/heidenhain_cycles.rs`: the Q parser fails on any Q value that is not a signed number. This covers each cycle that the file tests (G200, G205, G206, G207). The G205 inventory now includes `(208, "+99999.999")`, and the test asserts that the program has no `FMAX`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/heidenhain/drill_peck.nc`: the one word changes.
- `docs/decisions/3102-heidenhain-q208-numeric.md`: the decision record.

## Readings

- #3102: the iTNC 530 programming station (606425 004 SP20) prefixes the `N100 G205` block with `ERROR =` when it reads `Q208=FMAX`. With `Q208=+60`, the station reads the complete block.
- HEIDENHAIN "iTNC 530 Cycle Programming", ID 670388-25 (NC software 60642x-04), cycle 205: Q208 is the feed rate for retraction, input range 0 to 99999.999. The manual lists FMAX, FAUTO and PREDEF as dialogue inputs. Its own NC example writes `Q208=99999`.
- 99999.999 is the top of the range. It asks for the fastest retract that the control permits. `Q208=0` was not chosen: it retracts at the plunge feed Q206, which changes the requested behaviour.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `heidenhain_cycles` `peck_and_deep_have_distinct_documented_native_cycles_and_q_inventory` (and each other test of the file, through the numeric Q check).

This PR does not cause it: on a CRLF checkout the test finds no "```json" fence in `site/content/guide/automate/ai.md`. It is filed as #3119.

The known-fail steps of #1950 and #2849 are red as expected.

title: fix(xtask): seed a new worktree's target/ so solidcore is not compiled again
body:
## What changed

- New module `xtask/src/seed.rs`. Before its first step, `cargo xtask gate` copies the dependency units of another checkout into a new worktree. The units are `target/debug/{build,deps,.fingerprint}`. The source is the checkout of this repository with the most units.
- The copy skips each package without a `source` in `cargo metadata`. These are the workspace members and the path dependencies.
- The copy replaces a unit that is in the worktree already. `cargo xtask` builds its own dependencies before the gate starts, and their newer times made each copied unit above them dirty.
- The copy keeps the file times. It copies outputs before fingerprints. It renames each unit into place.
- The copy takes cargo's locks (`.cargo-lock`, `.cargo-build-lock`) without a wait. It passes over a checkout where a build runs.
- A seeded worktree gets `target/debug/.camcraft-seeded` and is not seeded again. `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1` turns the seed off. A dry run does not seed.
- `xtask/src/main.rs`: two module lines and one call in `gate`.
- `docs/decisions/2575-seed-worktree-target.md`: the decision, the reasons and the dropped options.

## Cause

sccache 0.19 hashes three things that name the worktree in a Rust compile:
- the `OUT_DIR` value of each env dependency;
- the cwd;
- the raw arguments.

Thus each crate with a build script misses in a new worktree, and each crate above it misses too (`solidcore`, `flecs`). `SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` applies only to C and C++ (`src/compiler/rust.rs`, hash key steps 3, 8 and 9). Cargo's own fingerprints do not name the worktree, so a copied unit reads as Fresh.

## Readings (#914 comparison)

18-core Mac, APFS, sccache 0.19 warm, `cargo xtask gate test after_defaults_to_none_and_writes_no_stream_word --crate app` in a new worktree:

| | to the first app test | units compiled | `solidcore` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1` | 107 s (step 99 s) | 231 | compiled |
| seeded | 42 s (seed 9 s, step 24 s) | 14 | Fresh |

With the seed, these compile: our 9 crates, plus `ring` and the 5 rustls crates above it. `ring` is dirty because "the env variable CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR changed" against the source checkout. I did not find why. The source checkout (`fix-2920`) was built by another session. Linux was not measured.

## Tests

Pins in `xtask/src/seed_tests.rs`:
- `a_seeded_checkout_finds_a_build_script_dependency_fresh`: two git dependencies, one with a build script that writes into `OUT_DIR`. Checkout `b` already has a newer unit of the lower dependency. After the seed, `cargo build -v` in `b` shows `Fresh seeddep`, and the local package compiles.
- `a_checkout_where_a_build_runs_is_passed_over`
- `local_packages_are_the_ones_without_a_source`
- `a_unit_entry_of_a_local_package_is_never_copied`

Red before the fix (no-op seed): `fresh-worktree build-script dependency must not compile again: Compiling seeddep v0.1.0 ...`.

Mutations:
- Copy local packages too: red (`the local package compiles in b`). The stale unit read as Fresh.
- Skip units that exist (no replace): red (`Dirty seeddep ...: the dependency seedbase was rebuilt`).
- Do not keep the file times: green on APFS. `clonefile` keeps the times on macOS. The guard is for Linux and Windows copies, and it is not pinned on this machine.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (xtask unit tests). `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- Linux and Windows. `fs::copy` uses `copy_file_range` on Linux (a reflink on btrfs and XFS, a full copy on ext4). On Windows it uses `CopyFileExW`.
- Disk use on a file system without clones: the copy takes the size of the source's dependency units.
- The gate skill does not describe the seed yet. The edit of `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md` needed an approval that this headless run did not have.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `xtask/src/main.rs` or the new files.

Process change: yes

Changelog: The gate seeds a new worktree's `target/` from another checkout, so the dependencies (solidcore included) are not compiled again (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1` turns it off).

Fixes #2575

title: fix(motion): Circular climbs to clearance between its rings
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: before each ring after the first, the tool climbs straight up to clearance at the end of the last ring. Then the ring's ladder enters from clearance, as the first ring does. This applies to the flat mode and to the vault.
- The unit tests of `circular.rs` move to `circular_tests.rs` with no change. This keeps `circular.rs` at 361 lines (it was 411 before this PR).
- Two goldens gain the one new climb move.
- New pins in `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`.

## Cause

Each ring runs its own level ladder (ring-major order). The first descent of a ladder expects the tool at clearance. After the first ring, the tool stood on that ring's floor. The descent then made one diagonal rapid from the floor up to clearance over the next ring's start. That rapid crossed the core that the next ring had still to cut. Verification convicted it and held the post. A 5 mm hole with a Ø6 tool has only one ring, so the catalog case did not show the fault. The vault had the same diagonal rapid.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_link_between_circular_rings_clears_the_stock` (motion): plunge, helix and ramp entry; planar and default links; flat and vault. No lateral rapid under the stock top. The verifier convicts no rapid.
- `the_issue_case_climbs_to_clearance_between_its_rings` (motion): the issue's four rings (R 7, 5, 3, 1). Each traverse onto R 5, 3 and 1 is at clearance.
- `a_spliced_diagonal_link_between_rings_is_still_convicted` (motion): the real path is clean. A diagonal link of the old shape, spliced in, gets `RapidInStock`. This is the "post stays blocked for a deliberately unsafe link" part of Done.
- `a_multi_ring_circular_links_its_rings_over_the_stock_and_posts` (app): the issue's job through generate, verify and post. No warning, and the program posts, for the plunge and the ramp entry.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the app pin reports `RapidInStock { at: 69 }` and `RapidInStock { at: 119 }`, the moves that the issue names. The motion pin reports rapids under the stock top at moves 69, 119 and 169.

Mutation: the fix with the climb disabled makes all three motion pins red (the flat case and the vault case at moves 20 and 40). The fix restored makes them green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 729 of 730 steps pass. The changed golden widened the run to the app suites. The one red step is `default_machine_missing` (`a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`). It fails on upstream/main 211105042 without this change too. I added that fact to #3111.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- After the gate, one clippy fix in the motion pin (`..*m` in place of `..m.clone()`). The pin was run again: green.

## Goldens moved

Two goldens. Each gains one line, `Rapid <x> <y> <clearance>`, at the first ring's end, with the same X and Y. The header move count goes up by one. No other line changes.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ring_arcs.cl`: 401 to 402 moves.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ramp_stay_down.cl`: 133 to 134 moves.

## Not exercised

- The helix entry with several rings is still refused. Each ring's helix touches the last ring's helix at the start of the ring, in the same depth band. The crossing law convicts that touch. The program is refused, not unsafe. Follow-up: #3109.
- I tried the pocket's z-major order for the flat mode on this branch. It removed the helix crossings, but the inner rings then started with an axial plunge that was not named, also under a ramp entry. Four ramp-entry tests went red. I dropped it (see the decision record).
- Heavy lanes and pixel snapshots were not run.
- The local builds used no sccache: the shared sccache server did not complete compile jobs during this run.

## Overlaps

- #2842 changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs` too, in the level ladder calls (`cut_levels_under`, `levels_from`). This PR changes the lines before `run_level_walks` and moves the test module. Touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Circular with several rings no longer links its rings with a rapid through the stock; each ring after the first climbs to clearance first, so verification passes and the program posts.

Effort: high

Fixes #2898

title: fix(circular): keep the helix entries of the rings apart
body:
## What changed

- A flat Circular with a helix entry turns the start of each later ring. The new start is a vertex of the ring's own polygon. At that vertex, the predicted helix orbit keeps 0.01 mm from the orbits that the earlier rings flew.
- After each ring, the kernel reads the descents that the ring flew. It uses the crossing law itself (`verify::crossed_pairs`, 0.01 mm and 0.001 mm chords). If a descent crosses a descent of an earlier ring, the operation is refused by name: `helix entry: the descent at ... crosses the descent of an earlier ring ...`.
- The first ring and each ring without a conflict keep vertex 0. Plunge entry, ramp entry and the vault mode do not change.
- The new logic is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular_helix.rs`.
- The test module of `circular.rs` moved to `circular_tests.rs` (the `#[path]` pattern). `circular.rs` was 411 lines. It is now 374 lines.

## Cause

All rings of a flat Circular run the same level ladder. Thus the helix of each ring shares each level's depth band with the helix of each other ring. The descent puts each helix next to the ring start, and all rings started at the +X vertex. With stepover 2 and helix radius 1, the helices touched. The crossing law reported each pair, and verification blocked the post.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/motion/tests/circular_helix_rings.rs`:

- `a_multi_ring_helix_circular_has_no_crossing`: the issue's job (R10, Ø6, stepover 2, helix 1) and four more sizes, climb and conventional, at two centers. No crossing pair. Red before the fix (`feed moves 2 and 83 cross ...`, 22 pairs).
- `the_issue_job_verifies_without_crossings`: full `verify` on the issue's job. No warning except `RapidInStock`. Red before the fix (Crossing).
- `a_helix_that_cannot_stand_apart_is_refused_by_name`: helix radius 3 on a Ø6 cutter in R10 is refused by name. Other sizes generate with no crossing, or are refused by name. Red before the fix (it generated with crossings).
- `every_ring_still_reaches_the_floor`: each ring still cuts its full circle at the floor.

Unit tests: `circular_helix::tests` (halving order, orbit test, the reading) and `a_phase_turns_the_ring_start_only`.

Mutations:

- Stagger off (phase always 0): the three generation pins go red, because the reading refuses the job.
- Refusal off: `a_helix_that_cannot_stand_apart_is_refused_by_name` goes red.
- The upstream `circular.rs`: three pins go red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (133 steps, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Expected test change

`crates/app/tests/circular_arcs.rs::the_issue_table_posts_arcs_and_verifies_the_same`: three rows now expect the named refusal. On upstream, Crossing warnings already held each of them:

| Row | Crossing warnings before |
|---|---|
| `helix_radius: 0.5` | 30 |
| `radius: 4.0` | 154 |
| `radius: 6.0` | 350 |

The radius rows were also the table's gouge check. They are judged again on a plunge entry, and they must still gouge.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. They must run before this PR is flagged ready.
- The app-level job of #2898 with a helix entry. The motion pin uses the same numbers.
- The two `RapidInStock` warnings on the ring links. They are on upstream too, at the same move indices. #2898 owns them (claimed, no PR yet).

## Overlaps

- No open PR changes `circular.rs`.
- #2898 has a live claim on the ring links of the same function `circular()`. It has no PR or branch yet. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3109-circular-helix-stagger.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Circular - a helix entry with several rings no longer makes helices that touch and block the post; each later ring starts where its helix stays clear, or the operation is refused by name.

Fixes #3109

title: fix(3d): an Adaptive fallback to Offset rings raises a warning
body:
Stacked on #3062 (merge #3062 first).

This PR is partial work on #3035. It does the warning part only.

## What changed

- `camcraft_sim::verify::Warning` has a new variant, `StrategyFallback { at, areas }`.
  - It is advisory. `blocks_post` is false.
  - `at` is the first cutting move. `areas` is the number of areas that the Offset rings cut in place of the Adaptive plan.
- Generate (`operation/generate.rs`) counts the fallback notes and adds the warning when the count is more than zero.
  - The op now reports `warnings` > 0 in MCP `get_job` and `generate`.
  - MCP `verify` lists the finding as `strategy_fallback` with `blocks_post: false`.
  - The UI folds the warning on its own key (225).
- `machining2d::RINGS_FALLBACK` holds the note tail `" - Offset rings cut "`. The 2D door (`pocket_hsm`) and the 3D ladder (`machining3d::hsm::rings_tag`) both use it. `machining2d::rings_fallbacks` counts the notes by it. The note text does not change.
- The rest pass and the offset shells are not counted. Their Offset rings are by design, not a fallback.

## Cause

The planner wrote each fallback to Offset rings only into the path notes. The op status stayed `ok` with `warnings=0`. In the QA run, 14 levels fell back and nothing showed it except the notes.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `app strategy_fallback::an_adaptive_fallback_to_offset_rings_is_a_warning` (new). Before the fix it failed: `one fallback warning: []`, left 0, right 1.
  - `motion lib machining3d::hsm::fallback_tests::a_refused_level_counts_as_one_rings_fallback` (new).
- Mutations:
  - `generate.rs` from upstream/main (no guard): the app pin is red. Restored: green.
  - `rings_fallbacks` that matches nothing: the motion pin is red. Restored: green.
- Expected changes: these suites pinned "verifies clean" as zero warnings on fixtures that already fall back to rings. Each now allows only the fallback warning, and only when the notes name a fallback:
  - `adaptive_pinch`
  - `adaptive_zero_margin_island` (the MCP `findings` check skips `strategy_fallback` only)
  - `climb_direction`
  - `shoulder_adaptive`
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 312 steps. The first run had 4 red binaries, all from the new warning. After the test updates, the 4 binaries are green (`--failed` rerun).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. The posted G-code does not change.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) did not run. A heavy test that asserts zero warnings on an Adaptive op that falls back will now see one advisory warning.
- The QA part of #3035 (the mould core STL on len) did not run.
- Two parts of #3035 stay open:
  - the run time of Rough12, Rest6 and Waterline6 (5 to 13 min, or more);
  - a long generate that blocks every other MCP call, with no cancel tool.

## Overlaps

- #3062: the same function (`fold_warnings_located`, `crates/ui/src/operations.rs`). This PR is stacked on it.
- #3080 and #2714 touch `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`, different variants and arms. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3103, #3033 and #2836 touch `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`, other functions. #2836 adds `UndercutLift` on key 222; this PR uses 225.
- Many open PRs touch `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. This PR adds 7 lines after the drill-size law.

Effort: max (this part is smaller; the rest of #3035 stays at its label).

title: fix(motion): turning offset claims a segment only where its tangent point lies on it
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: the line claim of a profile segment now holds only over its claim window. In that window the tangent point of the ball is on the segment. The claim window is the segment's station window, shifted by `d*b/sqrt(1 + b^2)`. At other stations, the circle about the nearer end point makes the claim.
- The OD ride (`profile_offset`) and the bore ride (`profile_offset_in`) use the same rule, through one private helper (`seg_claims`, `SegClaim`, `seg_range`).
- `seg_range` replaces the old probe of the ±1 neighbour segments. A shifted window can reach past the next segment.
- The two catalog programs `turning/cone-thread` and `turning/contour-finishes` are regenerated.
- `docs/decisions/2881-offset-tangent-window.md` records the decision.

## Cause

The old code held the infinite offset line of a segment over the segment's own station window. This is wrong in two directions:

- A steep, short chord claimed its line far above the bar. The first chord of a fillet has a slope of 16.6, so the claim was 167 mm too high (X354 on a 30 mm bar).
- A sloped face did not claim the stations before its inside corner, where it is the nearest piece. There the ride stood nearer than `d` to the face. This is a small gouge into the leave (0.884 instead of 1.0 at a 45 degree corner in the pin).

## Tests

New suite `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_window.rs`. Each test checks that every ride sample stands at exactly `d` from the profile:

- `a_steep_fillet_chord_keeps_the_ride_on_the_nose`: before the fix the max ride radius was 28.29 on an 11.66 profile.
- `a_sloped_inside_corner_is_not_gouged`: before the fix the ride stood 0.884 from the face at station -0.25.
- `the_inside_ride_obeys_the_same_window`: before the fix the bore ride dived to r 1.71 on an 18.34 wall.

Mutation checks:

- Old `offset.rs` put back: all 3 pins red. Restored: all 3 green.
- Sign of the window shift flipped: all 3 pins red. Restored: all 3 green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (motion lib, `turning_bore`, `turning_offset_window`, `turning_prof`, app `example_catalog`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Also run green in debug: app suites `turning_profile`, `turning_bore`, `turning_bore_feeds`, `turning_contour`, `turning_contour_stock`, `turning_axial_rapids`, `turning_stock_approach`, `turning_hidden_floor`, `turning_insert_zone`, `turning_holder`, `turning_holder_steel`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_turn_radius`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_field_sim`, `recorded_post_streams`, `coarse_laws`, `coarse_rims`, `sim_lathe_body`, `ladder_entry_height`, `carried_stock_entry`, `stepped_stock_rapid`, `project_roundtrip`.


## Latest review fixes

Final head: `8269ae9372c105c7d925828dcfc5e262523e3160`.
Base: `upstream/main` at `211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6`.

- Added the Gate map for `camcraft_motion::turning::offset` to `turning_offset_window.rs`.
- Checked suite selection with the real quick planner in an isolated Git fixture. Only `offset.rs` changed in the fixture.
- Map present: the planner selected `turning_offset_window`. Map removed: the selection assertion failed. Map restored: the assertion passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: all 6 steps passed. Motion lib: 488 passed, 10 ignored. Bore: 11 passed. Offset window: 3 passed. Profile: 8 passed. Catalog: 33 passed, 2 ignored.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: all 234 steps passed, 0 failed, exit 0. The run took 62.5 minutes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed, exit 0.
- The heavy gate reached all motion and app targets. The known-fail checks for `#1950` and `#2849` reproduced their source-marked expected failures.

## Goldens moved

Two `.nc` files. The `.camproj` files do not change: the catalog tests pass with the committed projects.

- `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc`: at the cone-to-flat inside corner (Z59.2), each rough rung and the finish ride lose a run of zero-length `G01` blocks and a vertical drop. The new ride rolls over the corner on the nose circle (for example `G01 X28.532 Z59.697`, then `X28.5 Z60.194`). It stands slightly farther out than the old drop, which was inside the true offset.
- `examples/catalog/turning/contour-finishes/contour-finishes.nc`: near Z0 to Z1 the rides lose about 50 short blocks each that went out toward the spike of a steep chord. The clearance radius drops from `X22.884` to `X21.6`, and from `X20.762` to `X20.1` for the chamfer. The chamfer retract is now a short feed out to X20.1, then the rapid. The operation's own lead-out law makes this choice for the new, nearer clearance.

No other `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.
