title: feat(post): encode a zero-step Agie punch setup from main
body:
## Scope

Add a public `camcraft_post::agie_setup::PunchSetup20::encode` function. A Rust caller can pair its complete SBL piece script and SBR resource manifest with an existing ISO file. The caller supplies a program name, stock bounds and the position of the 2 mm threading hole in micrometres.

The encoder supports one closed punch in 20 mm steel 0001 with Berco 0.25 mm wire, Ra 0.30 and 1 mm separation. It binds the requested native quality and removes the erosion steps on import. The returned review text gives the expected offsets for the operator. The API does not generate, position or verify the caller's ISO contour. The caller must use the matching resource and check it in the control.

This branch starts directly from main at c5f4e6f94. It has no feature-stack commits, no new dependencies and no automatic machining option. The new function works independently of the CAMCraft workspace post. The first workspace writer must call this function and report the controller review before it can ship. The existing feature drafts need their own safety reviews.

## References

The MIT-licensed Agie Processor implementation supplied the Agie-specific interface reference. The contributor's team wrote that implementation. The license notice is in assets/ui/LICENSES.md. The two synthetic expected files come from the contributor's control-checked CCSEP20 example.

## Verification

The complete quick gate passed all 107 steps in 3.1 minutes on the final head befdc57f9. The complete reached heavy gate passed all 197 steps in 64.3 minutes. These commands also passed on that head:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base c5f4e6f94
cargo xtask gate heavy --base c5f4e6f94
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-post --doc agie_setup
cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

All four integration tests passed. The public API example compiled and ran. An independent Rust caller reproduced the complete CCSEP20.SBL and CCSEP20.SBR files byte for byte. On a copy of the actual offline control, the new piece had zero working steps. FORMALCHECK required the operator to define the technology. The work showed the intended punch, ISO, stock height and threading hole.

The pinning tests are:

- `setup_files_match_the_control_checked_zero_step_punch`
- `a_named_resource_and_signed_micron_coordinates_round_trip`
- `device_names_paths_and_script_text_cannot_enter_an_agie_record`
- `stock_and_full_start_hole_must_fit_the_setup_span`

No physical erosion was performed.

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.

## Gates

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 687 steps.
  - The first full run had 685 ok and 2 red steps: `app build (--no-run)` and `app suites: break_through`. The cause was one test literal: the `strategy` field was in a Drill literal in `crates/app/tests/break_through.rs`, not in the Bore literal.
  - After the fix, `--failed` on that run: 2 steps, 0 failed. The fix changed only that test file.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on the final head c70e84309: the motion and app heavy lanes, 231 steps, 0 failed (50.3 min).

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A non-centre-cutting tool helixes like any other tool. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 2b95e5701.

Fixes #2830

title: fix(app): judge the mill kinds' first traverse on a mill-turn
body:
Stacked on #3097 (#3077). The diff against `main` also shows the commits of #3097. Review only the #3083 commits. Retarget this PR after #3097 merges.

## What changed

- `first_traverse::mill_order(kind, lathe_tool, params)` is new. It is true on a mill and on a mill-turn for a milling tool. A mill-turn posts a milling tool through the Fanuc mill post. That post sends Z to the clearance, then X/Y at that height (`fanuc.cps` `traverseZ`, `xyFirst`). This is the order that the first-traverse laws read.
- `generate.rs` reads `mill_order` in `turned_axis` and in the two `judge` calls, in place of `is_mill && !lathe_tool`. The planar, 3-D, hole and multi-axis kinds on a mill-turn now get the upright law, the 3+2 table law and the tip law. The laws do not change. The #3077 flag stays: `mill_order || mill_post_cross`.
- A rotary kind (`Mode::Rotary`) on a mill-turn stays out of the law. There it is a radial live tool on the spindle C, and the mill premise refuses each such program. Follow-up #3096 (P1) owns it.
- The struck-link planner and the mesh steel stay mill-only. The post gate judges each link of a mill-turn against the steel and refuses a struck link. The box verdict is stricter than the mesh verdict. Decision items 5 and 6 give the reasons.
- `current_stamp` writes the word `first-traverse-mill-turn-3083` for a judged mill kind on a mill-turn setup. Those caches read Stale one time. No stamp of a mill changes. No shipped example or catalog project mounts a mill-turn.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3083-mill-turn-first-traverse.md`. It states the premise: the start is at the tool-change height. A program that starts low is not covered.

## Readings

- 2D, refused: a steady with its top at Z40 and a face clearance of Z30 give `FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 30, top_mm: 40, fixture: true }`. The post refuses by name.
- 2D, clear: the same steady with its top at Z25 gives no warnings. The program is byte-identical to the bare program.
- 3+2 on the mill-turn's B at B10: clearance Z25 is refused, with the high corner of the stock at 5.209 mm along the tool axis. Clearance Z30 is clear.

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse_mill_turn::a_mill_turn_face_under_a_far_steady_holds_the_post_by_name`
- `first_traverse_mill_turn::a_mill_turn_face_over_a_low_steady_posts_the_bare_program`
- `first_traverse_mill_turn::a_mill_turn_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis`
- lib: `operation::first_traverse::tests::a_mill_turn_judges_its_milling_kinds_in_the_mill_order`

Two tests change because of the new stamp word. Each one generated a face on a mill and then mounted a mill-turn. The face now reads Stale one time, so each test regenerates it after the mount:

- `carried_fixtures_cache::a_carry_on_a_lathe_or_mill_turn_is_refused_by_name_on_every_path`
- `coolant_followups::m88_posts_on_the_shipped_mill_turn_machine`

## Gate

Debug, `-j 18`. The full list below ran on `8d60842b1` (main `fc32feb0e` + #3097 `2bfad698a`). There, only `coolant_followups` failed (the stamp case, fixed). The final head `dc80c1aeb` (+ #3097 LF head `6c4939b18`) ran again: `coolant_followups`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `drilling_cross` and clippy, all green.

- camcraft-app tests, green: `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `drilling_cross`, `coarse_cross_drill`, `drilling_cross_box`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `setup_align_mill_turn`, `coolant_followups`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `drill_prior_kinds`, `turning`, `drilling_cross_spindle`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `c_axis_fixture`, `c_axis_live_world`, `lathe_workholding_live`, `rotary_letter`, `setup_align_multiaxis`
- camcraft-app lib `first_traverse`: green
- camcraft-sim lib `live_traverse`: green
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.
- The other app binaries are not run here. They are left to the batch gate of the stack.
- A lathe post on a mill op of a mill-turn: not judged (decision, dropped options).

Changelog: On a mill-turn machine, the first rapid of the milling operations (2D, 3D, drilling and multi-axis) is now checked against the stock and the fixtures, as on a mill. A rapid that is too low blocks the post. Mill-turn operations of these kinds read Stale one time and must be generated again.

title: fix(sim): judge the first traverse of a lathe or mill-turn cross drill from the turret's index position
body:
## What changed

A cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn now has a first-traverse law. Generation refuses a cross drill by name if its first rapid from the turret's index position can pass the work or the steel.

- **Premise.** The unknown start is the turret's index position, at the top of the X and Z travel. This is the premise of #2987 and of the upright law. A program that starts with the tool low near the work (for example after a manual jog) is not covered. The decision file says so.
- **The post's real first move.** `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` (lines 717-720) writes `G00 C`, then `G00 X Z` to the first motion record. The record stream writes the END of each move only (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:532-536`). The start of the first move goes out only as `StartX/Y/Z` (`mod.rs:274-280`), and `liveMove` does not move there. So the first G00 X Z goes to the R-plane point of the first hole.
- **The law** (`camcraft_sim::verify::live_first_traverse`, `crates/sim/src/verify/live_traverse.rs`).
  - A G00 moves each axis at its own rate. Thus the tip can pass every radius from the first point out, at every Z from the first point up, in the station's plane.
  - The tool lies along the radius. The swept solid follows the tool stack: flute, then shank, then holder, the widest band so far.
  - The work and the chuck are read at the C angle: each facet is clipped exactly.
  - Fixed steel (a tailstock, the table) is read revolved about the spindle.
  - A face that only touches the swept solid passes. The model excess follows the #1053 law.
- **Seam.** `crates/app/src/operation/cross_traverse.rs` is called in the cross branch of `generate.rs`. A hit gives `GenError::Invalid` with the solid's name, so nothing posts. A mill-turn cross drill also answers to the upright law, because its default post is the mill post.
- **Cache.** The cross drill's op stamp gets the word `live-traverse-3077`.
- **One test fixture changed** (coordinator decision, recorded in the decision file).
  - In `drilling_cross::recognition_finds_the_bar_two_holes_and_they_generate`, the 44 mm box stock stands out to X 22 from Z 0 up. At clearance 20, the first hole's R plane is at radius 20, Z -10. The first rapid's Z leg passes 2 mm of uncut stock, so the law refuses it correctly.
  - The test's clearance is now 30, which puts the R plane at radius 30. The test still pins the recognition and the generation.
  - Dropped: a rule that this stock is not there.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3077-lathe-cross-first-traverse.md`.

## Readings

- Example refusal: "the stock reaches out to 22.000 from the spindle at Z0.000" (the old recognition fixture).
- `coarse_cross_drill`: a flange flush with the R plane (x 20) is clear. Earlier drafts refused it.
- `drilling_cross_box`: the Ø12 shank stands 30 mm behind the tip and does not meet a lump 3 mm beside the drill's line. An earlier draft refused it.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_cross_drill.rs`:
  - `a_cross_drill_over_its_chuck_has_a_clear_first_traverse`
  - `a_cross_drill_under_a_wide_tailstock_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_thin_tailstock_centre_is_clear_on_a_lathe_and_convicts_a_mill_turn`
  - `a_turning_collar_flush_with_the_first_point_is_clear_and_one_proud_of_it_is_refused`
- `crates/sim/src/verify/live_traverse_tests.rs`: 9 unit tests (tool width, touch, #1053 excess, shank band, half-plane, square bar, clipped facet, spindle off origin, unreadable input).

## Quick gate (local, debug)

- camcraft-sim lib `live_traverse`: 9 of 9 pass.
- camcraft-app on the final head: `drilling_cross` (9), `coarse_cross_drill` (6), `lathe_cross_drill` (9), `drilling_cross_box` (7) pass.
- camcraft-app on `37a84a2b5` (before the #1053 excess change and the fixture change): these binaries pass:
  - `cross_drill_neighbours`, `drill_reach`
  - `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_part`, `drilling_cross_spindle`, `drilling_cross_stock`
  - `first_traverse_rotary`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `stock_source_cross_drill`
- The later changes apply the excess only when the model has one, and they change one test case.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: not run, covered by the cut gate.
- The `operations` suite was not run on this head.
- The turret body is not modelled.
- The other mill-turn kinds stay outside this law (#3083).

Note: PR #3093 (#3081) also changes `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`. This PR does not change that file. It changes the call at the upright judge in `generate.rs`.

Changelog: A cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn is refused by name when its first rapid from the turret's index position can pass the stock, a part, a chuck or a tailstock.

Effort: max (escalated from high)

Fixes #3077

title: fix(sim): judge a reduced-accuracy model at its own chord error, up to 0.02 mm
body:
## What changed

A finishing operation can now post for an eligible model opened at reduced accuracy. The model page and program header state the true-surface bound.

The importer records whether the file tolerance caused the coarse mesh. Import, project save/load, model copies, stock copies and undo preserve this record. Update undo restores each copy's own cause. A cause change invalidates cached verdicts. Missing records, budget coarsening and mixed causes keep the strict law of #864.

For an eligible model, the chord `c` selects the law:

| Chord | Mesh allowance |
|---|---|
| Up to 0.010 mm | The existing strict law. |
| Over 0.010 mm through 0.020 mm | `min(t - 0.005, 0.005)` mm, where `t` is the law's tolerance. |
| Over 0.020 mm | The existing strict law. No allowance remains at `DEV_TOL`; the operation is refused by name. |

The allowance never exceeds the law's tolerance. Collision bands still grow by the full excess. Turning, rotary and probe guards keep their strict laws. The program gate also keeps the strict law for those operation kinds.

At a chord of 0.019 mm, the mesh allowance is 0.005 mm. The true-surface bound is 0.024 mm. The header says:

```text
Reduced accuracy: model brick was checked to 0.024 mm, not 0.010 mm
```

The model page and MCP facts state the same bound. The display rounds the bound upward. A chord of 0.0192 mm gives a numerical bound of 0.0242 mm and a displayed bound of 0.025 mm.

The engine sends each header note through `onComment` after `onOpen`. All 19 shipped posts use valid dialect comments and preserve the complete bound. A custom post can omit the note.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2996-wide-verdict.md`. The maximum widened true-surface bound is 0.025 mm. This is below the maintainer's accepted 0.030 mm limit.

## UI evidence

The model page now states both the mesh approximation and the true-surface bound used by the checks. The UI import path also preserves the recorded cause during a model update.

Both images render the actual Properties page through the existing egui shell test harness, with the same model at a 0.019 mm chord. The after image uses the current head. The before image uses the summary function body from `upstream/main`, temporarily substituted into the same harness. The harness uses a placeholder viewport. All temporary source edits were restored.

The temporary UI assertion `pr_3087_reduced_accuracy_note_capture` passed on this head. Substituting the old summary made it fail. Restoring this head made it pass again.

Before:

![Model note before this change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/63c577851d096674d43364f7e6722c04b75d3430/3087/model-note-before.png)

After:

![Model note after this change](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/63c577851d096674d43364f7e6722c04b75d3430/3087/model-note-after.png)

The images are stored only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No image, log or review evidence is committed to this PR branch.

## Tests and mutation checks

The main pins are:

- `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound`: all 19 shipped posts, with hostile note text.
- `model_excess::absent_or_budget_cause_keeps_the_original_mesh_tolerance`: missing and budget causes keep the original boundary assertions.
- `model_fidelity_cause`: import, persistence, copies and undo preserve the cause.
- `model_fidelity_wide`: a permitted model posts with the header note; a model beyond the limit is refused; a deeper gouge blocks posting. The suite also checks upward rounding and cache invalidation after a cause change.
- `model_excess::an_eligible_file_caps_larger_law_tolerances_at_the_header_allowance` and `coarse_probe_plasma::a_file_tolerance_plasma_check_keeps_the_stated_true_surface_bound`: larger base tolerances also respect the 0.005 mm cap.
- `coarse_laws`: rotary operations keep the strict law.

The [author's follow-up](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3087#issuecomment-7058458064) records 39 focused tests passed. All 12 mutations failed with the relevant fix removed, then passed after restoration.

The [latest independent review](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3087#issuecomment-7059566865) repeated two mutations. Taking the full excess failed at `model_excess.rs:312`. Using the widened deduction for collision-band growth failed at line 317. After restoration, all 16 tests in `model_excess` and `coarse_collision` passed.

No fixture, golden or snapshot PNG changes belong to this PR.

## Gate evidence

Validated head: `fb3e8cf4c8627ee9f3408b81340515df3d6fa70a`.

The latest independent review used `upstream/main` at `11402dba4c849c5f827dccebc14f850196614311`. Its trial merge was clean. All checks ran locally.

title: fix(app): a 3+2 first-traverse refusal names the heights the user set
body:
## What changed

- `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`) gets the field `tilted: bool` with `#[serde(default)]`. A cache saved before this change still loads, and reads as upright.
- `operation::first_traverse::judge` (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs`) puts a 3+2 verdict into the frame in which the user sets the heights. Generate shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the tilted frame. The new `in_user_frame` adds `origin.z` back to the two heights and sets `tilted` when the frame is not upright. The sim law does not change.
- A tilted verdict has a new text. It names the heights that the user set, says that they are measured along the tilted tool axis, and gives the raise. It has no `Z` value and no `X/Y`. The text of an upright verdict does not change.
- Guide: a troubleshooting entry for the new text (`site/content/guide/reference/troubleshooting.md`), and one paragraph in `site/content/guide/multi-axis/indexed.md` that says what the warning gives after a regenerate.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2991-tilted-first-traverse-message.md`.

## Readings

`examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`, `Indexed Face1` (B 20 deg, tilt origin Z 20, Fixed clearance height 30). The operation cache was removed in a scratch copy, so `camcraft-cli process` generated it again:

- Before: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z10.000, under the stock top at Z11.114 - raise the clearance height above Z11.114`
- After: `the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown position at the clearance height 30.000 mm, under the stock top at 31.114 mm (both measured along the tilted tool axis) - raise the clearance height by at least 1.114 mm`

A clearance height of 31.114 or more passes the law (the local value is then 11.114 or more).

## Pinning tests

- `first_traverse::a_3_2_plane_reads_the_stock_top_along_its_tool_axis` (app): the verdict gives the typed clearance (25, not the local 5), the corner in the same frame (25.209), `tilted: true`, the new text without `Z` or `X/Y`, and the post refusal with the raise. It fails without the change in `judge` (`tilted` stays false).
- `verify::first_traverse::tests::a_tilted_verdict_names_the_raise_not_a_z_value` (sim): the full tilted text and a serde round trip.
- `verify::first_traverse::tests::a_verdict_saved_before_tilted_reads_as_upright` (sim): a cache JSON without `tilted` loads as upright, with the old text.
- `docs_troubleshooting` (app): the new troubleshooting heading matches the source text.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 109 steps, 0 failed (sim, motion and app suites, with `first_traverse`, `clearance_in_stock`, `wcs_start` and `stale_rapid_law`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: the diff reaches 234 heavy steps (199 app, 34 motion). On head 9eee9c59d: 234 steps, 0 failed, wall time 58 min. The 16 known-fail steps (#1950, #2845 and others) are red as expected. `motion heavy: pocket3d_hsm` passes.

## Not exercised

- A saved cache keeps its old text until the operation is generated again. The verdict and the held post do not change. I did not change the op stamp salt, because that moves each stamp (`deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`, the example projects) for a text change. For the same reason I did not regenerate `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`. The decision file records the two choices.
- No GUI check of the Warnings pane. The pane shows the `Display` text that the tests pin.

Changelog: The first-traverse refusal of a tilted (3+2) operation names the clearance height that the user set, says that the heights are measured along the tilted tool axis, and says how much to raise the clearance height.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 2ec4ad7e0.

Fixes #2991

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.
- #2924 adds rows to `commands/mod.rs` and `script/mod.rs`, and changes `mcp/sketch_tools.rs`. This PR adds other rows to the two `mod.rs` files and puts its MCP tool in a new file. The files are the same and the functions are different. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2678 adds lines to `commands/mod.rs`. The lines are different.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

title: feat(waterjet): Waterjet Profile operation on a shared 2D sheet kernel
body:
## What changed

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/sheet/`).** The kernel code moves out of `plasma` and `wire_edm` without a change of behaviour:
  - `nest` (contour roles, inner-first cut order) and `ring` (kerf ring, walks), from `plasma`;
  - `laws` (kerf law, cover law) and `lead` (straight and arc leads), from `plasma`;
  - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), from `wire_edm::tabs`;
  - `open` (the one-sided offset of an open run), from `wire_edm::open`.

  A `Voice` keeps each refusal text word for word. Plasma and wire EDM now call the shared code.
- **Cover law.** The law now takes one span or more for each contour, and an `exempt` closure for a tab's bridge. Plasma exempts no point. The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
- **Waterjet generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`).** `waterjet_profile` does these steps:
  - It cuts the inner contours first, with the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side.
  - It adds straight or arc leads, with the pierce in the scrap. A lead with no room is halved up to four times.
  - It pierces a tight hole at its centre when the lead has no room after the halving.
  - It cuts tabs as uncut gaps. Each stretch between two gaps gets its own pierce, lead-in and lead-out.
  - It cuts open runs on the centre line, or to the left or right of travel.
  - It can post G41/G42, and it can send arcs as chords (`Move::chords`).

  The kerf law and the cover law certify the result.
- **App.** The changes are:
  - `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (stored id 44), `Section::Waterjet` and `Family::Waterjet`. The op mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet` nozzle only.
  - `WaterjetOp` with its command-door sanity check, `waterjet_op.rs` (seed, params, generate) and the digest bytes.
  - A `.camproj` DTO (`waterjet_profile`, additive).
  - Each exhaustive match in the app gets a waterjet arm.
  - Profile (DXF) sources are admitted. The family door has its own words: "mount a waterjet first".
  - MCP reaches the kind through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`. The `add_operation` text now names waterjet.
- **UI.** The changes are:
  - `waterjet_page.rs` with these fields: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side, send arcs as lines, sheet heights, tabs, lead shape and lengths, cut feed, pierce time, abrasive delay. It has no torch height or THC field.
  - The Waterjet ribbon section.
  - An original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-waterjet-profile.svg`, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`).

## Readings

- Golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` has 149 moves, 5 pierces and 3 holes cut before the outline. The outline is cut as two led-in stretches between 2 mm tabs.
- The existing goldens do not change. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows only the new file. The plasma golden `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl` stays byte-identical after the kernel move.

## Tests (pins)

Each pin was red before this change: the module and the kind did not exist, so the pins could not compile.

- motion `waterjet::tests` (9): `holes_are_cut_before_the_outline_and_every_pierce_is_in_the_waste`, `straight_leads_lay_no_arc_on_a_square_part`, `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_and_each_stretch_is_pierced_and_led_in`, `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre`, `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords`, `an_open_run_rides_its_stated_side`, `control_compensation_records_a_comp_span_per_untabbed_contour`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`.
- app `waterjet_profile` (6): the family door, hole first, tabs, a milling tool refused, create / edit / undo / redo, and a byte-identical `.camproj` round trip.
- app `mcp_waterjet` (1): add, edit, undo, redo and generate over MCP.
- app `golden_cl::waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes_matches_golden`.
- ui `waterjet_ribbon_tests` (2): the section shows on a waterjet only, the tip names the waterjet, the glyph is its own, and the page has a leads tab.
- Plasma and wire EDM: all `camcraft-motion` plasma, sheet and wire tests pass, and all 34 `golden_cl` tests pass.

## Mutation results

Each mutation was applied, the pins were run, and then the code was restored (green again).

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Inner-first order removed | red: `holes_are_cut_before_...`, `a_tight_hole_...` |
| Tabs ignored | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...`, `bad_input_...` |
| Tight-hole rule off | red: `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre` |
| Linearization ignored | red: `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords` |
| Cover law exempts every point | red: `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` |
| Cover law exempts no point | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...` (6 mm tabs) |
| Leads on the part side | red: 7 of 9 pins |

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 422 steps ran (374 app, 44 post, 3 motion, 1 cl). The only red steps were kind-count pins that this change extends on purpose: `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`, `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` and `tests/ribbon.rs` (`family_is_derived_not_forked`, `the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`). I updated them to 45 kinds and the Waterjet section. Because I edited during the run, the gate marked that run VOID. `--failed` on the committed tree then ran the red step: green. The app lib suite is green (290).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1324 passed, 0 failed. The waterjet row was added to `tips_match_the_imgui_table`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Not exercised

- Posting. No post serves `Kind::Waterjet` yet. The pierce time and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only. #1882 adds the CL record and the post hooks.
- `verify` and the post gate for a waterjet op. That is #1885.
- Selection of the cut data from the nozzle's recipe. This is follow-up #3047.
- The MCP skill row. The skill file is a protected path in this session. This is follow-up #3048.
- Heavy lanes. The diff reaches `motion` and the `app` heavy lanes. I did not run `cargo xtask gate heavy` locally.
- The UI page was not opened in an interactive window. The screenshots below come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell.

## Screenshots

These show the ribbon with the Waterjet section and each tab of the op page. The part is a 40x40 plate with a 10x10 hole and two 2 mm tabs. The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch (commit `1c0727b08`).

| View | Image |
|---|---|
| Ribbon, Waterjet section | ![ribbon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1c0727b08b498999fc59b2b2a13c951455bea92e/pr-3058/ribbon-waterjet-section.png) |
| Geometry tab | ![geometry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1c0727b08b498999fc59b2b2a13c951455bea92e/pr-3058/page-geometry.png) |
| Heights tab | ![heights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1c0727b08b498999fc59b2b2a13c951455bea92e/pr-3058/page-heights.png) |
| Passes tab (tabs) | ![passes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1c0727b08b498999fc59b2b2a13c951455bea92e/pr-3058/page-passes-tabs.png) |
| Lead in / Lead out tab | ![leads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1c0727b08b498999fc59b2b2a13c951455bea92e/pr-3058/page-leads.png) |
| Feeds tab | ![feeds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1c0727b08b498999fc59b2b2a13c951455bea92e/pr-3058/page-feeds.png) |

## Overlaps

- These open PRs also append an op kind to the same enums and tables (`kinds.rs`, `types/params.rs`, `project/params*.rs`): #2920, #2890, #2836, #2831, #2716, #2714. The conflicts are additive (both sides add arms). The PR that merges second takes the next free stored id.
- These open PRs touch `generate.rs` or `job.rs`, in other functions: #2997, #2822, #2678, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978. The PR that merges second refreshes.
- #2932 touches `crates/ui/src/interact.rs`, in other functions.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1883-waterjet-profile.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Waterjet Profile operation - inner-first 2D through-cuts with kerf offset, straight or arc leads pierced in the scrap, tabs as uncut gaps (each stretch led in and out straight, and a lead that cuts a tab's bridge is refused), the tight-hole centre pierce, open-run sides, optional G41/G42 and arc linearization; plasma and wire EDM now share one 2D sheet kernel.

body:
## What changed

This PR adds the UI for DXF profiles over the #1862 commands (`ImportDxf`, `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`). It follows the maintainer's scope change on the issue: the DXF door is on the Stock page, not on `Model > Open`.

- The Stock page has a new group "DXF profiles". It has the control "Add DXF profile…" (a `.dxf` file picker). The control is disabled when the active setup has no stock.
- The group lists each profile of the active setup with these controls:
  - "Profile X", "Profile Y" and "Profile angle (deg)". These are a draft. "Place profile" queues one `MoveSketch`.
  - "Hide profile" / "Show profile". This is view state, the same list as the browser eye.
  - "Delete profile". This queues one `DeleteEntity`.
- A `.dxf` file dropped on the viewport goes through the same import path. With no stock, the drop is refused by name: "drop refused: <file> is a DXF profile - make a stock first ...".
- A drawing without `$INSUNITS` opens the modal "DXF units". The modal shows the drawing size read in millimeters and read in inches, each with the size in the other unit. "Millimeters" or "Inches" runs `ImportDxf` with that unit. "Cancel", Escape or a backdrop click places nothing. The unit is never guessed.
- The status line shows the import summary: the name, the setup, the unit and its source (file or chosen), the layer count, the closed and open chain counts, the chains not chained, and the skipped entities by type.
- The browser shows each profile as a child row of its setup's Stock row (`Leaf::Sketch`), with the suffix "DXF profile" and the eye. A click opens the Stock page and selects the profile, so Del deletes it through the history.
- The viewport draws the profile lines, arcs and circles of the active setup on the stock top, at `sketch::world_pose`. Each free end of an open chain gets a magenta X. No curve uses that colour, so an open gap does not look closed.
- The overlay lines are cached by the sketch data `Arc` and the pose (`SketchLineCache` on `FrameCache`). A still frame builds nothing (crates/ui/AGENTS.md, frame cost).
- The operation page Source list offers the profiles of the operation's setup for a kind that `sketch_model::admits` (2D milling, plasma, wire EDM). A setup with a stock, a profile and no model can so have an operation on the profile.
- `camcraft_app` re-exports `camcraft_geometry::dxf`, so the UI can name the `Primitive` variants. This adds no crate dependency.

The import does not use `finish_import`. That function handles the model worker. `ImportDxf` checks the drawing at construction, so the typed `DxfUnitsMissing` error is caught where the UI builds the command. `docs/decisions/1863-dxf-stock-ui.md` records this and the other choices.

## Cause

The #1862 commands had no UI door. A user could place a DXF profile only through MCP or the script.

## Tests

New pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/dxf_profile.rs`:

- `the_stock_page_adds_lists_places_and_deletes_a_dxf_profile`
- `a_drawing_without_units_asks_millimeters_or_inches_and_never_guesses`
- `a_dropped_dxf_lands_on_the_stock_or_asks_for_one`
- `the_browser_lists_the_profile_under_its_stock_with_an_eye`
- `the_viewport_draws_the_chains_on_the_stock_top_and_marks_open_ends`
- `the_operation_page_takes_the_profile_as_its_source_without_a_model`
- `a_still_frame_builds_no_profile_lines_and_a_move_builds_once`

Also:

- `page_layout_windows::layout_window_dxf_units` (the named layout test of the new modal).
- `dxf_units_dialog::tests::readings_state_both_units_both_ways`.
- `dxf_drop::tests::dxf_by_extension_in_any_case`.

Red before the fix: yes. On upstream/main the pins do not compile. `CommandKind::ImportDxf`, `CommandKind::MoveSketch`, `State::dxf_units_prompt`, `Leaf::Sketch`, `sketch_overlay` and `op_source` do not exist.

Mutation checks (each red with the mutation, green when restored):

- Guess millimeters for a drawing without units: `a_drawing_without_units...` is red ("nothing lands before the answer").
- Remove the stock check of the drop: `a_dropped_dxf...` is red (the refusal does not name the file).
- Remove the profiles from the Source list: `the_operation_page...` is red.
- Draw a hidden profile: `the_viewport_draws...` is red.
- Bypass the line cache: `a_still_frame_builds...` is red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 4cf20695e (19 steps, 0 failed: app lib, ui lib and 17 ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No posted G-code, CL file or snapshot PNG changes.

## Not exercised

- Before and after screenshots are attached below. The captures use the real offscreen renderer. The structural tests pin the labels, the rows and the overlay vertices.
- A `.dxf` dropped in the browser build (wasm) is refused by name. The browser drop path delivers model bytes only.
- The native file picker of "Add DXF profile…" is not driven in a test. The test calls the same `CommandKind::ImportDxf`.

## Overlaps

These open PRs touch the same files, in different functions. The PR that merges second refreshes.

- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978, #2974, #2972, #2969, #2968, #2964, #2955, #2951, #2786, #2773, #2763, #2932. This PR adds enum variants, two fields and four dispatch arms only.

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_tree.rs`: #2714. This PR adds a variant to `Leaf` and rows in `setup_children`.
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs`: #2932 (a constant). This PR adds one line in `collect_overlay`.
- `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` is not changed.

Changelog: The Stock page places a DXF profile on the stock top ("Add DXF profile…", or drop a `.dxf` on the viewport), asks for the unit when the drawing states none, lists and places profiles, shows them in the browser and on the stock with open chain ends marked, and offers them as the Source of 2D, plasma and wire EDM operations.

Fixes #1863

title: fix(sim): verify shallow spot drills with their cone radius
body:
## What changed

The finish-wall check reads the cone radius at the stock top for ordinary axial drilling moves.
A 6 mm, 120-degree spot at 1 mm depth now verifies and posts inside a 5 mm pilot.
A spot that enlarges the finished hole still reports a gouge and blocks the post.

The check uses the existing `Cutter::judged` and cone atom geometry.
It keeps the nominal radius for model sections, tool poses, arcs, lateral moves and unsupported cutter shapes.
The solid and stock checks still judge the actual cutter.

## Cause

The previous tangency check compared the hole wall with the nominal cylinder.
At this depth, that cylinder remains above the stock.
The cone reaches a radius of 1.732 mm inside the 2.5 mm pilot radius.

## Tests

Both shallow pins failed on unchanged `upstream/main` at `3c761b5bb`.
The app pin reported `Gouge { at: 1 }`.

title: feat(post): waterjet records, CR LF, travel, programBounds and a generic waterjet post
body:
## Review fixes and final-head validation

Final head: `ca7ba50664f6d4605b96f468b17eccc6a04f5821`.

This update fixes the two findings in the latest review.

1. The engine preserves the original motion record's signed Z change on every generated chord. The waterjet post refuses that change before it writes a cutting block. Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_a_helical_arc_in_both_arc_modes`. The test checks the named Z refusal and no cutting blocks in circular and linear modes.
2. The missing-machine test checks the CLI refusal separately from the generation log. Pin: `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`. The test enables INFO logs and checks that the log names `Face1`. The selected refusal names `Setup2` and does not name `Face1`. The complete output still must name `Face2`.

Both pins pass. Each fix was removed separately. Each pin then failed with exit 101. Each restored fix passed.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 997 steps pass in 40.1 minutes.
- Clippy: GREEN in 78 seconds. All eight project crates pass with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. All 234 steps ran in 33.8 minutes. One step failed.
- The failed step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. Its failed test is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`.
- The test produced `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. Its Linux assertion expects `(4726, 4698, 549)`.
- All other reached motion and app heavy steps pass. The gate accepted the declared known-fail checks.
- The same test fails on the exact parent source, `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f`, with exit 101 and the same counts. The check restored all five changed files byte-for-byte. This update makes no unrelated change.

The PR remains a draft. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

The sections below describe the original implementation and its historical validation. Their test counts and gate results are historical.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 996 steps, 0 failed (wall 30.5 min; the `cl` change reaches each dependent crate). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branch history: the first commit was squashed onto a newer main by mistake, so it reverted nine files of the Tormach lathe G76 work (#2952). The second commit restores them from main. The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

## Goldens moved

None. All goldens are new: `crates/post/tests/golden/waterjet/plate.nc`, `plate_inch_chords.nc` and the input `plate.cnc`, plus `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/waterjet-iso/*.refusal`. No existing `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.

## Not exercised

- No generator writes the waterjet records yet. The `Toolpath::waterjet` field and its `.cl` dump come with the WaterjetProfile operation (#1883). The input stream here is written by hand.
- The post is not in `posting::BUILTINS`, so the app does not offer it yet (see the decision record). A user can post with it as a file of their own (`serves = ["waterjet"]`).
- The post did not run on a real waterjet control.

## Overlaps

- #3037 changes `engine.rs` (the `Script::load` line in `run_program_with`) and `js.rs`. This PR touches the same file, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2893 changes `engine.rs` and `js.rs` (fine boring). Same file, different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Post: generic ISO abrasive-waterjet post (`waterjet-iso.cps`), WATERJET / JET stream records with `onJetOn` / `onJetOff`, CR LF output (`lineEnding`), `machine.travel`, `programBounds` and arc linearization (`linearizeArcs`) for scripts.

Effort: high

Fixes #1882

title: feat(mcp): compact read modes and chat context budgets
body:
## What changed

MCP read modes for small context windows (`crates/app/src/mcp/`):

- `get_job` takes `summary: true`. The summary removes `machine.definition`. Each operation keeps only the `params` fields that differ from the kind defaults. Null and empty fields outside `params` are removed.
- `list_operation_types` takes `kind` (key or label) and `section`. An unknown name is refused with the valid names.
- `list_features` takes `compact: true`. Compact rows keep the id, the name and the pick facts. Counts replace the loops. The compact default `limit` is 25. The full default stays 500.
- `provider::tools_in(provider, ToolSet::Core)` gives a core set of 25 workflow tools. `tools(provider)` is unchanged.
- The new code is in `mcp/compact.rs`. `job.rs`, `features.rs`, `pick.rs` and `tools.rs` get small hooks only.

Chat worker limits (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/budget.rs`):

- A tool reply to the model is cut at 12000 JSON characters, with a hint that names the compact modes. The tool card keeps the full text.
- A request carries at most one viewport image (the newest).
- A turn stops after 12 model rounds. The old `MAX_TURN_STEPS` moved to `budget::MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and now has a test.
- A request carries at most 6 earlier turns. When older turns are dropped, the latest `get_job` reply goes in front of the first kept prompt.
- A local endpoint gets the core tool set. A cloud endpoint gets the full table.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1944-ai-context-budgets.md`.

## Cause

Enhancement. The full tool table and one full `get_job` or `list_features` reply can fill the context window of a small local model.

## Tests

The results in this section apply to original head `398a4a937a6267dce87da97495149713412920a5`.
The final-head results are in "Latest review findings" below.

Pins (all new; network is not used):

- `crates/app/tests/mcp_compact.rs`: `get_job_summary_drops_the_machine_definition_and_default_fields`, `get_job_summary_refuses_a_non_boolean`, `list_operation_types_filters_by_kind_and_by_section`, `list_features_compact_rows_are_short_and_the_default_limit_is_chat_sized`, `the_core_tool_set_is_a_small_subset_of_the_full_table`. Each asserts a character budget.
- `egui_app::tests::ai_chat::budget`: `a_long_tool_reply_is_cut_to_the_character_cap_with_a_hint`, `a_local_model_gets_the_core_tool_set_and_a_cloud_model_the_full_table`, `a_turn_stops_at_the_round_cap`.
- `egui_app::ai_chat::budget::tests`: `a_cut_keeps_whole_characters_and_says_how_much_was_shown`, `a_small_reply_passes_and_a_long_one_is_one_capped_text_block`, `only_the_newest_image_goes_with_a_request`, `old_turns_are_dropped_and_the_latest_get_job_reply_is_kept`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pin red; code restored, pin green):

- `job.rs` from upstream: the two `get_job` pins and the `list_operation_types` pin are red.
- `features.rs` from upstream: the `list_features` pin is red.
- Core filter turned off in `provider.rs`: the core set pin is red.
- `worker_mcp.rs` from upstream: the reply cap pin is red.
- `turn.rs` from upstream: the image pin and the history pin are red.
- `tool_set_for` gives `Full` to local: the tool set pin is red.
- Loop runs `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS + 1`: the round cap pin is red.

Original-head gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed (131 steps, 0 failed). Original-head clippy passed. That head later conflicted with upstream main. The final-head results below replace these results.

title: feat(mcp): generate the agent tool reference and local prompt from the tool table
body:
## What changed

- A new module, `crates/app/src/mcp/catalog.rs`, reads the live MCP tool table. It makes:
  - the Markdown tool reference (`reference_markdown`),
  - the compact local-model prompt (`local_prompt`),
  - the shared working rules (`RULES`).
- `camcraft-cli mcp reference` prints the reference. `camcraft-cli mcp prompt` prints the local prompt. `camcraft-cli mcp --help` lists the two words.
- The local Prompt-JSON context (`provider::prompt_context`) now starts with `RULES`. The old format sentence follows it without a change.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is the generated reference: 116 tools, with their arguments and full descriptions.
- New thin wrappers, with no tool list of their own:
  - `.agents/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` for Codex CLI and Antigravity.
  - `GEMINI.md` for Gemini CLI.
  - Codex reads `AGENTS.md`, and its skill table already names `camcraft-mcp`. `AGENTS.md` does not change.
- `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` now names the 34 live tools that it did not name before. Examples: `edit_machine`, `suggest_cutting_data`, `delete_tool`, `edit_tool`, `pick_in_box`, `electrode_from_faces`, `set_units`, `set_program`. A new paragraph tells how to get the reference and the local prompt.
- `tools::all` is now `pub(super)`, so that the catalog reads the same rows as `tools/list`.
- `docs/decisions/1947-mcp-single-source.md` records the choices.

## Cause

The skill, the guide and the local prompt were written by hand. Nothing compared them with the tool table, so they drifted.

## Tests

The new file `crates/app/tests/mcp_doc_drift.rs` has six pins:

- `the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table`: the failure message gives the command that writes the reference again.
- `every_tool_named_in_the_agent_docs_is_live`: it scans the Claude skill, the `.agents` skill, `GEMINI.md` and the guide.
- `every_live_tool_is_in_the_guide_and_the_local_prompt`
- `the_local_prompt_json_context_carries_the_shared_rules`
- `the_scanner_finds_a_tool_call_and_a_table_name`: this proves that the scanner can find a dead name.
- `the_drift_suite_maps_the_tool_table_catalog_and_prompt_context`: the suite must name the tool table, catalog, provider and fallback in its Gate map.

Results on the code before the fix: the pins failed. The guide did not name 34 live tools, and the reference did not exist.

Mutation checks. Each mutation made a pin fail. Each restore made all five initial pins pass again.

- The guide from `upstream/main`: `every_live_tool_is_in_the_guide_and_the_local_prompt` failed.
- `fallback.rs` from `upstream/main`: `the_local_prompt_json_context_carries_the_shared_rules` failed.
- The `undo` row removed from the reference: `the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table` failed.

## Review fixes and final validation

Head: `26a09578688587d2c8849a66507e371369a98586`.
Base: `upstream/main` at `08697d3c422a2f6ade1f3e1fd9970b16ed3177eb`.

- Merged current main without conflicts. Generated the reference again. Only the `import_model` row changed.
- Added Gate maps for `app::mcp::tools`, `app::mcp::catalog`, `app::mcp::provider` and `app::mcp::fallback`.
- A temporary tool-only diff selected `mcp_doc_drift` in the real quick plan. Restored the temporary edit.
- Restored the stale reference: `the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table` failed. Restored the generated reference: passed.
- Removed the Gate map: `the_drift_suite_maps_the_tool_table_catalog_and_prompt_context` failed. Restored the map: passed.
- All six drift pins pass after the restores.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. 127 steps. 978 tests passed, nine ignored, none failed. Duration: 10.4 minutes.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: FAIL. 200 actual steps, one failed. Duration: 38.1 minutes.
- The sole unexpected failure was `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.
  At `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`, the Linux count expected `(4726, 4698, 549)` and received `(3158, 3130, 1141)`.
  This PR changes neither that test nor the machining algorithms. The test and algorithms remain unchanged.
- The heavy run also reported the expected failures for #2845 (two tests), #2849 (three tests) and #1950 (one test).

The heavy gate selected the app heavy targets. These targets ran tests:

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| `app heavy: adaptive_fig8_crossing` | PASS: 2 |
| `app heavy: adaptive_pinch` | PASS: 1 |
| `app heavy: carried_engine_agreement` | PASS: 1 |
| `app heavy: feature_pick_wire` | PASS: 1 |
| `app heavy: import_solidcraft` | PASS: 3 |

| `app heavy: rotary_field_parity` | PASS: 6 |

| `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm` | FAIL: one unexpected failure; one expected failure (#1950) |
| `app heavy: feature_edge_g1_join` | One expected failure (#2845) |
| `app heavy: winding_align` | One expected failure (#2845) |
| `app heavy: lead_approach` | Two expected failures (#2849) |

Other selected targets had no ignored tests to run. The run passed 40 tests and found one unexpected failure. Six tests had expected failures.

A separate run of the failed bore test failed again with the same counts (2.42 seconds).

- The heavy gate remains red. This PR remains a draft.
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS. Duration: 1 minute, 14 seconds.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Held: the Claude skill edit

This session could not write under `.claude/`. A write there needs an approval prompt. Thus, this PR does not change `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The issue has a comment with the exact patch and its pin:

- Remove the shipped `set_units`, `set_program` and face lay from "Known Remaining Gaps".
- Link the generated reference.
- Add the pin `the_known_gaps_name_no_shipped_tool`.

For this reason the PR says `Refs #1947`, not `Fixes`.

## Commits

The first two commits retain the original work history. The first commit was squashed onto a `main` that moved during the gate. Thus, it also reverted other merged work. The second commit restores the tree of `main` and keeps only the 11 files of this issue. Read the whole PR diff, not the first commit alone. Force-push is forbidden, so the history stays as it is. A merge commit keeps the tree of the PR head, which is correct.

None of these PRs changes the same lines:

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...814dca499f9f9793f3c9e6bcd3eafab5f32e2022).

## Author gate status

The guarded source at cfc281268 passed the complete reached heavy gate, 247/247 steps in 58.1 minutes on macOS arm64. It includes the separate default-machine correction merged upstream in #3092. The mixed-condition regression passed in the 19-test Agie writer module. Both input orders received the exact error and no files.

On the corrected production source 766fc7109, the regular CLI exported all 20 synthetic jobs. Their 32 works and 72 native files matched the previous guarded outputs byte for byte. All 20 controller-review receipts matched. All 20 repeat attempts refused to replace an existing job and preserved every byte. This corpus is a software comparison. The real control checks below cover the stated representative jobs.

The full quick gate on 766fc7109 found the missing dedicated test suite for the built-in Agie CPS dispatcher. The next commit added the suite and its 11 expected refusal records. Passing each record requires the direct single-file post to fail with the native-job diagnostic and leave no NC file.

The final head is 814dca499. It changes only tests above cfc281268. On a real plasma stream and 1300PL machine, the Agie single-file dispatcher must fail with its specific native-directory diagnostic. The workspace must exclude the post from the plasma registry. The single-file smoothing test now uses the workspace's native-post predicate. With smoothing enabled, a mounted Agie punch must refuse the setup and create no job directory. The other posts retain their previous checks.

All 49 targeted tests passed on the final head: seven plasma, seven smoothing, 12 native app, 11 native dispatcher and 12 recorded-stream tests.

The original full quick on cfc281268 ran 1,013 steps in 80.6 minutes. All but the two cross-post tests passed, including strict Clippy. On 814dca499 the official failed-step replay selected both suites and passed both in 0.8 minutes. Each suite ran seven tests. The complete 247-step heavy result belongs to cfc281268. The whole quick and heavy gates have not been repeated on 814dca499.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6 --failed gate-logs/quick-20261121-023002
```

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Integration order

The maintainer requests a separate P1 change from main and a safety-tier review of each feature PR. The standalone zero-step encoder is #3104. The first workspace writer in #2951 uses it. Keep earlier feature drafts that still generate erosion steps on hold until each takes its own safety correction and review. The standalone machine template in #2948 has no writer.

## Gate commands and pinning tests

The earlier macOS bore fixture and missing operation name were reproduced on ba5ff0ae1 with these commands:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 1d81b609c --only 'app suites: default_machine_missing'
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 1d81b609c --only 'app heavy: pocket3d_hsm'
```

The scoped CLI and native writer checks include:

- `native_punch_links_its_three_files_and_uses_the_uncompensated_contour`
- `every_punch_has_its_own_geometry_and_uses_the_requested_piece_quality`
- `nine_model_owners_resolve_all_resources_and_the_same_registered_quality`
- `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero`
- `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality`

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. Later changes clarify the repeat-import result and pin the refusal for mixed wire conditions.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. The two UI screenshots were checked locally. Public screenshot attachment is pending.

Effort: high
Changelog: Agie native jobs import with zero machining steps. Review each work's effective native quality and offsets before assigning its technology in Agie Control.

Fixes #2984
