title: feat(ui): draw the viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA
body: ## What changed The viewport overlay drew as `wgpu` lines. A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths, height planes, outlines, triads and the ground grid now draw as wide anti-aliased lines. The viewport also has MSAA. - **Wide lines** (`crates/ui/src/viewport/wide.rs`): - Each segment is one 32-byte instance: two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours. The grid fades along a line, thus each end keeps its own colour. - The vertex shader makes a quad that faces the screen. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over 1 px. - The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed. - **Clean corners.** Each end reaches half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet close the corner and do not overlap past it. - **Depth lift.** Each vertex moves toward the eye by 3 line widths (`LIFT_WIDTHS`). The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. - The lift prevents this: without it, the depth test hid half of a line that lies on a face. - Effect: a line behind a face by less than 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen. - **Near plane.** The shader clips a segment to the near plane before it calculates the screen direction. Thus an end behind the eye does not turn the quad over. - **Line width setting.** The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt. The default is 1.5 pt. The value is multiplied by the display's pixels per point, and the result is held to 1..16 px. - **Anti-aliasing setting.** The choices are Off, 2x and 4x. The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. - A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets one time. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound. - The traced stock writes one depth for each pixel. Thus its own edges are not smoothed, and its cost does not change. - **Sample counts that the device offers.** - Bring-up requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it. The shell then reads the adapter's counts for the colour and depth formats. - Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts 1 and 4 are offered. The browser build offers 1 and 4. - A row for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A queued pick of such a count is refused by name. - A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so one time. - **Where the settings are.** - They are in the viewport's Display menu (#2818), in its Graphics group, after the projection: "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing". The first version put them in the Theme door; a manual test found that place wrong (they are not part of a theme), so they moved when #2818 reached `main`. A general Settings window is proposed in #3025. - Like the other Display menu entries, a pick calls its `State` method directly (`select_line_width`, `select_antialias`). No command is queued. - They are kept in the per-user `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. A file word that the build does not know reads as the default and does not refuse the file. - They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme. - The origin-name switch now writes all the view settings, so it does not reset the line settings. - **File size.** The pipelines and the render targets moved to `viewport/pipes.rs` and are built through one helper. `viewport.rs` went from 1543 to 1265 lines. - **Docs.** - The guide has a short section "Line width and anti-aliasing" (`first-run.md`). - The decision record is `docs/decisions/2958-wide-overlay-lines.md`. ## Screenshots Before and after: 1 px lines without anti-aliasing (`main`), and 1.5 pt lines with 4x anti-aliasing (this PR, the defaults). The Display menu with the new "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing" entries in its Graphics group (2x is not offered on this device): The line widths: 1 pt with anti-aliasing Off, 1.5 pt with 4x (the default), and 3 pt with 4x: ## Readings Frame time: a 2560×1440 target, a release build and DX12, the median of 35 frames (submit and wait). The scene is one plate and a raster path at the overlay limit (512k segments), or a typical path (20k segments). "Before" is `main` at acd5b02d3 (1 px lines, no MSAA). "After" is 1.5 px wide lines. | GPU | Path | Before (1 px) | After, Off | After, 2x | After, 4x | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 20k segments | 0.17 ms | 0.20 ms | 0.26 ms | 0.29 ms | | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 512k segments | 0.27 ms | 0.70 ms | 0.72 ms | 0.78 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 20k segments | 1.00 ms | 1.33 ms | 3.38 ms | 3.64 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 512k segments | 1.77 ms | 6.92 ms | 8.76 ms | 9.09 ms | On the integrated GPU, the cost is clear: - 4x adds approximately 2.3 ms to a typical frame at 1440p. - At the overlay limit, the frame is 9 ms. This is near the 10 ms frame target. The default 4x follows the issue. If the maintainer prefers the lower cost on integrated graphics, the default can change to 2x or Off. This is a one-word change (`Antialias::default`). - Upload (`set_overlay`) of 512k segments: 9.6 ms (NVIDIA) and 8.8 ms (AMD), against 7.1 ms and 7.0 ms before. The upload occurs only when the scene changes, not when the camera moves. - Overlay buffer at the limit: 16 MiB (32 bytes for each segment). Before, it was 24 MiB (two 24-byte vertices). - Without the lift, the pinning test counts 292 px of a 6 px line on a face against 628 px in the air. With the lift, the two counts are the same. ## Pinning tests - `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render/wide_lines.rs` (in the `gpu_render` binary): - `a_line_on_a_face_keeps_its_full_width`: fails without the lift (292 vs 628 px). - `two_lines_that_meet_close_the_corner_and_do_not_reach_past_it`. - `the_line_width_setting_widens_the_band`. - `msaa_smooths_the_edges_that_one_sample_leaves_hard`. - `crates/ui/tests/trace_composite.rs`: `the_traced_stock_paints_the_same_with_msaa`. The 4x pass with the composite has no validation error. - `crates/ui/src/viewport/wide_tests.rs`: - `each_segment_is_one_32_byte_instance` - `an_odd_vertex_and_bad_colours_never_reach_the_gpu_as_garbage` - `the_line_width_scales_with_the_display_and_stays_in_range` - `an_unoffered_sample_count_falls_back_to_the_highest_offered_below_it` - `the_shader_lifts_by_the_documented_widths` - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/display_quality.rs`: - `the_defaults_are_one_and_a_half_points_and_four_samples` - `a_line_width_pick_is_kept_survives_a_restart_and_undo_leaves_it` - `an_offered_antialias_pick_is_kept_and_an_unoffered_one_is_disabled` - `the_graphics_group_offers_the_line_widths_and_the_antialiasing` - `a_pick_of_an_unoffered_count_is_refused_by_name_and_not_kept` - `crates/app/tests/view_file.rs`: `the_line_width_and_the_antialias_round_trip`. ## Gates - `main` was merged into the branch (b78bef768). The conflicts were with #2818 (display modes): `viewport.rs` keeps the hidden-edge stage and the `draw_list::plan` loop of `main`, with its pipelines from `viewport/pipes.rs`. `app/view.rs` and `state_view.rs` keep the fields of both sides. - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on bdea342b6: 22 steps, 0 failed (2.3 min). - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on the final head bdea342b6: the change in `app::view` reaches all the `app` heavy lanes. 199 steps ran in 29.2 min, and 198 are green. title: feat(wire): post a native Agie Classic Cut 2S job
body:
**This first writer now uses the zero-step encoder from #3104. Keep it in draft for the required safety-tier review.** Later feature drafts still need their own safety review before they can introduce machining behavior. A stale controller quality can change the effective finish, pass count and offsets.

This change builds on the machine template in #2948 and the standalone encoder in #3104. These branches are in a fork, so this PR targets upstream main. Review [the first-writer safety adoption above its integration parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/1ea87ebac0204f3613c3d2549692b4108f620f66...025ed4760e592c3401859a66285457021a98341b).

## Change

The desktop Post command and cam.post write a native Agie job directory with linked ISO, SBR and SBL files. CamCraft writes the nominal contour in Rust. The setup requests a resident quality and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. The post validates the work before it creates the destination. It publishes all three files together and preserves an existing directory.

The supported case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. Select the Classic 2S template from #2948. Enter the AGIE_QN2 condition for Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and cold die steel. Select the 1.0 mm separation cut explicitly. The template starts without an installed condition. A cut needs 0.4 mm clearance at each stock face and 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Other contours, tapers, skims, custom X/Y travel limits and additional workpieces are refused.

## Reference material for review

The contributor's team wrote [Agie-CAM at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42) and released it under the MIT license. This draft retains the license and copyright notice. The implementation reference documents observed controller examples for parts of the JEScript sequence and the resident technology selection. The published guides linked on #2945 give the file roles and some interface arguments. They do not document the full sequence and all defaults. Please review that source against the project rules before merge.

The controller supplies its own runtime and technology table. This PR includes the writer and original synthetic examples and expected output. It includes no controller image, vendor post, runtime library or technology database.

## Control verification

On the corrected writer, the normal CLI produced the same three CCSEP20 files as the independently verified import in #3104. Only the output stem was changed from the PUNCH40 example. The copy of the actual control showed the closed punch at zero steps. FORMALCHECK blocked it until the operator assigns technology. See [the file hashes and native work details](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3104#issuecomment-7055077111). The native bytes were tested once in that replay. No physical cut was made.

On successive imports, select the newly created piece. Match its ISO, start hole and zero steps to the intended setup. Verify the effective wire, height, quality and offsets before assigning TECCUT. Run the control's graphic and formal checks on the resulting steps.

On the earlier writer, the control plotted a rough pass and three trims after automatic generation. The measured offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm. That historical result does not qualify an automatic release on this or another installation.

The synthetic example runs from the repository root:
```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
```
Use a new PUNCH40 destination.

## Final head checks

At a08c802b6, all five writer tests, four standalone encoder tests and ten application integration tests passed. The normal PUNCH40 script reproduced the previous guarded ISO, SBR and SBL. A repeat export refused to replace them. Both PUNCH40 and the CCSEP20 variant returned `working_steps_generated=false` and the controller review.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib agie::tests::
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test agie_native
```

Pinning tests include `script_post_reports_the_required_control_review_and_zero_working_steps`, `stock_origin_and_fractional_setup_coordinates_are_refused_before_publication`, `the_native_files_match_the_control_checked_rectangular_punch` and `qn2_requires_the_rough_wire_size_in_the_mounted_condition`.

The earlier guarded head was 5bdbb5fe4. It includes the upstream diagnostic fix from #3092 and a dedicated recorded-stream suite for the Agie dispatcher. The single-file post entry point must refuse the Agie dispatcher. Each of 11 input streams checks the diagnostic, the failure exit code and the absence of NC output. The suite inventory also requires this post to have its own tests.

On 5bdbb5fe4 the recorded suite passed 12/12 tests. The dispatcher suite passed 11/11. All nine default-machine regression tests and all 19 native tests passed. The normal CLI and an independent Rust caller reproduced the checked setup files and the matching ISO. Both duplicate exports preserved all files. Against upstream 211105042, the full plan selects 1,017 quick steps and 251 reached heavy steps. These two full gates did not run on that head.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test default_machine_missing
```

The final head 025ed4760 adds cross-post tests. The plasma suite now runs the direct Agie dispatcher and requires its native-directory refusal. The single-file smoothing test uses the same native-post predicate as the workspace. A mounted, otherwise valid Agie punch with smoothing enabled must report the setup-option error and create no directory. The existing native test checks all three default-option files against their expected bytes.

All 48 targeted checks passed on 025ed4760: seven plasma tests, seven smoothing tests, 11 native app tests, 11 dispatcher tests and 12 common recorded-stream tests. No full quick or reached-heavy result is claimed on this revision.

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

The compiled desktop picker and receipt were checked locally on the safety-adoption source a08c802b6. The picker identifies Ra as requested. The receipt shows the ISO, threading-hole and working-step checks, the TECCUT assignment and the required offsets. Updated screenshots remain local for review.

## Earlier desktop Post dialog

These pictures show the earlier writer. The corrected picker labels Ra as requested. The corrected receipt reports zero working steps and the required check of effective quality.

| Before (Generic ISO) | After (native Agie) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic ISO Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/625ef345a047980ab6974df99ea8ca2ac5f783b2/before.png) | ![Native Agie Post dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/625ef345a047980ab6974df99ea8ca2ac5f783b2/after.png) |

Effort: high
Changelog: The Wire EDM desktop and script workflows can post a supported Classic Cut 2S punch as a native zero-step Agie setup directory for control review.

Fixes #2945

title: feat(machine): add the AGIECUT Classic 2S wire EDM template
body:
Stacked on #3092 for the default-machine diagnostic. Review [the template changes above that head](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/d0fe169a159a14dc5a5973a6c9af332ad70a6cc1...f2cc7ac5010e305b0ca73bbb8cf25938137f96c4).

## Change

Add the AGIECUT Classic 2S wire EDM machine template to the desktop and embedded machine libraries. Mounting the template preserves the selected post.

The template states the X/Y rapid speed of 900 mm/min, the Z/U/V rapid speed of 600 mm/min and U/V travel of ±70 mm. It lists the four standard wire sizes from 0.20 to 0.33 mm. The X/Y/Z stroke lengths appear in the description. The operator supplies the installed datum, guide planes and cutting conditions. The handbook qualifies its maximum taper angle by guide type and work height.

The native job post is separate work in #2945. This change does not select an Agie dialect.

## Source

[AGIE, AGIECUT Classic technical handbook, edition 06.2002 C2.1](https://static.gindumac.com/products/9ccc9b7e-b589-49db-9843-eff1da09434c/documents/ES-EDM-AGI-2002-00001.pdf). Section 1.1 on printed page 4 identifies the model group, travels and speeds. Section 5.2 on printed page 44 lists the wire sizes.

## Verification

Independent checks used head 08601a2bc. All 68 tests in machine, machine_library, mcp_wire_contour and posting passed. Clippy passed on all camcraft-app targets with warnings denied.

The pinning tests are:
- agiecut_classic_2s_exposes_the_sourced_axes_and_wire_sizes
- agiecut_template_refuses_a_wire_job_without_an_installed_condition
- every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration

The normal command script selected the exact library name and mounted AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S. An attempted wire job with C110 failed with a missing-condition diagnostic. It created no NC file. Physical travel and cutting were not tested.

On the refreshed head f2cc7ac50, the full quick gate passed all 256 steps in 36.0 minutes. The verifier rebuilt it in its own target directory on macOS arm64. The axis-direction, default-machine and process-folder suites passed all 23 targeted tests. The complete reached heavy gate passed all 196 steps in 58.4 minutes. Both debug and release executables resolved the template from this checkout. Verification used `cargo xtask gate quick --base 1d81b609c` and `cargo xtask gate heavy --base 1d81b609c`.

The former head had two inherited failures: its per-operation refusal named only the setup, and its optimized bore fixture used different platform counts. The refreshed head includes the upstream Apple silicon fixture and the default-machine correction in #3092.

The standalone Generic ISO wire post also reported missing machine codes on a committed contour stream. The machine template supplies machine data. The operator still needs a suitable post and an installed cutting condition.

Effort: medium
Changelog: The machine library includes an AGIECUT Classic 2S wire EDM template with the manufacturer's stated axes, rapid speeds and standard wire sizes.

Fixes #2946

body: ## What changed - **Home button.** The top band has a **Home** button, left of **Donate**. The glyph is the Tabler `home` outline (MIT). A click shows the start page. A second click hides it. - **Start page.** The page stands in for the dock in the central area. The ribbon and the status strip stay. The page shows: - **Recent projects**: the #662 list from the user settings file, newest first. A file that is not there any more is greyed, reads "(missing)" and takes no click. Its hover gives the refusal text. - Each row shows the path in a faint ink. The page removes the Windows verbatim prefix (`\?\`) from the path that it shows (`home::shown_path`). - **Open project…**, **New project** and **Back to the project**, through the form seam's `action_bar`. - **Open.** A click on a project queues `OpenRecent`, the same command as the ribbon's Open list. The unsaved-changes prompt and the refusals are Open's own. - **Close.** The page keeps the `doc_version` that it opened over (`State::home_page`). It closes when the document changes: an open, New, an import or a command. A refused open or a cancelled prompt does not change the document, so the page stays. - **Start.** The native window shows the page when the command line names no file (`home::at_start`). A fresh `State` has no page, so the harnesses, the snapshots and the browser build start as before. - **Version.** The version label was already the rightmost toolbar item (#556). It stays there. A test pins it at the right of the top bar. - **No command, no MCP tool.** The page and the button are view state. It also takes `act-report.png`: #1696 added that icon to the app but not to the site, so `test_guide_icons` was red on main. - **Guide.** `getting-started/first-run.md` has a "The start page" section. - Decision record: `docs/decisions/2384-home-start-page.md`. ## Screenshots Headless render, dark theme, the seeded document, three recent projects (one missing). title: feat(2d)!: Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains
body: Stacked on #2716 (merge #2716 first) This branch starts at the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). The diff against `main` shows the changes of #2716 too, until #2716 merges. The changes of this PR are the one commit `feat(2d): Slot and Trochoidal Slot read DXF sketch chains`. ## What changed - A `Slot` and a `Trochoidal Slot` now take one picked chain of a DXF profile (`FeatureSel::SketchChain` or a `SketchLayer` that holds one chain). - One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`. - One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The typed `width` stays. - The pick seeds in its own command (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick and the seed. This is the law of #1504. - Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain. A slot that left its outline is refused by name. A slot whose ends are not the ends of its centerline is refused by name. - The verification and the stock simulation use the setup stock (`part_solid = false`), as #2716 does for the 2D Contour. - Slot parameters keep their two-point form. This branch writes project v74 for sketch selections and per-chain overrides. A v73 file steps up and keeps its protection. Older readers refuse v74 files. These picks are refused by name: - a closed chain that is not a slot outline (a rectangle, a circle): "is not a slot outline"; - an open chain that is not straight: "the picked centerline is not straight"; - more than one chain: "a slot on a DXF profile cuts one chain, and this selection has 2 chains"; - the whole profile as the source: "needs one picked chain"; - a channel narrower than the tool. The `Slot` refusal now gives the slot width and the tool diameter. Files: - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_line.rs` (new): `SlotBound::from_centerline`, `SlotBound::centerline` and the ends law. - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room.rs`: the `Room::Line` kind in each match of the room law. - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs`: the numbers in the "slot is narrower than the tool" refusal. - `crates/app/src/operation/slot_sketch.rs` (new): resolves the picked chain to a slot room, and holds the outline test. - `crates/app/src/operation/slot_pick.rs`: `slot_bound_of` reads sketch picks; `slot_from_picks` and `confine_slot` include the `Trochoidal Slot` on sketch picks; `slot_fit_of` describes a centerline. - `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`: the job reads the slot room for a `Trochoidal Slot` on sketch picks, and its region is the authored stadium. - `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the `Trochoidal Slot` arm judges the slot against the slot room. - `crates/app/src/operation/material_region.rs`: the preview does not read sketch slot picks as a region. - `crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch_pick.rs`: `visit_src_chains` and `transform_chain_pts` are `pub(super)`. - `crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`: the profile law admits picked chains for the two slot kinds. - `docs/decisions/1868-slot-dxf-sketches.md`: the decision. ## Cause `sketch_model::source_problem` refused picked chains of a profile for each kind but the 2D Contour. `slot_bound_of` refused sketch picks. The slot room had no centerline kind. ## Tests Pins, in `crates/app/tests/slot_dxf_sketch.rs`: - `a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` - `a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline` - `an_open_straight_chain_is_the_centerline_at_the_typed_width` - `picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name` Pins, in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_room_pins.rs`: - `a_centerline_room_holds_its_two_ends_and_refuses_other_ends` - `a_bent_short_or_doubled_centerline_is_refused_by_name` The four app pins were red on the unchanged code. Each failed with "picked chains of a profile are not supported yet". Readings from the outline pin (4 mm tool, 10 mm outline, centres (45, 25) and (75, 25)): - seeded ends (45.000, 25.000) and (75.000, 25.000), width 10.000 mm; - cutter centre X 42.000 to 78.000 and Y 22.000 to 28.000; - stock simulation: 0 gouge cells. Mutation results. Each mutation removes one guard. Each made a pin red. The restored code is green. | Mutation | Result | |---|---| | M1 outline area test off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M2 one-chain rule off | red (same pin) | | M3 centerline straightness test off | red (same pin) | | M4 centerline ends law off | red (`an_open_straight_chain_is_the_centerline_at_the_typed_width`) | | M5 slot room judge off in the `Trochoidal Slot` arm | red (`a_trochoidal_slot_reads_the_same_outline`) | | M6 whole-profile refusal off | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M7 old profile law back | red (all four app pins) | | M8 old "narrower than the tool" text back | red (`picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`) | | M9 doubled-back centerline test off | red (`a_bent_short_or_doubled_centerline_is_refused_by_name`) | | M10 sketch read off in `slot_bound_of` | red (all four app pins) | Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-2716` on head `bd24b9328`, where `base-2716` is the head of #2716 (`2e77ca0ee`). Git for Windows checks out text files with CRLF (`\r\n`) by default when `core.autocrlf=true`.

- STEP, STL, and OBJ model fixtures (`testdata/**/*.step`, `testdata/**/*.stp`, `testdata/**/*.stl`, `testdata/**/*.obj`)
- Skill, agent, and GitHub workflow definitions (`.claude/**`, `.github/**`)

title: fix(motion): turning rides keep no sample closer than half the chord share
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`: a new private step `thin` runs after the bisection in `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in`.
- `thin` drops each sample that is closer than half the chord share (`MIN_GAP_SHARE = 0.5`) to the last kept sample.
- The first and the last sample (the window ends) always stay. At the end, a kept sample that is too near the last sample gives way to it.
- Each kept sample is an exact point of the offset curve. No new point is made.
- A chord moves by at most two gaps (one share). The callers pass a quarter of the user tolerance as the share, so the ride stays within half of the user tolerance.
- The module doc now states this bound.

## Cause

The bisection (`settle`) halves the interval toward a vertical tangent of the offset curve. The samples come closer than 1 micrometre. Exact float twins of candidate stations also occur (a gap of 1e-16 mm). `out.dedup()` removes only exactly equal samples. The lathe posts wrote these runs as identical `G01` blocks.

## Tests

New file `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_spacing.rs`:

- `od_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped bar and the collar, tol 1e-2, 2.5e-3 and 1e-4.
- `id_ride_has_no_move_shorter_than_half_the_share`: the stepped hole wall.
- `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap`: the window ends 1e-7 past a candidate station. This pins the give-way at the end.
- `thinning_keeps_the_window_ends_and_the_nose`: the ends stay, and each sample is at distance d from the profile.
- `thinned_chords_stay_within_the_bound`: 9 points on each chord stand at least `d - 2 * tol` from the profile.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged `offset.rs` the OD and ID spacing pins fail with `gap 0.00000000000000044` (OD) and `gap 0.00000000000000011` (ID).

Mutations:

- The old `offset.rs`: 2 pins red. Restored: green.
- The tail give-way disabled (`while ... && false`): `a_window_end_next_to_a_candidate_keeps_the_gap` red (`gap 0.0000001`). Restored: green.

Latest review fix (final head `a8dc06bd903d41af16461ebb15e7827a747f3b4a`):

- The branch merges `upstream/main` at `fc32feb0e`. The merge is clean.
- This includes the reviewed fix for #3050, PR #3078 (merge `eefee2453e`).
- The Linux bore count pin is `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. The verification checks stay in place.
- `cargo xtask catalog --case turning/contour-finishes` rebuilds the project and the NC file.
- Both catalog regeneration paths pin the refreshed NC bytes.
- Artifact review: the NC file goes from 620 to 246 lines. The diff removes 388 lines and adds 14 lines.
  - 374 short `G01` blocks are removed.
  - 13 `G00` blocks and one `G01` retract change X from `20.762` to `20.76`, or from `22.884` to `22.88`.
  - The other command types and feed rates stay the same.
  - The project changes two operation stamps and two cached move lists (60 to 16, and 536 to 206).
  - The parameters, model, machine, and setup stay the same.
- Catalog mutation: with the old NC file, both `catalog_turning_contour_finishes::regenerates` and `catalog_turning_contour_finishes::rebuilds` fail. With the refreshed NC file, both pass.
- Bore pin mutation: with the old Linux helper counts, `the_linux_x86_64_bore_count_pin_is_exact` fails. With the current helper restored, it passes.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 33 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 655 steps, 0 failed, 37.4 min.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: green, 234 steps, 0 failed, 41.3 min. All reached lanes ran, with no omissions.
  - The 234 steps include one release build and 233 test lanes. All gate steps are green.
  - Motion heavy lanes: 37 lanes; 57 ordinary tests pass. Two known-fail lanes for #1950 are red as expected.
  - App heavy lanes: 196 lanes; 43 ordinary tests pass. Four known-fail lanes are red as expected: one for #1950 and three for #2849.
  - `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm` passes, including `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green, exit 0, 38.1 s (`--all-targets -- -D warnings`).

## Catalog example

`examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread` came to main after this branch was made. The branch merges main and rebuilds the case with `cargo xtask catalog --case turning/cone-thread`.

- `cone-thread.nc`: 1197 lines to 732 lines. 465 `G01` lines are removed and 0 lines are added. The runs of same-X `G01` blocks go from 509 to 82.
- `cone-thread.camproj`: rebuilt with the new ride samples.
- `README.md`: the limit line for #2882 (repeated blocks) is removed. The taper blocks and the thread blocks that the README names stay the same.
- Mutation: with the old `.nc` back, `catalog_turning_cone_thread::regenerates` and `catalog_turning_cone_thread::rebuilds` are red. With the new `.nc`, they are green.

## Goldens moved

4 files. Each diff only removes lines (516 removed, 0 added):

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/profile_rough_finish.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_mm.nc` (-129)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/turning_inch.nc` (-129)

Most removed lines are runs of identical blocks, for example 40 x `G01 X7. Z2. F0.04` and 39 x `G01 X9.1 Z3.05 F0.05`. The other removed lines are sub-gap steps at the start of the same face, for example `Z2.001` to `Z2.005`. The goldens were made again with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`.

## Not exercised

- At a very small user tolerance (for example 0.001 mm) the gap is less than the posted resolution. Two rounded blocks can then still be equal. This costs no position.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `offset.rs` or the new test file.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/2882-ride-min-spacing.md`. The post-side alternative (drop a repeated block in each lathe post) was dropped.

Written by an Opus lead + Haiku workers (lane trial). The workers wrote about 85% of the lines: `thin` and its call sites, the first four pins, and the decision record. The lead wrote about 15%: the chord-bound correction (1.5x to 2x share, because the give-way at the end can double the gap), the tail pin, the clippy fix, the golden refresh and the review.

Effort: high

Changelog: Turning profile rides no longer post runs of identical G01 blocks: samples closer than half the chord share are dropped.

Fixes #2882

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |

title: fix(motion): the corner check reads a cusp loop that crosses itself
body:
## What changed

- `connected_pieces` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` reads each outer loop with `Region::from_slices`. Before, it used `Region::new`.
- A loop that crosses itself is now read as its even-odd lobes. The check does not stop.
- The noise filters of the check are the same (`PIECE_AREA_MIN`, `SLIVER_HALF_WIDTH`, `CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`).
- `docs/decisions/2849-corner-cusp-loop.md` records the decision.

This PR is partial work for #2849. It fixes the defect that the issue names ("loop crosses itself" in the corner check). It does not change the three toolpath tests of the issue.

## Cause

- `unreached_corners` computes `leftover = piece.difference(&swept)`. Then it calls `connected_pieces(&leftover)`.
- A bore drawn as chords leaves a cusp a few microns wide at each chord vertex.
- On the micron lattice, the boolean can return such a cusp as one loop that crosses itself.
- `Region::new` refuses that loop. The error stopped the whole corner check.
- The user then saw only the note "the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself)".
- The defect does not need the solidcore importer. It is on `main` for a synthetic bore.

## Tests

Pin: `machining2d::unreached::law::a_chord_cusp_that_crosses_itself_does_not_stop_the_corner_check` (`camcraft-motion`, lib).

- The pin builds a 25 mm bore with 50, 60 and 63 chords. The reach is 2, 3 and 4 mm.
- It asserts that the check runs, names no corner and gives no note.
- On unchanged `upstream/main` (`326c938b1`) the pin fails: `50 chords, reach 2: invalid geometry: loop crosses itself`.
- Mutation: with `Region::new` put back, the pin is red. With `Region::from_slices`, the pin is green.

A probe sweep (not committed) used 24 to 400 chords, 9 reach values and 4 phases.

- Before the fix, 4726 of 13572 cases stopped with the error.
- After the fix, no case stops.
- After the fix, 36 cases name corners. Each has 24 to 28 chords and a reach of 8 or 10 mm. Their chord corners are larger than `CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on the final code.

- `motion lib`: ok.
- `app:adaptive_zero_margin_island`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main` shows one source file and one decision file.

## Not exercised

- The three tests of the issue with the solidcore mesh. PR B of #917 is not pushed, so the mesh is not available. The owner's diagnosis on the issue says that this fix does not change them.
- `Milling-test.step` through the solidcore reader. The pin uses a synthetic bore, not the real outline.
- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`). They did not run. They must run before this PR is flagged ready.
- A note that changes for a real project. A pocket that showed "did not run" can now show a corner note, or no note.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs`.

PR B of #917 marks the three tests with `known-fail #2849`. This PR does not close the issue, so those markers stay valid.

Changelog: The 2D pocket corner check no longer stops with "loop crosses itself" on a bore whose outline has fine chords.

Effort: high

Refs #2849

title: fix(geometry): order sheet cuts before material release
body:
Stacked on #2808 (merge #2808 first)

## What changed

Add `camcraft_geometry::nesting::cut_order` for one placed sheet.
Build a global containment forest for closed loops and open chains.
Resolve closed `Auto` sides by depth parity and open `Auto` sides to `OnLine`.
Traverse the forest iteratively. Sort siblings by enclosed area, then stable ID.
Schedule marking, internal, rough profile, and final breakthrough phases.
Use an explicit `release_phase` to distinguish blind pockets from through cuts.
Refuse invalid geometry, side requests, incomplete schedules, and cuts after material release.
Report circular-tool corner limits without changing the picked geometry.

## Cause

The geometry crate lacked one cut order across a nested sheet.
An enclosing hole can free a smaller part before that part's cuts finish.
Independent operation orders cannot enforce that sheet relationship.

## Tests

The initial pinning build failed on unchanged upstream base `f3b0e1955` with `E0432` because the planner API was absent.
The tested stacked base is parent commit `1947b6b6c30d214baf3db2072f95ed51ccb2dae3` from #2808.

All 17 pins pass:

- `sheet_tree_cuts_parts_in_holes_before_release_and_small_siblings_first`
- `sheet_pass_phases_keep_marking_first_and_breakthrough_last`
- `sheet_refuses_a_phase_that_frees_a_hole_before_its_nested_part`
- `sheet_order_validator_refuses_released_ancestors_missing_and_extra_passes`
- `sheet_order_validator_checks_global_phases_but_accepts_safe_sibling_orders`
- `sheet_order_validator_names_unrequested_and_duplicate_open_passes`
- `sheet_refuses_a_later_pass_after_the_same_contour_releases`
- `sheet_blind_pocket_pass_keeps_material_until_final_breakthrough`
- `sheet_refuses_invalid_release_phase_requests`
- `sheet_open_chain_sides_resolve_and_invalid_sides_name_the_chain`
- `sheet_refuses_invalid_width_ids_and_pass_requests`
- `sheet_refuses_degenerate_self_crossing_and_retraced_geometry`
- `sheet_refuses_area_accumulation_overflow_by_name`
- `sheet_refuses_crossing_or_touching_contours_and_boundary_crossing_chains`
- `sheet_crossing_open_features_keep_the_same_containing_parent`
- `sheet_corner_limits_use_tool_radius_and_ignore_input_winding`
- `sheet_open_side_corner_limits_follow_the_directed_cut_side`

Each of 21 runtime guard mutations failed its pins. Each restored version passed again.
The mutations covered:

- Width, duplicate IDs, pass requests, release requests, mandatory breakthrough release, and open/closed side requests.
- Minimum vertices, finite coordinates, coordinate bounds, zero-length segments, open closure, retracing, self-crossing, boundary crossing, and area overflow.
- Unknown cuts, extra or duplicate passes, global phase order, released material, and missing passes.

The area mutation used wrapping addition. Only the new overflow pin failed; the other 16 pins passed.
The spiral fixture checks positive and negative overflow in a valid 642-vertex loop.
Copying the upstream nesting entry back failed with `E0432`. Restoring the stacked entry passed all 17 pins.
The four planner/test files stayed byte-identical when the branch moved onto #2808.
The stacked branch passed the focused pins and the upstream-entry mutation again.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test nesting_cut_order`: 17 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: batch fallback, 937 steps, zero failures.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

## Goldens moved

None in the #2159 commit. It changes no `.nc` or `.cl` files.
The direct comparison with newer upstream also shows eight upstream-only Explain fixtures added by #2793:
`carvera.nc`, `grblhal.nc`, `sinker-iso.nc`, `sinumerik.nc`, `tinyg.nc`, `tormach-lathe.nc`, `tormach-plasma.nc`, and `wire-iso.nc`.
These are under `crates/post/tests/golden/explain/`. The child patch does not change or delete them.

## Not exercised

The tests did not cover placement-to-planner adapters, posted output from this planner, or physical machine execution.
I did not run release-only heavy lanes or pixel snapshots.
I did not trial-merge later parent changes after `1947b6b6c` or newer main commits into this branch.

## Overlaps

#2808 rewrites `crates/geometry/src/nesting.rs`, including its header and module declarations.
This branch starts at parent commit `1947b6b6c`.
The #2159 change in that file adds the `cut_order` export beside the placement API.
Merge #2808 first. Refresh this child after the parent merges.

Effort: max; no escalation.

Changelog: Add deterministic sheet cut order with material release checks, cut-side resolution, and cutter corner diagnostics.

Fixes #2159

title: feat(motion): equal depth steps as an opt-in ladder parameter
body:
## What changed

- The default depth ladder does not change. It keeps the remainder in the last step. `top 20, bottom 2, stepdown 5` cuts `[15, 10, 5, 2]`.
- A new operation parameter, `equal_steps`, is in the `links.approach` object. The default is off.
- With `equal_steps` on, the ladder cuts the same number of levels in equal steps. The same example cuts `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- `camcraft_motion::machining2d::equal_stepdown` gives the stepdown of the equal ladder. The level law `cut_levels_under` walks it. There is still one level law.
- `cut_levels_for(top, &approach, bottom, stepdown)` reads the mode and the stock top from the approach. These ladders call it: 2D Pocket (rings, adaptive, HSM, trochoidal, avoid), 2D Adaptive rest, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular (and its vault rings), 3D Pocket (plain, shell, rest refine).
- With stock above Top Z (#2004), the level at Top Z stays. The steps below it are equal.
- The project file writes `equal_steps` only when it is on. Older files load without a change.
- The params digest takes one byte only when the mode is on. The stamp of each existing operation does not change.
- The pocket region law of the app (`operation::area::ladder_planes`) reads the same mode through `OpParams::ladder_stepdown`. The region is built at the planes that the generator cuts.
- The Lead in / Lead out tab has one new row, "Equal depth steps", in the Linking group.
- `docs/decisions/2012-equal-steps.md` records the decision.

The parameter is undoable through `EditOperationParams`. The MCP `edit_operation` patch reaches it as `params.links.approach.equal_steps`. No new command and no new MCP tool are necessary.

## Cause

Issue #2012 asks for a decision between a remainder last step and equal steps. The level law had only the remainder ladder. The project rule "CAM choices are parameters" asks for a parameter with a default.

## Scope limit

Face, Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal Slot have no `links` object. They cannot save the parameter and keep the remainder ladder. Issue #2832 adds the parameter to them. Turning has its own infeed laws and is not part of this change.

## UI screenshots

The images show the Lead in / Lead out tab before and after the new row.
The before image uses the same merged scene with only the new row removed.
A temporary CPU renderer drew the real egui meshes, fonts and textures.
The test harness uses a placeholder viewport. The environment has no WGPU adapter.
No capture code or images are in the PR branch.

![Before: Linking group without Equal depth steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/d20bbdb08204c89873c18935732cf7039c10375c/pr-2842/leads-before.png)

![After: Linking group with Equal depth steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/d20bbdb08204c89873c18935732cf7039c10375c/pr-2842/leads-after.png)

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `the_default_ladder_keeps_the_remainder_and_equal_steps_is_opt_in`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_count_and_never_pass_the_stepdown`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_at_top_z_under_stock`
- `equal_steps_refuse_what_the_remainder_ladder_refuses`
- `a_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_pocket_with_keepouts_and_relief_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_trochoidal_adaptive_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_slot_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_bore_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_circular_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_3d_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`
- `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back`
- `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`
- `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode`
- `the_generated_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps`

Red before the change: yes. The motion pin did not compile on `upstream/main` 3970d3d03 (`Approach` has no field `equal_steps`; `cut_levels_for` and `equal_stepdown` do not exist).

Mutation results:

- Mutation 1: `ladder_stepdown` ignores the mode. Result: red. 10 of the 11 motion pins fail. The refusal pin stays green, which is correct.
- Mutation 2: the 12 caller files are the files of `upstream/main`, and the new law stays. Result: red. The 7 operation pins fail. The 4 law pins stay green.
- Mutation 3: the digest byte and the DTO write are removed. Result: red. `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`, `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back` and `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps` fail.
- After each mutation the code was restored and the pins were green again.

The first stamp pin did not fail in mutation 3. A default approach hashes no bytes, so each approach that is not the default already has a different stamp. The pin now also compares two approaches that are not the default.

Gate on the reviewed-finding fix:

- Head: `db53a0a827db8d3a59b518e1960f1f862198e0cd`. It merges `upstream/main` at `81407b31bab58d4037bbae90b18bbecfe9229103`.
- The merge conflict affected imports only. Both import sets stay. `pocket_avoid_with_relief` calls `cut_levels_for`.
- New pin: `a_pocket_with_keepouts_and_relief_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`. It checks both ladders with keep-outs and dogbone relief endpoints.
- Caller mutation: bypass `cut_levels_for`. The pin is RED on the equal cut planes. Restore: GREEN.
- Relief mutation: suppress corner relief. The pin is RED on the missing bottom relief endpoint. Restore: GREEN.
- Law mutation: ignore the equal mode. Eleven pins are RED. The refusal pin stays GREEN. Restore: all 12 motion pins GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. 163 of 164 steps pass in 22.8 minutes. Both motion and app `equal_steps` suites pass.
- The one failed step is `ui suites: lib`: 1,278 passed, seven failed, seven ignored. All seven failures report `No adapter found`.
- The explicit UI library rerun has the same result in 54.50 seconds. Neither run has a SIGSEGV.
- The seven failures are six `egui_app::report_tests` capture tests and `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`. The environment exposes no WGPU adapter.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN on this head.
- The final worktree has no capture helper, review evidence or image files. The merge takes main's process version without a manual edit.

File length: `crates/motion/src/approach.rs` was 440 lines and is now 446. `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs` is now 402 lines.

## Latest review validation

Head: `db53a0a827db8d3a59b518e1960f1f862198e0cd` (unchanged). No source change was required by the latest review.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. 232 of 233 steps passed in 32.4 minutes.
- Motion heavy tests: 56 passed, zero failed. App heavy tests: 40 passed, one failed. Nine known-fail checks passed as expected.
- The failed pin is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` in `app:pocket3d_hsm`.
- The failure is the path count assertion at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`. Actual counts are `(3158, 3130, 1141)`.
- This platform uses the unmeasured macOS count range documented with #2371. Earlier safety assertions pass.
- Baseline check: remove all PR source changes in motion and app. Run the exact ignored heavy pin. It fails with the same counts.
- Restore the source and run the exact pin again. It fails with the same counts. `git diff --exit-code` passes after restoration.
- This count failure therefore predates the PR source changes. No count range was changed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. 163 of 164 steps passed in 26.1 minutes.
- Motion: 1,046 passed, zero failed, 54 ignored. App: 1,002 passed, zero failed, 18 ignored.
- All 12 motion `equal_steps` pins and all six app `equal_steps` pins pass.
- UI library in quick: 1,278 passed, seven failed, seven ignored. The other selected UI targets pass.
- Explicit UI library rerun from `crates/ui`: the same counts in 37.23 seconds. Neither run has a SIGSEGV.
- All seven UI failures report `No adapter found`. They are the six report capture tests and `headless_run_succeeds` named in the review.
- This machine reports an Apple M3 Max GPU with Metal support. The test process finds no Metal adapter.
- A passing local UI library run with an accessible graphics adapter remains required.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- All commands ran locally with sccache disabled. No tests were skipped to obtain a pass.
- No source, test, screenshot, log, evidence file, or process version was committed. The PR stays a draft.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.cnc"` is empty. The default ladder is the same.

## Not exercised

- No pin generates these ladders with the mode on: the 2D Adaptive rest ladder, the Circular vault rings, the 3D Pocket shell and rest-refine ladders, the rotary and multi-axis roughing. They call the same function as the pinned ladders.
- No pin generates a pocket on a part with the mode on. `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode` pins the stepdown that the region law reads, not the region.
- Code that reads `stepdown` as a bound is not changed (the 3-D shell floor below a plane, the first entry height of the contour). With equal steps it reads a bound a little larger than the real step. The decision file records this.
- The new UI row has no test of its own. No snapshot PNG is changed.
- The heavy lanes ran on the final head. See the validation results below.
- Nothing was run on a machine or in the stock simulation.

## Overlaps

- #2678 (`needs-rework`, `conflicts`) changes `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs`. It replaces the same `cut_levels_under` calls with its own `floor_levels::cut_levels`. It also changes `levels.rs`, but in `run_level_walks`, which this PR does not change. This PR is not stacked on #2678, because #2678 does not merge with `main` now. Whichever merges second refreshes, and must keep the mode in the 3-D ladder.
- #2796 changes `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs`, in a different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2716 and #2714 change `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. This PR does not change that file.

Build note: the shared sccache server on the build machine did not answer. The tests and gates ran with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
Stacked on #2714 (merge #2714 first)

## What changed

This fix changes 23 files relative to parent `b95c27b2e`.
It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.

## UI screenshots

These inherited parent renders use the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU).
The before views show upstream `5ed5b7fe2`.
The after views come from parent PR #2714.
The pictured UI files are unchanged in #2836.
The images are stored only on `mkinney/Camcraft` branch `pr-screenshots`, at commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`:

| View | Before | After |

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (13 tests):

- `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (review fix)
- `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line`
- `a_face_radius_past_half_the_row_spacing_turns_on_the_semicircle`
- `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool`
- `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off`
- `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_contour_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_slot_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (6 tests):

- `face_contour_and_slot_take_arc_turns_and_a_radius_through_edit_operation_and_undo`
- `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key`
- `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked`
- `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp`

Two unit tests in `blend.rs`: `a_user_radius_turns_on_corner_arcs_where_the_stride_has_room` and `a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` (review fix). Two unit tests there changed with the plan type (`bool` became `Option<Turn>`).

Red before the change: yes. On the unchanged code the motion pin does not compile, because `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` and `SlotParams` have no such fields (`error[E0560]`).

Mutation results. Each mutation put one guard back to the old behaviour. Each pin went red, and green again after the restore.

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Contour reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Contour has no radius door | `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |
| Face does not read `blend_radius` | `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Face has no radius door | `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off` | red |
| Face step goes inside the overrun line | `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line` | red |
| Face corner arcs only for rows within the tool diameter | `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool` | red |
| Slot rounds nothing | `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Slot has no radius door | `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |
| Slot reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Slot of one row says nothing | `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so` | red |
| `sane.rs` door without the three kinds | `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Face radius | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Slot option | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Contour radius | `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| Slot digest without the option | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Face digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Contour digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Slot project file drops the option on save | `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key` | red |
| Face takes the semicircle when half the spacing is less than 0.005 mm past the radius (review fix) | `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short`, `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` | red (`actual radii: [0.012500000000000178]` for 0.01 mm) |

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

Pins: `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (the reviewer's 60 x 10.025 mm case and three other spacings), and the unit test `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on head `acd5b8f73`: 708 steps, 0 failed, 48.2 minutes. The `ui suites: lib` and `ui suites: shell` steps passed on this machine (a software graphics adapter is available). The gate is this large because the diff changes `motion` and most test files of `app` and `ui`.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` is green on head `acd5b8f73`: 218 steps, 0 failed, 44.8 minutes. The lanes that ran:

- `motion heavy`: `lib`, `bins`, `doc` and 29 binaries, `arc_turn_kinds` included.
- `app heavy`: `lib`, `bins`, `doc` and 179 binaries.
- Three known-fail steps for #1950 were red as expected: two in `motion heavy: lib`, one in `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Screenshots

The images show the Passes tab of the Properties panel, cropped. A temporary test rendered the real egui shell with `Harness::render()`. That test is not in the PR. "Before" is `upstream/main` `5fdbed9bd` with arc turns on. "After" is this PR with arc turns on and a radius set. The header of the panel names the seeded operation, so the crop leaves it out. The images are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

Face, before and after (default, then a 2 mm radius):

![Face before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/face-before.png)
![Face after, default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/face-after-default.png)
![Face after, 2 mm radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/face-after-radius.png)

2D Contour, before and after (1 mm radius):

![Contour before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/contour-before.png)
![Contour after, 1 mm radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/contour-after-radius.png)

Slot, before (no option) and after (1 mm radius):

![Slot before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/slot-before.png)
![Slot after, 1 mm radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/b27df2476ce10b35ceed354e20e7cb2128b8e08d/pr-2831/slot-after-radius.png)

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty. The default output of each kind did not change.

## Size of the diff

The diff touches about 290 files. Most hunks are one line: an exhaustive `OpParams::Face`, `OpParams::Contour`, `OpParams::Slot`, `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` or `SlotParams` literal gets `blend_radius: None` (and `blend_turns: false` for Slot). The logic is in these files:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/blend.rs`, `face.rs`, `slots.rs`, `slot_turns.rs` (new), `contour_params.rs`, `tab_bridge.rs`
- `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`, `types/sane.rs`, `generate.rs`, `params.rs`, `params/mill2d.rs`
- `crates/app/src/project/params.rs`, `params_impl.rs`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/kind_editors.rs`, `mill2d_page.rs`, `mill2d_more_page.rs`

## Not exercised

- No posted G-code test for the new Face corner arcs or the Slot arcs. The post reads them as the same G2/G3 moves that the semicircle and the pocket arcs give.
- No UI test clicks the new radius rows. They use `arc_turn_rows`, the rows of the pocket kinds. No snapshot PNG changed.
- 2D Contour generation with a radius ran through the app only as a refusal (a radius past the tool radius). The arcs at the radius are pinned in the motion crate.
- A Slot with arc turns and a Ramp or Helix entry, or keep-down links, has no test of its own. The fillet does not move the start or the end of the pass.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket from the previous operations
body:
## What changed

The rest group of the 2D Pocket has a new mode, "previous operations".
In this mode the rest area is read from the stock that the earlier operations of the same setup leave.
The entered-tool mode of #1489 does not change, and it stays the default.

- `RestParams` has the field `source` (`RestSource::EnteredTool` or `RestSource::PreviousOperations`).
- `machining2d::rest_pocket_previous` plans the rest passes from a column grid.
  `rest_stock_from_columns` builds the `RestStock` of #2031 from that grid, one floor for each cut depth.
  `rest_plan_stock` makes the rest area from it.
- The grid is the one that `rest::prior_state` builds for the 3D Pocket: the setup stock, cut by the cached paths of the earlier operations, each with its tool shape.
- The reading is conservative:
  - A column stands at a cut depth when its top is above that depth. A floor allowance is material.
  - The standing columns grow by one cell diagonal.
  - A column that cannot be read stands. The pocket outside the grid stands.
  - The rest area is the union over all cut depths. A roughing pass that stops above the floor leaves the whole pocket.
- The two modes never use the planner of the other mode. Each planner refuses the other mode by name.
- The mode rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest.source` and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter.
  A file without the key reads as the entered tool.
- The Pocket page has the row "Rest stock from". The previous tool rows hide in the new mode.

Generation refuses by name when the stock cannot be established:

- an earlier operation of the setup has no toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup has a stale toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup is suppressed and has a cut on record;
- the Pocket is tilted (also refused at the edit).

When no earlier operation cut, the stock is known. The whole pocket is cut and a note says it.

## Cause

The rest generator trusted the entered previous tool.
It could not see the depth that the earlier operation reached (#1490, item 3).

## Tests

Pins, all new:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_tests.rs` (lib): `each_reading_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `a_floor_cut_at_the_cut_depth_does_not_stand_and_one_above_it_does`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_previous.rs`: 6 tests. They compare the rest area with an independent simulation of the earlier operations: a flat tool, a wall allowance, a bull-nose tool, mixed tools with a partial depth and disconnected cuts, an island. The rest path cuts each column that was left and cuts no wall.
- `crates/app/tests/rest_previous_ops.rs`: 7 tests. The real job against an independent simulation; the shallow roughing pass; the four refusals; stale after a changed tool, depth and order; `RegenerateAll`; undo and redo; the project file; MCP with save and reopen.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` now also covers the mode.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/rest_source_tests.rs`: 2 tests for the new row.

Red before the change: the pins use the new API and do not compile on `upstream/main`. Thus the mutation results below are the proof for each guard.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| every cut depth is read (`Guards::depth`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| an unreadable column stands (`Guards::unknown`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| the pocket outside the grid stands (`Guards::outside`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| one cell of growth (`Guards::cell`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| `rest_plan` refuses the new mode | `the_two_rest_modes_never_use_each_others_planner` | red | green |
| `rest_pocket_previous` refuses the entered mode | same | red | green |
| `validate` does not read the previous tool in the new mode | same | red | green |
| job: tilted plane refused | `a_tilted_plane_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_at_generation` | red | green |
| door: tilted plane refused at the edit | same | red | green |
| job: `previous_ops_refusal` is called | `a_stock_that_cannot_be_established_is_refused_by_name` | red | green |
| earlier operation suppressed | same | red | green |
| earlier operation stale | same | red | green |
| earlier operation never generated | same | red | green |
| the Pocket arm routes the mode | `the_rest_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left` | red | green |
| stamp byte 0xD8 | `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red | green |

The first four guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off. The other eleven were removed by hand.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head merged with `upstream/main` c4ac3ce6d: green, 357 steps, 0 failed (29.2 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup (#318). The code path is `rest::prior_state`, which the 3D Pocket uses. No test here crosses a setup boundary. The check for stale operations reads the same setup only.
- A WCS yaw. The existing `wcs_yaw::enter` turns the grid. No test here has a yaw.
- The field stock engine (#586, #637). The reader is `Columns`, which reads the two engines. The tests use the column grid.
- Zigzag and Offset rings in the new mode. They use the passes of the entered-tool mode, which has its own tests. The new tests use Waterline.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane). The new row moves the rows of a Pocket page that has rest machining on.
- The app was not started by hand. The UI tests ran the page in the test harness.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/2033-rest-previous-ops.md`)

- One rest area for all levels. An upper level can cut air where only a lower level has material.
- The strict reading keeps a band of about 1.5 cells along each wall that an earlier tool rode. The rest pass follows those walls.

title: test(ui): run the diag event-level test in a binary of its own
body:
## What changed

`diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` moves from the `diag` unit tests in the `camcraft-ui` lib to a new test binary, `crates/ui/tests/diag_events.rs`. That binary holds this one test only. The test calls `diag::warn` and `diag::info` directly. The lib keeps `the_macros_take_println_shaped_arguments`, which compiles the two macros. The assertions do not change.

## Cause

`tracing` caches the interest of each callsite for the whole process. The test installs a thread-local subscriber with `with_default`. In the lib binary, other tests on other threads call `diag_info!` through the same callsite. If another thread registers the callsite with the dispatchers that it saw before the new subscriber, and that registration ends after the rebuild of the new subscriber, the cached interest is "never". The INFO line is then lost and the WARN line (another callsite) stays. This agrees with the output in the issue. No other test in the lib installs a subscriber. In a binary of its own, no other thread uses these callsites.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2595-diag-events-own-binary.md` (the dropped options: `rebuild_interest_cache()`, a shared lock, a global subscriber).

## Readings (Windows 11, 16 threads)

- `diag_events` binary: 50 runs, 50 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=16`: 3 full runs, each `1251 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 3 steps, 0 failed (ui build, ui lib, diag_events).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` does not change: one test moves from the lib to the new binary.

## Pinning test

`diag_events::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level`

## Not exercised

- I did not reproduce the failure on this machine before the change. The issue measured 1 failure in 3 full lib runs on Linux.
- No run on Linux or macOS.

title: fix(ui): ribbon cell fill holds its whole label in each theme
body: ## What changed A ribbon cell painted its fill and took clicks in a box of `cell_h` (30 px). The label sits at `glyph_px + 2` below the cell top. The shipped themes (`horizon-day`, `teal-night`) set `glyph_px` to 22. Thus the label ran from 24 px to about 38 px, and the fill covered only the top half of the label. This occurred for a toggled cell, a hovered cell, and a toggled cell under the pointer. The built-in tables overflow by about 2 px. - `ribbon_cell::cell_box` extends the fill and the click target down to the label bottom. The box stops 2 px above the group caption row. - A filled cell writes its label in `contrast::on_fill(fill)`, the same ink as its glyph. A cell without a fill keeps `text` / `text_faint`. - `cell` and `fit_label` move from `painted.rs` (468 lines) to the new `ribbon_cell.rs`. `painted.rs` re-exports `cell`, so the callers do not change. `painted.rs` is now 370 lines. - The ribbon layout (`cell_h`, `ribbon_h`, the rows) does not change.
