title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`, `Stock::with_partial_undercut`, `SdfTool::Dovetail`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. Both the stock view and Simulate playback cut the head and neck with it. Notice `cut_twin_work::twin_tool` maps `SdfTool::Dovetail` to `"dovetail"`.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror (keeping `0.0` `bulge` and `neck_slot` keys in JSON), the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, and the kept-parts law for both stock and part sources.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. `list_operation_types` and `edit_operation` include `bulge` and `neck_slot` when they equal `0.0`.
- **UI**: the four undercut kinds in the tool editor (`tool_undercut_row.rs` seeds valid defaults, `Flank angle (deg)` / `flank angle °` edits `ToolKind::Dovetail`, and `Corner radius` stays hidden for undercut kinds), the Slot Undercut page (`undercut_page.rs`), and five original icons (SVG masters rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## UI screenshots

Before/after renders from the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU) on `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`) and this PR branch (images stored on `mkinney/Camcraft` `pr-screenshots` commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`):

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

## Tests

New pins cover the new behaviour. Each review fix below also has a direct test and mutation check.

- `camcraft-tools --lib` (`107 passed; 0 failed`): `undercut::tests` checks sane cutters, refusals by name, the profile contact point, and the drawn outline.
- `camcraft-motion --lib` (`459 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`): `machining2d::undercut::tests` pins single-station Z moves, entry slot refusals, concentric arc slots, profile contact offsets, and input refusals.
- `camcraft-sim --test undercut_laws` (`14 passed; 0 failed`): pins `UndercutLift`, `ShankHit`, `acquit_undercut_by_prior`, `Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`, `Atom::cap`, and `Stock::simulate_undercut`.
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_slot_undercut` (`7 passed; 0 failed`): pins MCP cutting, verification, posting, refusals, `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts`, and `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play` (`8 passed; 0 failed`): pins `playback_removes_undercut_head_and_neck_and_matches_field_view`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play_partial` (`4 passed; 0 failed`): pins `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy`.
- `camcraft-motion --test golden_undercut`: pins four golden CL files. The generator suite and its unchanged goldens now live in `crates/motion/tests/`.
- `camcraft-app --test tool_law` (`5 passed; 0 failed`): pins undercut cutter compatibility.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` (`1256 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`): includes `tool_undercut_row::tests`, `tool_cutter_params::each_milling_kind_shows_the_parameters_its_outline_is_drawn_from`, and `tests/tool_undercut.rs` (`new_tool_undercut_kinds_seed_sane_defaults_hide_corner_radius_and_show_dovetail_flank_angle`, `dovetail_properties_and_editor_edit_flank_angle_without_corner_radius`, and `slot_undercut_page_shows_its_geometry_heights_passes_and_feeds_fields`).

Review-fix mutation checks (guard reverted -> RED, restored -> GREEN):

- UI dovetail flank angle, undercut defaults, and corner-radius filter reverted: RED (`3 failed` across `tests/tool_undercut.rs` and `tool_cutter_params`). Restored: GREEN (`11 passed; 0 failed`).
- `is_part_kept_kind` reverted in `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`: `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts` RED (`post` succeeded instead of refusing). Restored: GREEN (`7 passed; 0 failed`).
- `skip_serializing_if = "is_zero"` restored in `crates/app/src/project/undercut_dto.rs`: `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot` RED (`list_operation_types` omitted `bulge` and `neck_slot`). Restored: GREEN (`7 passed; 0 failed`).
- `stock_play.rs` and `stock_play_head.rs` undercut playback handling reverted: `playback_removes_undercut_head_and_neck_and_matches_field_view` and `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy` RED. Restoring `stock_play.rs` alone kept `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy` RED. Restored both: GREEN (`8 passed; 0 failed` and `4 passed; 0 failed`).

Gate on `b95c27b2e52fc8b976ce9372bcc5e4141c247113`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 651 steps with zero failures (45.9 minutes). The merged main revision is `e5b0ca3c1`. It includes #2767, which fixes the four reviewed area-preview failures. The UI unit suite passed 1,258 tests (7 ignored). All 16 UI integration suites passed. `cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed with zero warnings.

Latest review-fix checks:

- The motion `golden_undercut` suite passed all four tests. Removing the motion test target gave RED. A feed change from 120 to 121 made all four goldens fail. Restoring the suite and feed returned all four tests to GREEN. The four CL files moved without byte changes.
- Reverting the main geometry fix gave exactly the four reviewed frame-cost failures. Restoring it returned all eight frame-cost tests to GREEN.
- The temporary literature audit gave RED on the old decision (0/8 checks) and GREEN on the updated decision (8/8). The decision records checked sources, design choices, and limitations. No audit script or review evidence is on this branch.

Current merge blocker: main advanced to `744c0847b04d54cfc6e3e8b24a21520c40b6bcef` during validation. A later local refresh exposes safety overlaps: `verify/avoid_poly.rs:25` omits `Atom::cap`, and `verify/swept.rs:130` omits `Prof::Dove` and `Prof::Ball` in keep-out dilation. The refresh compile checks and clippy are RED. The gate was stopped after the compile failures. No new collision semantics were selected. Local commit `b8c5cb42e` is not pushed. The pushed head and its GREEN gate remain `b95c27b2e`. The `Addressed:` comment records the blocker.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden changed. Four golden CL files are new:

- `slot_undercut_tslot_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_keyseat_arc.cl`
- `slot_undercut_dovetail_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_lollipop_arc.cl`

No snapshot PNG changed. Five icon PNGs are new (`cargo xtask icons` wrote them from the new SVG masters and changed no other PNG).

## Not exercised

- The literature search ran during the latest review fix. `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md` records checked handbook, Autodesk behaviour, and research sources for entry, exit, profiles, and field simulation. It records the limits of those sources and the implementation. The search used the web tool because Perplexity was unavailable. The implementation preceded this search.
- Dovetail and lollipop parts are not tested through the app. Their profiles are tested in the sim crate (solid law and field stock) and the generator.
- The program verdict before a post reads the stock from above. It does not show the undercut as removed. The undercut law and the solid law judge the operation instead.
- A flipped WCS and a rotated work offset refuse the kind. An aligned setup and a WCS yaw do not list it. No 3+2 tilt.
- One depth level for each operation. The far end of a blind slot stays square. The centre line is typed, not picked.
- Issue #896 (form cutters with a drawn outline, corner rounding, slitting saw) stays open. This PR adds only the four parametric kinds that #1444 needs.

## Overlaps

No open PR changes the same function. These open PRs change other functions in the same files. The PR that merges second refreshes.

- #2678, #2149: `mcp/job.rs`, `operation/generate.rs`, `project/file.rs`, `verify/mod.rs`, `verify/probe.rs`, `verify/types.rs`, `ui/state.rs`
- #2675, #2666: `operation/generate.rs`
- #2663: `ui/egui_app/tool_settings.rs`
- #2665, #2662, #1798: `ui/state.rs` (#1798 also `icons.rs`)
- #2594: `ui/egui_app/browser_tree.rs`

#2670, #2563, #1713, #1798, #2665, #2712, #2715, #2730, #2731, #2741, and #2742 merged while this work ran. Their changes are in the branch through the merge of `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`).

title: feat(post): add Hurco WinMax (NC) ISNC post and Hurco VM10i machine
body:
Replaces #2640 with the same Hurco commit (`4cd8bdae2`, cherry-picked unchanged) on a branch straight off `main`. #2640 was stacked on the Grbl post draft #2506, so it could not merge before #2506; this one does not need it.

## Latest review fixes

Head: `ed04216dc468f9880dea0651c813b5762c401488`.

- Finding 1: Cancel active cycles before travel. Seat each hole at the section hop before descent to R. Refuse missing hops.
- The `cycle_hop` suite includes Hurco. It checks back-to-back cycles and cycles after probing, feeds, and arcs.
- Finding 3: Set the vendor to `Camcraft`. `hurco_post_vendor_is_camcraft` pins the value.
- All 30 focused tests passed. Cycle seating, feed tracking, arc tracking, and vendor mutations failed their pins. Restored fixes passed.
- Update the synthesized Hurco golden for safe hops. Conformance passed all 7 tests.
- Clippy for `camcraft-post` and `camcraft-app`, all targets with warnings denied: passed.
- Quick gate ran 648 steps. After the golden update, only `continuous_4axis_part` remains red: `/version: 71 != 70`.
- Finding 2 remains open. No simulator access, load results, or path comparisons are available. Issue #2573 remains incomplete.

Re-checked on this branch: `camcraft-post --test script_hurco_winmax` 11 passed; `camcraft-app --test hurco_winmax_post` 7, `post_spindle_rule_all` 2, `conformance` 5 passed.

---

## What changed

- Add clean-room built-in post `Hurco WinMax (NC)` in `assets/posts/hurco-winmax.cps`.
- Add clean-room 3-axis VMC definition `Hurco VM10i` in `assets/machines/hurco-vm10i.mch`.
- Register both entries in `BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`, and `embedded()` inside `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`.
- Emit Hurco WinMax ISNC blocks (`G20`/`G21` unit block, `O0001`..`O9999`, `G90 G17 G94 G54..G59 G40 G49 G80`, `G54.1 P1`..`P93`, decimal-second `P` dwell on `G04`/`G82`/`G89`, `G84.2`/`G84.3` rigid tapping and `G84` floating tapping, `G68`/`G69` rotation, `G31` probing with `G10 L2`, no `G91.1`).
- Record design decisions in `docs/decisions/2573-hurco-winmax-post.md`.

## Cause

No built-in post processor or machine definition existed for Hurco WinMax 3-axis NC/ISO (ISNC) mills.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `crates/post/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs` (8/8 pass; red before fix `0/7`: `hurco-winmax.cps` missing): multi-op contour/arc/drill/peck/tap across two tools and two offsets, `G20`/`G21` and `EndUnits`, decimal-second `P` dwell, `G84.2`/`G84.3`/`G84`, `G54`..`G59` and `G54.1 P1`..`P93`, `G28`/`G53` safe retract, `O0001`..`O9999` bounds, `G41`/`G42` compensation, `G68`/`G69` rotation, `G31` probing, smoothing note, named refusals, and a strict documented WinMax ISNC word-set allowlist check over posted programs and all 21 `.nc` goldens.
  - `crates/app/tests/hurco_winmax_post.rs` (2/2 pass; red before fix `0/2`: missing registry entries): checks `BUILTINS`/`MACHINES` registration, `post_serves`, VM10i parse, full ECS contour/pocket/drill/peck/rigid-tap workflow across two tools and `G54`/`G55`, plus `G54.1 P1`.
  - Cross-post suites updated and green: `conformance` (7/7), `machine` (33/33), `machine_library` (11/11), `post_spindle_rule_all` (5/5), `bore_cycle` (9/9), `comp_plane` (3/3), `decimal_point_fanuc_family` (3/3), `declared_options` (3/3), `end_units` (3/3), `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family` (9/9), `radius_arcs` (7/7), `script_hurco_winmax` (11/11).
- Mutations (each verified RED when reverted/weakened, GREEN when restored):
  - `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` reverted to `HEAD`: `0/1` (`hurco_winmax_post_and_vm10i_are_registered_and_serve_mill` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `oWord()` `1..=9999` check removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `workOffsetMax` raised and `> 99` guard removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `G53` missing `safeRetractZ` check removed: `0/1` (`extended_work_offsets_and_safe_retract_and_o_word` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - `rigidTapping === false` check removed: `0/1` (`tapping_modes_and_rigid_tapping_guard` fails), restored `1/1`.
  - Cycle illegal dwell `rawDwell > 0` check removed: `0/1` (`cycles_refuse_illegal_dwell_and_tilt_and_zero_spindle` fails), restored `1/1`.

title: fix(ui): Tab, Shift+Tab and Enter move between the value fields of a page
body:
#2516: in a group of value fields, Enter did not move the focus to the next value field, and Tab seemed not to move it either.

## What I found

egui's own Tab moved the focus, but in draw order over each focusable widget. On the operation property panel, Tab from a value field went to:

- a group header (it has no visible focus mark), then
- a checkbox or a combo, then
- the action bar: Generate, Clear toolpath, Close and Delete operation.

Thus the focus seemed to leave the form. Enter committed the value and dropped the focus (egui's default for a DragValue).

## What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/field_ring.rs`: a ring of the value fields of the Properties pane.
  - The form seam's number helpers in `fields.rs` register each field (`num`, `num_feed`, `num_narrow`, the `num_*_row`/`_named`/`_by` forms, `num_plain`, `int_range_row`, `num_unit`).
  - `group_open` (`layout/form.rs`) marks the group of the fields in its body.
  - `pages::properties` opens the ring before the pane and closes it after.
- From a registered field:
  - Tab moves to the next field, and Shift+Tab to the previous one. The ring wraps at the two ends.
  - Enter commits the value to the draft (as before) and moves to the next field of the same group. After the group's last field, the focus drops (as before).
  - From a combo, a checkbox or a button, egui's own order stays.
- The moved-to field gets the focus when the next frame begins, before any widget draws. Thus egui's DragValue selects its text, and a typed number replaces the old one, as after a click. A repaint is requested for that frame.
- Focus is ephemeral UI state and queues no command. A value still reaches the document only through Apply (`EditOperationParams`).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2516-field-focus.md`.

## Tests

- `egui_app::field_focus_tests` (new, on the real operation property panel of a Pocket op):
  - `tab_and_shift_tab_walk_the_value_fields_and_wrap` (Heights): Tab goes 25 → 12 → 9 → 1 → 25, past the combos and the group headers. Shift+Tab wraps from the first field to the last, then goes back. No command is queued.
  - `enter_commits_the_value_and_moves_to_the_next_field_of_its_group` (Feeds): a typed 750 lands in the draft, and the focus moves to the plunge feed. A typed 150 there replaces the old value. The document keeps 800 until Apply. Enter in the group's last field drops the focus.
- `egui_app::layout::field_ring::tests` (3): the pure rule (wrap, Enter within the group only, no move from a widget outside the ring).
- Mutation check: with the ring's move switched off, both panel tests fail.
- Changed: the `thread_hand_tests` helpers `edit_number` and `type_dip` click a field only when it is not focused. After Enter, the next field already has the focus with its text selected. A click on a focused field only places the cursor, so the typed text was appended.

Gates on 213874858:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 9 steps, 0 failed (`ui lib` and the 7 UI suites of the gate map). The last edit after the gate is a clippy fix (`Option::replace`), with the same behaviour. The `field_` and `thread_hand` tests (18) are green after it.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- No hand test in the real window. The tests drive the real `pages::properties` code through the harness.
- Fields drawn with a raw `DragValue` outside the form seam helpers are not in the ring. egui's own Tab order stays for them (#1122 moves the pages to the seam).
- Dialogs outside the Properties pane (for example the tool library window) are not in the ring.

Changelog: In the Properties pane, Tab and Shift+Tab move between the value fields, and Enter commits a value and moves to the next field of its group (#2516)

Effort: medium (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #2516

title: feat(machine): a machine file names its post, and the Setup page offers it
body:
**What changed**

- A `.mch` file can state `controller.post`, the name of a built-in post. `Machine.post`
  holds it. A file without the key reads as before.
- The reader refuses a value that is not a non-empty string, at `controller.post`
  (`post::machine::post_name`).
- The validator also refuses a name that is not a built-in post, and a post that does not
  serve the machine's kind. The post crate gets the registry as a closure, as the holder
  lookup does (#828), so there is no new crate edge.
- `posting::post_offer` returns `Option<PostOffer>`. It offers the machine's named post
  (`OfferWhy::Machine`) when that post is in the registry, serves the mount, and is not
  the setup's post. Otherwise it gives the kind offer as before (`OfferWhy::Kind`). A
  `.cps` file post is never offered over.
- The Setup page's banner tells which offer it is: "the machine names grblHAL as its post;
  switch to it?" or the kind text as before. The button queues `SelectPostNamed`, so it
  rides undo.
- A mount never changes the post by itself (#343, #388).
- The MCP tools say the same, after the QA finding on #2374. `post_offer_for` asks for any
  setup (`posting_offer.rs`). `load_machine` replies with `post_offer` for the setup that it
  mounted to, and `get_job` gives `post_offer` for each setup: the post, why, and the
  `set_setup_post` call that takes it. `null` means no offer.
- The description of the `post` tool lists every name in `BUILTINS`. The hand-written list
  did not have "Tormach PathPilot", grblHAL, TinyG or the Carvera posts.
- 32 shipped machine files state their post, where `MACHINES`, a machine's issue or its
  post writes the pairing: the PathPilot mills, routers, lathes and plasma table, grblHAL
  and the Sienci AltMills, TinyG, the Makera machines, the Doosan DNM 5700s and the Haas
  machines. The generic machines, the Sodick ALC400G, the Mach3-era Tormach mills and the
  sinker template state none.
- The Machines pane's file editor gives a user's own machine its post. General has a Post
  row, a dropdown (`Field.choices`) of the built-in posts that serve the file's kind, plus
  "(none)", which takes the key out. A stated name off the list stays in view with its
  refusal. Only built-in posts are offered: a `.cps` file has no stable name for a machine
  file to state.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md`.

**Screenshots**

Taken by hand in the Windows release build. "Before" is a build of `main` from before this
branch; "after" is this PR's head `b6bc94239`. Same document, setup and window in each pair.
The path line under "Editing ..." is masked: it showed a local user folder.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Setup page, Post: a setup on the shipped Tormach 770MX with the Fanuc post | ![Setup Post before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/setup-banner-before.png) | ![Setup Post after: the machine names Tormach PathPilot as its post; switch to it?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/setup-banner-after.png) |
| Machines pane, file editor, General: a user's own grblHAL machine | ![Machines editor before: no Post row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/machine-editor-before.png) | ![Machines editor after: a Post row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/machine-editor-after.png) |

The Post dropdown open, after: "(none)" and the built-in posts that serve a mill.

![Machines editor after: the Post dropdown open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roer70/Camcraft/c15c4c720e0f6a3c4265d3c998afeb3ad0904e46/2554/machine-editor-after-open.png)

**Readings**

Branched from `main` at `6349a542e`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 346 steps, 0 failed, on `2d26ef2a3`.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --base upstream/main`: 837 steps, 836 ok, 61.9 min. The one red step was
  `clippy -D warnings` (`bool::then` with a closure in `posting_offer.rs`), fixed in
  `a9205467b`; that step reran green with `--failed`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head `b6bc94239`, clean tree: green,
  346 steps, 0 failed, 10.0 min.
- By hand, the release build: a setup on the grblHAL machine is offered the grblHAL post
  and the switch rides undo; a user's own machine picks its post from the editor's dropdown,
  writes it, and the Setup page then offers it.

**Pinning tests**

- `crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`:
  `a_machine_that_names_its_post_is_offered_it_and_the_choice_rides_undo`,
  `the_named_post_must_be_a_built_in_post_that_serves_the_machine`,
  `the_editor_offers_the_built_in_posts_that_serve_the_machine`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machine_named_post.rs`:
  `the_grblhal_machine_offers_its_own_post_and_the_switch_rides_undo`,
  `a_users_own_machine_picks_its_post_from_the_editors_dropdown`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_machine_post.rs`:
  `mounting_the_770mx_offers_pathpilot_and_the_agent_takes_it_as_one_undo_step`,
  `the_offer_follows_the_setup_the_machine_went_to_not_the_active_one`,
  `a_machine_that_names_no_post_and_serves_the_current_one_offers_nothing`,
  `the_post_tool_lists_every_registry_post`
- `crates/post/src/machine/post_name.rs`: five unit tests for the reader and the rule.
- Not changed and still green: the lathe-over-mill-post offer test in
  `ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`, `plasma_post.rs` (only moved to `offer.post`) and
  `sinker_burn.rs`.

**Not exercised**

- By hand: a `.cps` file post on the setup is not offered over. The tests pin it.
- An older reader on a new file. `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops
  the key and loses only the offer, never a posted line. Thus no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.
- The pairing for machines with no written pairing. They state no post, and the kind offer
  does not change for them.
- An MCP agent on a document without setups. The `set_setup_post` refusal names
  `select_post`, which is not an MCP tool; the offer's hint says `add_setup`, then
  `set_setup_post`. The refusal text did not change here.

Changelog: A machine file can name the post that writes its programs; the Setup page and the MCP `load_machine` and `get_job` replies offer that post, the Machines editor picks it from a dropdown, the `post` tool lists every built-in post, and the shipped grblHAL, PathPilot, TinyG, Makera, Doosan and Haas machines name theirs (#2374)

Fixes #2374

title: fix(drill): name each hole wider than the drill, without holding the post
body:
#2496: `detect_holes` on a Drill op took holes wider than the drill. `generate` and `verify` then passed with no warning, and `post` wrote the program. Each such hole is drilled at the drill diameter, so it comes out undersize. Nothing told the user.

The fix follows the triage on the issue: name each hole that the drill does not make at its size. A pilot drill stays possible, so the post is not held.

## What changed

- **The law** (new `crates/app/src/operation/drill_size.rs`): `undersize_holes` gives each Z hole wider than the Drill-kind tool by more than `DRILL_SIZE_TOL` (0.1 mm on the diameter).
  - It reads only cycles that drill to size: Auto, Drill, Peck and Ream. Spot, Tap, FloatingTap, Bore and BackBore size the hole another way.
  - It reads only the mill's Z holes, not the turret's radial list.
  - A NaN or infinite hole radius, or a bad tool diameter, names nothing and does not panic.
- **Detect holes** keeps each such hole and names it in the new `DetectedHoles::undersize` list. Example: `the 8.000 mm hole at (-50.000, 0.000) is wider than the 6.000 mm drill: it is drilled 6.000 mm (a pilot) - use a 8.000 mm drill, or follow with a Bore or a reamer`.
  - MCP `detect_holes` answers it as `undersize`, beside `skipped`.
  - The GUI status line shows it. The GUI's pending command field `skipped` is now `notes`, with the skipped and the undersize sentences.
- **Generate** adds a new advisory `Warning::DrillUndersize { at, hole_mm, drill_mm }` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`) for each such hole, at its first cutting move.
  - `blocks_post()` is false, as for `Scallop`, `ProbeSearch` and `SinkerFinishOrder`.
  - MCP finding kind: `drill_undersize`.
  - The UI warning list groups it on its own line (key 216). `warned_moves` frames its move.
- The MCP tool description of `detect_holes` names `undersize` and `drill_undersize`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2496-drill-undersize.md`.

## Readings

- The issue's reproduction (D6, D8 and D12 through holes, catalog `DR-0600`) on a synthetic plate:
  - `detect_holes`: `holes: 3`, `skipped: []`, and `undersize` names the D8 and the D12 holes.
  - `generate`: `ok`, with two `drill_undersize` findings, `blocks_post: false`.
  - `verify`: `ok: true`. `post` writes the program.
- A D5 hole under the D6 drill: `verify` gives `ok: false` with a blocking `gouge`. The hole-wall excuse is capped at the facet sagitta (`WALL_SAG`, 0.05 mm), so it does not hide that cut. This law does not name it.

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/drill_undersize.rs` (new, MCP):
  - `holes_wider_than_the_drill_are_named_at_detect_and_on_the_path_and_the_post_writes`
  - `a_hole_at_the_drills_own_size_names_nothing`
  - `a_hole_narrower_than_the_drill_is_held_as_a_gouge_not_named_undersize`
- `app::operation::drill_size::tests` (4): the size band (D6.04 and D6.1 are the drill's size, D6.2 and D8 are not), the narrower hole, the cycles and tool kinds that the law does not read, and the bad numbers.
- `ui::detect_holes_note_tests::detect_holes_on_a_drill_op_keeps_a_wider_hole_and_names_it_undersize`: the GUI status line.
- Mutation check: with the generate hook removed, the first MCP test fails (`one warning per undersize hole: []`).

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (325 steps, 23 min) ran on the first version, with a 0.05 mm band. 319 steps were green. 6 failed:
  - `drilling_axial::an_axial_drill_runs_clean_on_the_lathe_and_posts_its_cycle`: from this change. Its "matched" fixture has a 4 mm drill in a 4.1 mm hole, and the 0.05 mm band named it. The band is now 0.1 mm (5b16ed7e4), and the suite is green. A wider band names fewer holes, so it cannot make the 319 green steps fail.
  - `example_catalog` (2 tests), `first_part_programs` (2 tests), `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number` and `wire_taper_angle::an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: not from this change. They fail the same way, at the same lines, on a clean worktree of the same base (bd0400ebb) on this Windows machine. `example_catalog` compares an LF program with the committed file read back with CRLF.
- On 5b16ed7e4: `drill_size` (4), `drill_undersize` (3), `drilling_axial` (7) and the GUI `detect_holes` tests (4): green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: one error, at `crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs:128`. That is #2479 (Clippy 1.99), in a file that this PR does not change. With only that lint allowed (`-A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`): clean.

## Not exercised

- The turret's radial holes (`cross`). The law does not read them.
- The real STEP file of the issue. The test uses a synthetic STL plate with the same hole sizes.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Changelog: A Drill operation names each hole wider than its drill, at Detect holes and as a warning on the toolpath that does not hold the post (a pilot drill stays possible) (#2496)

Effort: high (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #2496

title: refactor(tools): name each tool kind in the kind rules, with no catch-all
body:
#2505: the kind check in `Tool::kind_rule` (`crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`) ended with `_ => None`. A `ToolKind` added later passed the check with no kind rule. The equivalence test did not see it, because its kind list was written by hand.

## What changed

- `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`: the `_ => None` arm is gone. The last arm names the 13 kinds that have no rule, or whose guarded rules held: `EndMill`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`, `Bore`, `Drill`, `Tap`, `Turning`, `Groove`, `Thread`, `Form`, `Taper`, `Probe` and `Torch`. A new `ToolKind` does not compile until this match names it.
- `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity_tests.rs`:
  - New `kind_slot`: an exhaustive match that gives each kind a slot. A new kind does not compile until it gets a slot.
  - New test `the_sweep_list_holds_each_kind_once`: each slot occurs exactly one time in `KINDS`. A new slot fails the test until `KINDS` holds the new kind.
  - The oracle `old_is_sane` keeps its `_ => true`. It is the old law, verbatim.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2505-exhaustive-kind-match.md`. It also says why there is no `ToolKind::ALL` constant: `tools.rs` has 691 lines.

## Tests

- A trial variant `ProbeKindForTest` added to `ToolKind` gives `E0004` at `tool_sanity.rs:108` (the kind rules) and at `tool_sanity_tests.rs:125` (`kind_slot`). The trial was removed.
- `the_named_law_gives_the_old_verdict_everywhere`: green. Thus the verdicts for the 18 kinds do not change.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on d7aa843e5: green (tools lib; app `project_tool_refusal`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

- No behaviour changes, thus no UI or app suite other than the gate's selection was run.

title: fix(ui): show a progress overlay over the viewport while a toolpath generates
body: #2257: while an operation generates its toolpath, the viewport shows no progress. The cause is that generation ran in the frame, on the UI thread. Thus no frame painted until the job ended. ## What changed - **Generation on a worker** (native window only). `GenerateOperation` already had a seam between the world reads and the pure work (M5.3 B). That seam is now public as `StagedGeneration`: - `StagedGeneration::new` reads the world on the UI thread. - `StagedGeneration::finish` runs the generator, the verification and the stamp on a worker thread. - The result lands through the same undoable `GenerateOperation` as before. The generators, the verify check and the post gate do not change. - **The overlay** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/gen_overlay.rs`) lies at the top centre of the viewport while a job runs. The navigation strip at the bottom and the view cube stay clear. It shows: - the label of the operation; - "(2 of 5)" when more generations wait in the queue; - the elapsed time and an activity bar (the generators report no fraction); - a `Cancel generation` button. - **Stale results are discarded.** The user can edit, undo or delete while the worker runs. A result lands only while its operation and its cached path are the same as at staging (`GenerateOperation::still_current`). If not, the status line says: `generation of X discarded: the operation changed while it generated - generate it again`. - **Cancel** drops the result and the queue. The old toolpath stays. A worker that runs finishes in the background, and its result is ignored. - **New and Open** drop a running generation. A result for the old document never lands in the new one. - **The viewport takes no press inside the overlay.** A click on Cancel is not also a viewport pick. - **Only the window turns it on** (`State::gen_jobs.background`). Tests, headless runs, scripts and MCP keep the synchronous path. `State::settle` waits for the worker. The browser has no threads: a failed spawn runs the job in place, as the import worker does. - **Repaint:** the shell asks for a repaint every 50 ms only while a job runs or waits (`view_pass::state_redraw_delay`). A frame with no job does no more work than before (#2238). - **No world search in a frame.** The job finds its operation entity one time, when it starts. Each frame reads the label from that entity (`model::live_operation_label`, which checks that the entity is alive). A rename shows at once. A deleted operation shows its name. - Decision record: `docs/decisions/2257-generate-progress-overlay.md`. ## What it looks like Rendered headless from the seeded shell at 1280x800 (a throwaway test, not in the branch). The images are below. - Before: while `Contour1` generates, the viewport shows nothing. - After: the overlay at the top centre, with the operation name, the elapsed time, the activity bar and `Cancel generation`. **Before** (the viewport while `Contour1` generates): **After** (the overlay at the top centre): ## Tests New pinning tests: - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/generate_progress.rs` (structural; the result comes through a channel that the test holds, so no frame races a real generator): - `the_overlay_names_the_running_operation_and_goes_when_it_lands`: the overlay text `Generating Contour1 - ...` is over the viewport, and the Cancel button is there while the job runs. The two go when the job lands. - `a_refusal_ends_the_overlay_and_keeps_its_message` - `cancel_ends_the_overlay_and_drops_the_result`: a click on Cancel ends the overlay. The status says that the generation is cancelled. No history entry is written. - `a_result_for_an_operation_edited_meanwhile_is_discarded`: the edit stays, and the old result writes nothing. - `background_generation_lands_the_same_toolpath`: a real worker run through `settle`. - `the_overlay_text_counts_a_batch` - `one_search_for_each_job_and_a_rename_shows_without_another`: 10 frames and 100 progress reads do one name search. A rename shows in the overlay with no new search. - `a_deleted_operation_shows_its_name_and_no_dead_entity_is_read`: the overlay shows `Contour1` after a delete. Without the `is_alive` check, the test process stops (0xc0000409). - `crates/app/tests/generate_staged.rs`: - `staged_then_finished_lands_what_the_one_shot_command_lands`: the same path either way. - `a_result_is_stale_after_an_edit_a_generation_or_a_delete` Gates on 08022981: - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (222 steps): green, with two exceptions. Neither comes from this change: - `app suites: wire_tool` does not compile on main. That is #2244 (`CuttingRow` gained `stepdown` and `stepover`). - `ui suites: lib`: three tests in `setup_picks_disarm` failed one time. They pass alone. The same suite on a clean `upstream/main` worktree fails 1 of 3 runs at `--test-threads=16` (`setup_picks_disarm`, `setup_mount_pages`). Thus the failures are timing failures on main. - `generate_progress` (6) and `generate_staged` (2): green after the last layout change. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --bins --test generate_staged -- -D warnings`: clean. `--all-targets` stops at `wire_tool` (#2244). - No snapshot PNG changed. Review fix on 43b789ed (label read from the entity): - `generate_progress` (8): green. - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` at `--test-threads=16`: 1025 passed, 0 failed. - `generate_staged` (2): green. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - `model.rs` gets 7 lines (`live_operation_label`). The file was 482 lines before this change. The helper is next to `operation_label`, because the UI crate does no raw world call. ## Not exercised - No hand test in the real window on a long job. The structural tests drive the same `viewport_panel` code through the harness. - `RegenerateAll` (the batch fix of the stale operations) stays synchronous. Its rounds write the world between rounds, so it does not split at one seam. It shows no overlay. The overlay's "n of m" counts single generations that wait in the queue. - The browser build was not run. Its generation stays synchronous through the spawn fallback. Changelog: While a toolpath generates, a progress overlay over the viewport names the operation, counts the queued ones and offers Cancel; the window stays responsive (#2257) Effort: medium (the label of the issue). Not escalated. Fixes #2257 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(tools): a refused tool names itself and the rule it breaks
body:
#1186: the project loader refused a tool with bad numbers. The message was `tool parameters are not usable: ToolDto { ... }`, with the full structure. The refusal was correct, but it did not name the tool or the field. `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` printed a similar dump. The library import and the library reader gave a general message.

The branch has upstream main at a529c455, merged in.

## What changed

- **`Tool::why_not_sane() -> Option<String>`** (new file `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs`). It gives the first rule that a tool breaks, in plain words. Examples:
  - `turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min (it must be over 0)`
  - `corner radius 100 mm is more than half the 6 mm diameter`
  - `a drill's tip angle 50 degrees must be over 60`
  - `a sinker electrode turns no spindle: its spindle speed must be 0, not 1000 rpm`
  - `TurningData::why_not_sane` gives the same for the turning limits.
- **One source of truth.** `Tool::is_sane` and `TurningData::is_sane` are now `why_not_sane().is_none()`. Thus the message and the verdict cannot be different. The rules moved out of `tools.rs` in the same order, with the same limits.
- **The rules that main added are included.** Main added these after the branch started:
  - the `pitch_min` field;
  - the waterjet, electrode and thread-mill kinds and their rules;
  - the catalog and cutting-row refusals.
  - Each of these rules has its own message now.
- **Four refusals now read `tool '<name>': <rule>`:**
  - the project loader (`project/validate.rs`), which is the case in the issue;
  - `AddTool` and `ChangeTool` (`commands/tool.rs`);
  - the tool-library import (`commands/tool_import.rs`);
  - the library reader (`tool_library.rs`).
  - The MCP tools `add_tool` and `edit_tool` use the same commands. Thus an agent also gets the named rule.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1186-tool-refusal-names.md`.

## Tests

New pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/project_tool_refusal.rs` opens a saved file with one bad field through the real loader (`project::open`).
  - `a_bad_turning_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: surface speed 0, a negative feed per rev, and a max rpm below the rpm of the tool.
  - `a_bad_milling_field_is_refused_by_tool_and_field`: a corner radius more than half the diameter, and feed 0.
  - The two tests also make sure that the message has no `ToolDto` dump.
- `tools::tool_sanity::tests`:
  - `a_turning_field_is_named`, `a_milling_field_is_named` and `the_newer_kinds_are_named`.
  - `the_named_law_gives_the_old_verdict_everywhere` keeps the `is_sane` body of main as an oracle. It also keeps the `TurningData::is_sane` body.
  - The test examines each catalog tool as each of the 18 kinds (Wire added at the merge of 2026-11-18). It sets each of the 14 numeric fields to 13 edge values: 0, negative, the 60 and 180 degree limits, more than 500, NaN and infinity. It also examines flute counts, orientation codes and turning data.
  - The new law gives the same verdict in all cases. Thus no tool changes from accepted to refused, or from refused to accepted.
  - `a_bad_wire_is_named` (added at the merge of 2026-11-18): an EDM wire with a spindle speed, a diameter out of range or a corner radius is refused, and the message names the wire and the rule.
  - `a_valid_wire_is_accepted` (added at the merge of 2026-11-18): a wire with rpm 0 and a diameter of 0.02, 0.25 or 1 mm is accepted.

Changed test: `tool_cutter_params::a_reshape_is_refused_by_name_against_the_new_numbers` looked for the old text "finite and positive". It now looks for `tool '<name>': diameter -1 mm is outside`.

Gates on dbf7799e:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green.
  - The tools step ran the lib tests and `waterjet`.
  - The app step ran the lib tests and 44 suites. These include all `tool_*` suites, `project_tool_refusal`, `project_roundtrip`, `thread_mill`, `waterjet_machine`, `plasma_profile`, `mcp` and `commands_undo`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

## Not exercised

- The UI shows these refusals in the status line, as before. No UI test reads their text. A search of `crates/ui` finds none of the old messages.
- A missing or unknown field is a serde parse error. It occurs before this law runs. The serde message already names the field, and it does not change.

Changelog: A tool refused for unusable numbers (project load, add or edit tool, library import) now names the tool and the rule it breaks, e.g. "tool 'T1': turning surface speed 0 m/min is outside 0..2000 m/min", instead of printing the whole definition (#1186)

Effort: low (the label of the issue). Not escalated.

Fixes #1186

title: feat(ui): WCS page applies its origin from the footer beside Close, and says where the origin is
body: #870: a Makera Z1 user cut air on their first program because they hadn't understood where the origin was. Then it "took a while to find out how to actually save the setting, as the 'set origin' button is crammed next to a lot of other options". Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a. ## What changed - **Set origin in the footer.** The WCS page's apply button leaves the page body (where it shared a row with *Level*, among the quarter turns) and moves into the property pane's fixed footer, beside *Close* (`egui_app::wcs_footer`). Every other page keeps its plain *Close*. - **Pending edits are flagged.** While the typed X/Y/Z or angles differ from the placed WCS, the footer shows **Origin not applied** in the warning ink. - The position is compared to 1e-9 mm. The angles are compared as rotations, so yaw 360 is not an edit. A non-finite field reads as pending. - The drafts survive a close and reopen, so closing loses nothing silently. Closing does not apply them either. - **The origin in words.** A new pure module, `app::setup_origin`, places the origin against the box the page anchors on (the stock box, else the model's bounds). - A point on one of the 27 anchor points is named, e.g. `top of stock, front-left corner`, `top of stock, centre` or `mid-height of stock, front edge, centred`. - Any other point is given as signed distances from the box's left side, front and top, so it never claims a corner it is not on. - The WCS page states it under its heading: `G54 origin: top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)`. The setup sheet gains an `origin:` line under the WCS numbers. - **Viewport marker:** the WCS axis triad already marks the origin; nothing was added. - **Docs:** `docs/user-guide/work-origin.md`, a short page on where the origin is shown and how to change it. - Decision record: `docs/decisions/870-wcs-set-origin-footer.md`. **Refresh onto main (2026-11-18, maintainer option (a)).** Main now has the WCS page body in `wcs_page.rs` (#759 landed). The merge takes main's page and redoes this PR's change on it: - `wcs_page.rs` `quarter_turns`: the body's *Set Origin* button is removed. *Level* has its row alone. - `pages.rs`: the page calls `wcs_footer::origin_line` under the heading, and the WCS footer is `wcs_footer::footer`. All other pages keep *Close*. - `wcs_footer.rs` calls `wcs_page::apply_wcs_drafts`, which sends the undoable `SetWcs` command. - Main's tests are updated: `wcs_page_tests::quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`, `wcs_page_tests::milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment`, `page_layout::layout_page_wcs` (now in a 900 px window, with *Set origin* as its last anchor). ## How it was tested New pinning tests: - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/wcs_footer.rs` (structural: painted text, AccessKit labels, coarse placement): - `the_page_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` - `set_origin_sits_in_the_footer_beside_close_and_nowhere_else`: one row, Set origin before Close, below the page body, exactly one apply button, no flag on a fresh page. - `a_typed_origin_is_flagged_until_set_origin_applies_it`: the flag appears, a click on Set origin places the typed X and clears it, and yaw 360 does not raise it. - `app::setup_origin` unit tests: `every_anchor_point_is_named`, `a_point_off_the_anchors_is_given_as_distances_never_as_a_corner`, `a_non_finite_origin_or_box_says_so`. - `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs`: `the_setup_sheet_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` (corner, centre, off-anchor). Two existing ui tests got a taller window, 1280 x 900 instead of 720. The new origin line makes the WCS page one to two rows taller, and at 720 px the bottom of the page scrolls under the footer. The page scrolls; nothing is lost. - `one_wcs::the_wcs_page_shows_the_work_offset_dropdown_and_no_setups_page_pointer`: its bottom note was out of view. - `origin_page_shows_the_anchor_grid_and_arms_pick_mode`: its SE cell click missed. Main's tests changed by the refresh: - `egui_app::wcs_page_tests::quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`: Level is live and spans the pane; no Set Origin button is in the body. - `egui_app::wcs_page_tests::milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment`: the live list is Turn Z+, Turn Z-, Level. - `egui_app::tests::page_layout::layout_page_wcs`: 1280 x 900 window, anchors end with Set origin. Gate on de0891e00: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 20 steps, 0 failed (`ui suites: lib` included). The ui `#[test]` count is 1266 (main: 1263). No snapshot PNG touched. Clippy on app and ui is clean, apart from one `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` lint in main's `crates/app/src/operation/heights.rs:128`, which this PR does not touch. ## Not exercised - Not looked at in the running app. The layout is pinned structurally only. - On a rotated or aligned setup (#326), "left" and "front" are the world box's, as the anchor grid's compass names already are. - The release-lane pixel snapshots were not run. If one frames the WCS page, it moves at the cut's regeneration. Changelog: WCS page: Set origin sits in the footer beside Close, unapplied edits are flagged, and the page and setup sheet say where the origin is in words ("top of stock, front-left corner") (#870) Effort: medium (the issue's label). Not escalated. ## Screenshots Headless harness render at 1280 x 900, after the refresh onto main. The stock is a 100 x 50 x 20 box, and the origin is at its top front-left corner. Before (main): ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1209/before.png) Before, with a typed X that is not applied: nothing on the page says so. ![before, typed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1209/before-typed.png) After: ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1209/after.png) After, with a typed X that is not applied: the footer says "Origin not applied" beside Set origin and Close. ![after, typed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-1209/after-typed.png) ## What it looked like before the refresh **Before:** the typed origin was applied by a *Set Origin* button tucked into the row of quarter-turn buttons, beside *Level*. It was easy to type new X/Y/Z values, press *Close*, and leave the origin where it was, with nothing on the page saying so. **After:** *Set origin* sits in the footer beside *Close*. A line under the heading says where the origin is in plain words (for example "top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)"). While a typed value is not applied yet, the footer says **Origin not applied**. Fixes #870 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(post): doosan-dnm states a touch probe's spindle stopped before its first move
body:
#1035: #574 made every built-in mill post state its spindle stopped (M5; MOTOFF on Mazak) after a touch probe's tool change and length offset, before its first move. A control whose tool change leaves the spindle turning (a same-tool continuation, a manual change) then still brings the probe to the part stopped. `doosan-dnm.cps` (#614) came after #574. Its `startPreamble` skipped S/M3 for a section with a stated speed of 0 but wrote no M5, and `probe_spindle_stop.rs`'s `MILL_POSTS` left it out.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 17; merged with upstream main at a0891091.

## What changed

- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: after the tool change, the G43 and the skipped spindle start, a section with a stated speed of 0 writes `M5`, before the first move. A cutting section is unchanged.
- `crates/app/tests/probe_spindle_stop.rs`: `("doosan-dnm", "M5")` joins `MILL_POSTS`, so both of its tests cover the post:
  - `a_probe_section_stops_its_spindle_after_the_tool_change_on_every_mill_post`
  - `a_cutting_section_states_no_spindle_stop_before_its_first_move`
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1035-doosan-probe-m5.md`.

**Overlap with #1034** (#995, @mkinney, open draft): it edits the same `startPreamble`. It adds a `touchProbe` variable at the function's top line and gates the coolant line.
- This PR writes its condition inline after the spindle block instead (`spindleWait && !(sRpm > 0)`). A zero-speed section never clears `spindleWait`, so the condition still holds at that point.
- Neither PR touches the other's lines. A trial merge of this branch with #1034's head 5d8b71e2 is clean.
- I did not stack on #1034: it carries a breaking `feat(post)!` (Air coolant, #869) and merges at the next cut, which would hold this P2 fix until then.

## How it was tested

- Pinning test: `probe_spindle_stop::a_probe_section_stops_its_spindle_after_the_tool_change_on_every_mill_post`. It fails on main with "doosan-dnm: no M5 between the tool change and the first move" and passes with the fix. Its cutting-section twin stays green for doosan-dnm.
- Every app suite that posts through `doosan-dnm` or probes, run by hand, all green: `conformance`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `post_unit_word`, `golden_cl`, and the 12 `probe_*` suites.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 66 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, but for a `.cps`-only change it plans almost nothing (#923). That is why the suites above were run by hand.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG touched. No posted golden changes (none probes on doosan-dnm).

## Not exercised

- Not run on a Doosan control.
- The fix is pinned with the generic `3axis-vmc.mch`, as the other posts in `probe_spindle_stop` are, not with a Doosan machine file.

Changelog: Doosan DNM post: a touch probe section states its spindle stopped (M5) before its first move, like the other mill posts (#1035)

Effort: high (the issue's label: posted G-code is under the safety floor). Not escalated.

Fixes #1035

title: feat(ui): keep the theme and colour-vision mode as user preferences
body:
#877: the theme and the colour-vision mode were document state. The theme was saved in the project file and set again on open, File > New reset it to Dark, and both were undoable edits that marked the project changed. The colour-vision mode was not saved at all, so it reset on every restart. The reporter decided on the issue that both are purely user preferences and survive restarts.

Fork synced at v0.17.0, PROCESS_VERSION 14; merged with upstream main at 19ac4630.

## What changed

- **New `app::prefs`** (`crates/app/src/prefs.rs`): a per-user `prefs.json` in our own `camcraft-prefs/1` format, in the recent-files config folder (#662: `%APPDATA%\camcraft`, `~/Library/Application Support/camcraft`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/camcraft`, or `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`). It reuses `recent::config_dir_for` and the atomic `write_atomic`. On load:
  - A missing file is a quiet default start.
  - A corrupt or foreign file starts at the defaults with the reason.
  - An unknown theme name or colour-vision word falls back for that preference alone and is named.
  - A theme file path is kept as written even if the file is gone; `sync_theme` refuses it by name as before.
- **New `ui::state_prefs`** (`crates/ui/src/state_prefs.rs`): `load_prefs()` at startup (the real window only, in `shell_window.rs` beside `load_recent()`), and `select_theme` / `select_color_vision` moved here from `state.rs`.
  - A pick validates as before (the JSON pre-parse plus `check_theme`, or the colour-vision gate), sets the singleton and writes the file.
  - A stored colour-vision mode is gated against the theme it lands on.
  - Headless States have no store, so the tests never touch the user's file.
- **Not undoable any more:** `SetTheme` / `SetColorVision` are no longer `Command`s. `commands::check_theme` keeps the existence law. A pick is not on the history and not an unsaved change. It no longer bumps `doc_version` either: the overlays read the singleton every frame.
- **Project file:** the `theme` key is no longer written, and opening ignores it. `ProjectFile` doesn't deny unknown keys, so older files that carry `"theme": {...}` open cleanly. No version bump. File > New no longer resets the theme.
- Doc comments that described the theme as document state or undoable are updated (`schema.rs`, `panes.rs`, `theme_drop.rs`, `ribbon_pins.rs`, `state.rs`).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/877-theme-user-pref.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs`:
  - `the_preferences_survive_a_restart`
  - `no_file_is_a_quiet_default_start`
  - `a_corrupt_or_foreign_file_starts_at_the_defaults_and_says_why`
  - `an_unknown_value_falls_back_alone_and_is_named`
  - `a_pick_is_checked_by_name`
  - `the_project_file_never_carries_the_colour_vision_mode`
- `project_roundtrip::the_project_file_never_carries_the_theme_and_an_old_theme_key_is_ignored`: a save writes no `theme` key, and four older shapes (dark, a stranger name, a gone file, v40) open without changing the user's theme.
- `egui_app::tests::prefs_door`:
  - `a_pick_survives_new_open_and_a_restart`: pick Light and Deutan, the file is written, the document is not dirty; File > New and opening an older project that names `dark` keep both; a new State reading the same file restores both.
  - `a_corrupt_preferences_file_starts_dark_and_says_why`
  - `a_headless_state_keeps_its_picks_in_memory`

Removed, because they pinned the old design (as the issue lists):
- `commands_undo::theme_choice_undoes_redoes_and_refuses`
- `commands_undo::color_vision_is_an_undoable_view_preference`

Their refusal and project-file checks moved into `view_prefs.rs`. `project_roundtrip::the_theme_choice_round_trips_and_a_v40_file_means_dark` is replaced by the test above.

Updated to assert that undo leaves the pick (or to switch back with a pick):
- `colorvision_tests::switching_is_a_preference_outside_undo`
- `theme_door::the_theme_door_switches_the_theme_and_undo_leaves_it`
- `theme_door::the_theme_door_carries_the_colour_vision_modes`
- `law_tests::path_tests::the_path_wears_the_colour_vision_palette_and_off_restores_it`

Gates:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the merged tree:
  - app suites green, `view_prefs`, `commands_undo` and `project_roundtrip` among them;
  - ui suites: every suite green except one ui lib test, `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam`. It flags `refusal_ghost.rs:44`, which this PR doesn't touch: upstream main is red there (#907, fixed by #908). Before this PR's own `diag_warn!` fix (c4e96ead) it flagged `state_prefs.rs` too; that is fixed.
- The first ui run hit a full disk (linker LNK1318/LNK1106). The ui suites were rerun after freeing space.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

Visual check: the reporter ran the built app on Windows and confirmed it. Picking Light and a colour-vision mode wrote `%APPDATA%\camcraft\prefs.json` without marking the project unsaved. File > New, opening a project and Ctrl+Z left the pick as it was, and a restart came back in the same theme and mode.

## Not exercised

- macOS and Linux were not run. The folder resolver is #662's, pinned there per OS.
- The wasm build was not run. `load_prefs` is called only from the native `shell_window.rs`, so the browser keeps both preferences for the session, as it does recent files.

Changelog: The theme and colour-vision mode are now your own preferences: they survive restarts, and New, Open and project files no longer change them (#877)

Effort: medium (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #877

title: fix(ui): light theme gets a light viewport and inks that read on it
body:
#698: the light theme's viewport stayed dark, because the 3D pass cleared to a fixed colour. It now follows the theme, and everything drawn over the viewport reads on a light ground. The light values were tuned on screen with the reporter in a running build. The dark theme looks as before; every dark ink is asserted equal to its old value.

Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed

- **Viewport ground:** a theme token, `Tokens::viewport`. Light is `#DDE1E7`; dark keeps the old clear colour. Theme files can set it with a new `viewport` key. The 3D pass clears to the live theme's ground.
- **Light-ground inks**, new module `ground_ink.rs`:
  - Toolpath moves: deep feed green, plus the rapid blue and plunge red the reporter picked. All three clear 3:1 on the ground.
  - Saturated boundary roles.
  - Wireframe edge (a new shader uniform), world axes, and the region, retract, cut, pick and hover overlays.
  - The corner control hint and the playback tool marker, which were white.
- **Colour-vision modes** (added after review): protan/deutan and tritan get light-ground sets too (`RED_GREEN_LIGHT_GROUND`, `TRITAN_LIGHT_GROUND`), changing only the line inks. On the light ground their dark-tuned lines read 1.01-2.8:1 (a pale yellow feed and a white "open" boundary). Each light set keeps its eye's surviving axis (blue-yellow, or red-cyan) and moves the pale end to near-black, so lightness still carries the pairs. Every must-distinguish pair passes the CIEDE2000 floor (weakest: protan 25.7, deutan 27.7, tritan 24.4), and every line ink clears 3:1 (3.5-14.6:1).
- **Dimmed paths:** unselected paths under "Show all toolpaths" fade toward a light ground instead of being scaled toward black. At 0.45 that turned every hue into near-black, and the lines couldn't be told apart.
- **View cube:** in light theme, the faces are mid grey, a step under the ground, with darker edges and dark labels. The four buttons under it match.
  - The Axes button's triad is now centred and symmetric (equal arms, 120° apart), in saturated X/Y/Z colours, in both themes. Before, it was off-centre and pastel.
- **Hover (light only):** `field_hover` and egui's hover fill are the viewport grey, with dark ink. This covers the toolbar, menus, the tree and buttons. Dark keeps its steel-blue hover.
- **Window title bars (light only):** egui's `open.weak_bg_fill` is the window fill and `open.fg_stroke` the text. They were egui's dark defaults, so light windows had black title bars with invisible icons. Dark keeps egui's own values (pinned).
- **Debug info window:** draws its own title row (new `window_chrome.rs`). Its collapse arrow hovers grey, and close hovers red with a white X, like the OS caption buttons. egui's built-in title bar paints these glyphs with no hover fill. **Why it is in this PR:** the reporter hit it during the light-theme check. On the light ground the window's arrow and close glyphs were invisible, then vanished on hover. It is a light-theme readability fix of the same kind as the rest.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/698-light-viewport.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `egui_app::viewport_ground_tests`:
  - `the_light_viewport_is_light_and_the_dark_one_stays_dark`
  - `every_overlay_ink_clears_3_to_1_on_the_light_viewport`
  - `the_light_palette_move_inks_clear_3_to_1`
  - `the_light_palette_is_the_hand_tuned_set`
  - `a_dimmed_path_fades_toward_a_light_ground_and_darkens_on_a_dark_one`
  - `the_light_wireframe_and_axis_inks_clear_3_to_1`
  - `the_light_cube_sits_a_step_under_the_viewport_with_darker_edges`
  - `the_dark_cube_keeps_its_greys`
  - `light_hover_is_the_viewport_grey_with_dark_ink_and_dark_keeps_its_accent`
  - `the_dark_ground_keeps_the_house_inks`
  - `every_mode_wears_its_light_set_on_a_light_ground`
  - `the_light_colour_vision_sets_pass_the_cvd_gate_and_clear_3_to_1`
  - `the_dark_title_bar_keeps_eguis_own_open_fill`
- `egui_app::debug_info_tests::the_title_row_folds_the_window_and_its_close_button_closes_it`: folds, unfolds and closes through the AccessKit labels.

Gates:
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick`) on 6177922d: green. ui lib 468 passed, plus the boundary, boundary_picks, edge_loop_pick, gpu_render, operations and theme_files suites; 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

Visual check: the reporter tuned the light colours over several rounds in a running Windows build, and approved them.

## Not exercised

- The light pixel snapshot golden (`egui_app_light`) will differ on the viewport, hover and title bars. Per the pixel-snapshot law it is regenerated at the cut, not here.
- The light colour-vision sets were checked by the simulation gate (Machado 2009 with CIEDE2000, the same as the dark sets), not by a colour-vision-deficient viewer.
- The light-set literals live in `ground_ink.rs`, not in theme tokens, so a theme file cannot change them yet (review note 4: a follow-up).
- Part shading and the selected-part amber on the light ground were not re-tuned.
- Boundary role inks on the light ground are under 3:1 (hue chosen over contrast). They are pinned as chosen, and listed as open in the decision note.
- The other four floating windows keep egui's title bar. It is now themed, but has no caption hover fill.
- macOS and Linux were not run.

`theme.rs` is at 402 lines.

Changelog: The light theme now has a light viewport, with toolpath, overlay, view cube, hover and window title bar colours that read on it (#698)

Effort: low (the issue's label). The work grew past it: 4 more files than planned and a new window title row. Not escalated, because the work was steered visually with the reporter in the main session.

Fixes #698

title: fix(app): machine check reads a 4th-axis table's pose through the tool axis
body:
Was stacked on #798 (Tormach microARC 4, #785). #798 has merged, and upstream main (with the #844 build fix) is merged into this branch at `eb5bd15d`, so the diff is this PR's own 7 files.

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (process files PROCESS_VERSION 12).

## What changed

The machine check judged a tilted move's canonical letters one by one. On the 770MX + microARC 4, whose only rotary is an A about X, it refused the face underneath (A0 B180) with "states no B axis". That table reaches the pose as A180, and the PathPilot post already posts it as `G0 A180`.

- `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs`: the pose gate moves here from `mod.rs` as `pose_problems`.
  - On a machine with exactly one rotary, stated along X (the post's own test, x² ≥ 0.998·|d|²), the gate reads the tool angle about X from the letters. It uses the post's formula and tolerances (`tormach.cps` `toolAngle`), so the check and the post agree on every pose.
  - The angle is signed by the stated direction (a `[-1,0,0]` table commands the negated angle, as the post writes the word) and judged against the rotary's travel.
  - A pose with an X component, meaning any B or C a turn about X cannot make, is refused by name: `move i commands A .. B .. C .. deg; <model>'s only rotary, A about X, cannot reach that pose`.
  - Every other machine keeps the letter law unchanged: none, two or more rotaries, or a single rotary that is unstated or not along X.
- `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`: calls `pose_problems` instead of the inline letter loop. The file shrinks from 396 to 355 lines.
- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: this post writes the stream's letters as they come (G43.4), so it now refuses a turning letter with no rotary of that name: `tilted move commands B - the machine states no B rotary`. Before this PR, the check stopped A0 B180 reaching that dialect on an A-only table. Now the post does, so the safety floor is unchanged.
  - From the review: it also refuses a tilt on a lone rotary stated along -X (`tilted move on rotary A, stated along -X - ...`). The check judges that table by the negated angle; this dialect writes the letter unnegated, so A-45 on a `[-1,0,0]` 0..90 table would pass the check and post outside the travel. No shipped machine states a -X rotary, so no shipped output changes. Only a non-zero A is refused: A0 is the same word on either sign, so an upright section that states A0 still posts.
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` (delta review): the shipped DNM's A about X leans off Z, so the mirror sets `machine.rtcp` and Doosan's RTCP path writes the stream's letters raw. It now refuses, by name, the same two cases as Fanuc: a turning letter with no rotary of that name (so the A0 B180 the check now passes never posts a `B180` word to a machine with no B) and a non-zero A on a lone rotary stated along -X.
- `judge.rs` doc: no longer claims every post agrees with the check. The PathPilot post does; the two G43.4 dialects (Fanuc, Doosan) write letters unnegated and refuse the B of A0 B180 and a turning A on the -X table by name.
- `crates/app/tests/microarc_test_part.rs` (from #798): the wrap test now expects the post's refusal (`simultaneous 4-axis motion in operation WRAP`). It also asserts that the machine check no longer flags the wrap, whose every pose is reachable as an angle about X. The header comment is updated.
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/README.md`: one sentence updated to match.
- `docs/decisions/797-a-only-pose.md`: the decision record.

## How tested

The new suite, `crates/app/tests/fourth_axis_pose.rs`, holds the pinning tests:

- `an_a0_b180_slot_posts_as_a180_on_the_microarc4`: a real Slot with tilt A0 B180 on the bar job, built through the app's commands.
  - The check is clean.
  - `post_setup` writes exactly one index, `G0 A180`, and no B word.
  - The cuts land on the skin (Z 0.375 → 0.36) inside the stick-out.
- `the_face_underneath_is_judged_as_a180_against_the_travel`:
  - With A travel -90..90, every move is refused as `commands A 180.000 deg (the pose A 0.000 B 180.000), the travel is -90.000..90.000`.
  - A `[-1,0,0]` table commands -180: it passes on -180..0 and is refused on 0..180.
- `a_pose_the_a_axis_cannot_reach_is_still_refused_by_name`: a B30 lean on the same machine is refused by name by the check, and `post_setup` refuses and writes no file.
- `a_second_rotary_keeps_the_letter_law`: A about X plus C about Z still refuses B180 with `states no B axis`.
- `the_fanuc_dialect_refuses_a_b_on_an_a_only_table`: fanuc.cps on the microARC mirror refuses A0 B180 by name and writes no `B180`. A90 posts.
- `the_fanuc_dialect_refuses_a_lone_a_stated_along_minus_x`: on the microARC mirror stated `[-1,0,0]`, travel 0..90, fanuc.cps refuses A-45 by name and writes no `A-45`; stated `[1,0,0]` it posts A-45 as before.
- `an_upright_a0_still_posts_on_a_minus_x_fanuc_table`: A0 on the -X table posts with no warning.
- `the_doosan_dialect_refuses_a_b_on_its_a_only_table`: the shipped DNM passes the check on A0 B180; doosan-dnm.cps refuses the B by name and writes no `B180`. A90 posts.
- `the_doosan_dialect_refuses_a_turning_a_stated_along_minus_x`: on the DNM stated `[-1,0,0]`, travel 0..90, A-45 is refused by name and no `A-45` is written; an upright A0 posts. Both Doosan tests fail against the previous `doosan-dnm.cps` (checked by running them on it). They live in `fourth_axis_pose.rs` beside the Fanuc ones, because `doosan_dnm_post.rs` would pass 400 lines.

Gate, on the merged tree `eb5bd15d` (main incl. #798 and the #844 fix):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: app suites (the lib plus the gate-mapped `app::machine` suites, `fourth_axis_pose` among them) and ui suites, 477 passed, 0 failed.
- Delta-review fix (693b2809), merged with upstream main at 7a7dba04 (only `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` conflicted; took main's 14): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green, 482 passed, 0 failed. Run alone: `fourth_axis_pose` 9/9, `doosan_dnm_post` 7/7, `fanuc_post` 11/11, `machine` 33/33, `tormach_fourth_axis` 12/12, `microarc_test_part` 2/2, `conformance` 6/6, `index_swing` 9/9; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- First review fix (d1c73221), run alone: `fourth_axis_pose` 6/6, `fanuc_post` 11/11, `machine` 33/33, `tormach_fourth_axis` 12/12, `microarc_test_part` 2/2, `conformance` 6/6, `index_swing` 9/9; clippy clean.
- Before the review fix, run alone: `fourth_axis_pose` 5/5, `microarc_test_part` 2/2 (the kit golden now checks out LF, from #798's `.gitattributes` fix), `fanuc_post` 11/11, `tormach_fourth_axis` 12/12, `machine` 33/33.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No real PathPilot or Fanuc control was run.
- A refused tilt blocks the post in the app (`posting.rs`, `posting_per_op.rs`, `posting_mounts.rs` return "post blocked" on any counted warning), so no NC file is written. The dev CLI `crates/post/src/bin/post.rs` still writes the file and prints the warnings; left to the maintainer.
- Doosan's indexing (non-RTCP) path was not changed: a -X rotary always leans off Z, so it always takes the RTCP path.
- The release-lane `--ignored` heavy tests were not run.
- The ui snapshot lane was not run.

Changelog: The machine check reads a 4th-axis A-about-X table's pose through the tool axis, so the face underneath (A0 B180) posts as A180 on the 770MX + microARC 4; an unreachable pose is still refused by name, and the Fanuc post refuses a letter the machine has no rotary for.

Effort: high

Fixes #797

title: refactor(tools): ship the starter tool catalog as assets/tools/catalog.json
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 9); upstream main merged into the branch.

## What changed
The 28-tool starter catalog moves from a Rust table in `tools.rs` to `assets/tools/catalog.json`, a `camcraft-tools/1` library (the #300 envelope), embedded with `include_str!` like the posts. `catalog()` keeps its signature, names, order and values, so no call site or test changes. `camcraft-tools` reads it with a small strict reader (`catalog_asset.rs`: format/version/units/name/duplicate/unknown-key/`is_sane` checks, errors name the tool); a failing embedded asset is logged and yields an empty catalog, never a panic. Decision (layering, embed vs runtime read, rejected options): `docs/decisions/741-tool-catalog-json.md`. Type is `refactor`: user-visible behaviour is unchanged.

## How tested
- Before deleting the Rust table, a test compared the JSON catalog with it tool for tool (Debug-equal, all 28): identical. The permanent pins are below.
- `camcraft-tools` (all, 38 pass): `the_shipped_asset_parses_and_every_tool_is_valid`, `the_json_catalog_keeps_the_old_tables_values` (order + per-kind values), `a_bad_catalog_is_a_named_error_not_a_panic`.
- `camcraft-app` `--test tool_library` (6 pass) incl. new `the_shipped_catalog_asset_reads_the_same_through_the_library_reader` (app `parse_tool_library` agrees with `catalog()`); also `tool_gate`, `cutting_data`, `tool_list`, `mcp`, `scripting`, `drill_reach` pass; ui lib subset (tool_number, ball_corner, footer, fresh_op) passes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
Full `cargo xtask gate quick` / batch (the diff touches `Cargo.lock`, which falls back to batch) and the other ui suites; catalog values are unchanged and pinned, so I ran the catalog-touching ones. No snapshots or goldens changed. The optional user-override catalog folder is not done.

## New dependency
`serde` and `serde_json` added to `camcraft-tools` (both workspace deps already in `Cargo.lock`; no new crate). `Cargo.lock` gains 4 lines.

Changelog: The starter tool catalog is now the data file assets/tools/catalog.json instead of a Rust table (#741, PR #TBD)
Effort: medium

Fixes #741
